en: Get your paws off that Hatch, you Skulk. Come on out and face me!

speaker: Edward
en: Peace, man. My name's Edward Kenway, a friend of Bonnet's. I'm looking for his Crew, not a Fight.

speaker: Sharp
en: Edward Kenway? As I live and breathe... come, join me by the Fire.

speaker: Sharp
en: "Flash Rogue with a Hangman's Grin." Major Bonnet told me to look out for you, Captain Kenway. Name's Rowland Sharp. I'm in charge of this here Crew. It's an honour to meet you, a real honour.

speaker: Edward
en: The Pleasure's mine. Where's Major Bonnet now? What happened to his Ship?

speaker: Sharp
en: After the Major sent us on ahead of him, there was a Mutiny. The Traitors filched the Key to the Major's Cabin belowdecks. We've been holding them off since, but they took the Provisions for themselves.

speaker: Edward
en: When does Bonnet get here?

speaker: Pirate 1
en: Mister Sharp! Trouble! The Mutineers are further down the Shore, gathering for an attack. All of them.

speaker: Sharp
en: You'll have answers, Captain Kenway. But we need your help. This is our chance to get the Major's Key back.

speaker: Edward
en: Lead on, Mister Sharp.

speaker: Pirate 2
en: Weeks of this miserable stalemate. Now we break it.

speaker: Pirate 3
en: With Captain Edward Kenway's help, no less!

speaker: Sharp
en: These Mutineers are a savvy bunch. Have you your Wits about you?

speaker: Edward
en: Wits, Steel, and Powder besides.

speaker: Sharp
en: Gird your Loins, lads. For the Major!

speaker: Ignatius Pell‏‎
en: Oi oi, look what washed up. Bonnet's Cabin Boys. I'm shitting my Drawers in Fear.

speaker: Sharp
en: Pell, you Swab! He's a damned fine Captain. Too good for the likes of you.

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: He's soft as his three Chins. You'd follow such a weakling?

speaker: Sharp
en: Have you forgotten when he ate naught but Hardtack for weeks, so that we could have Meat? I'd follow this kind of Captain over you lot, that's certain.

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: Then you can follow him straight to the Gallows, and Blubber and Grovel all the way!

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: That Dandy lorded over us like he was our better. He broke the Pirate Code!

speaker: Sharp
en: What would you know of any Code? You can't even read!

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: What, and you can?

speaker: Sharp
en: I'm not the one talking about it, am I?

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: Gut them, lads!

speaker: Sharp
en: Bonnet's Brigade fights on! Get stuck in, lads, fight like the Major himself was here!

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: All this Bluster, Sharp, and for what? You still thinking the Oaf is going to share his Treasure with you?

speaker: Sharp
en: It's only ever about Reward, isn't it? What would you know of Loyalty?

speaker: Pell‏‎
en: Come show me then!

speaker: Sharp
en: The Mutineers are dead! We have the Key!

speaker: Edward
en: Keep your Eyes open. I have a sense it's not over yet.

speaker: Pirate 4
en: Yonder on the Horizon! There's a Brig and she's heading this way!

speaker: Edward
en: That Ship's carrying the Union Jack. Ready yourselves, the Navy's here.

speaker: British Officer 1
en: By Order of the King, the Property of the Pirate Stede Bonnet is to be seized by the Crown, and his Crew apprehended!

speaker: Edward
en: What in Blazes is going on?

speaker: Pirate 5
en: Were we the ones who called for the Navy?

speaker: Sharp
en: Not on your Life. It must have been Pell and his Boys.

speaker: Pirate 5
en: The Gall of them. Rats!

speaker: Sharp
en: Traitors!

speaker: Pirate 5
en: Cowards!

speaker: Sharp
en: Lily-livered!

speaker: British Officer 2
en: Will you shut your Gobs and listen to me. You're all under Arrest!

speaker: Pirate 6
en: Hold on, this here Island's got no Governor, does it? Then why's the Navy here?

speaker: Pirate 7
en: Actually, the Acts of Trade and Navigation empower them to stake what they like from Ships not manned by "loyal" subjects.

speaker: Pirate 6
en: Oi, who made you a Barrister, then?

speaker: Pirate 7
en: Well, I did secure a Pupilage at Gray's Inn, before shipping off.

speaker: Pirate 6
en: How the Hell did you end up with us?

speaker: Pirate 7
en: Ain't it all the same? We take what we want, at someone else's expense.

speaker: British Officer 3
en: Excuse me! I'm still here! And you're all under Arrest!

speaker: Edward
en: It's done. That's the last of them.

speaker: Sharp
en: And we've got the Major's Key again. Come with us to the Cabin, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm still owed some answers, Sharp. Where's Bonnet?

speaker: Sharp
en: I wish I knew. There was Trouble in Charles-Towne. The Governor put a Bounty on the Major's head, and his men chased us out to Sea. The Major sent us on ahead. Then he turned back upriver to draw them off our tail.

speaker: Edward
en: That must be how he was captured. He held them off alone?

speaker: Pirate 8
en: "See how Edward taught me to fight!" he said. And have we seen it!

speaker: Sharp
en: You're exactly as he said you'd be, Captain Kenway.

speaker: Pirate 9
en: I snuck a last Letter from Major Bonnet out of Charles-Towne, and sailed alone to get it here. He was in an ill Mood when he passed it to a paid off guard in the Prison. We stowed the Letter in the Cabin.

speaker: Sharp
en: Here. Bonnet's Letter was meant for you.

speaker: Edward
en: Thank you, Mister Sharp. I'll have a look around.

speaker: Edward
en: What's this... Sugar? He recovered it.

speaker: Edward
en: Looking properly Dashing.

speaker: Edward
en: Looks like he took the King's Pardon, then reneged. Sly dog.

speaker: Edward
en: Bonnet's Diary. What Adventures am I to discover, Captain Bonnet?

speaker: Edward
en: Rich. Definitely Bonnet's Quarters.

speaker: Bonnet
en: Edward, I... I am to be hanged on the Morrow. I imagined facing Death like you, swords drawn, full of Gusto. Instead, I found myself begging and weeping at the Governor's feet. I fear your Advice was wasted on a Constitution like mine. Perhaps I should've left off Pirating altogether, and sailed home to my Wife and Children. But I'm not quite the same man who left them, am I? That was the Gift you gave me, the Courage to live free. I'll muster that Courage when the morning comes. The Stories I promised will have to wait, Edward. But if, on your Adventures, you should hear any Tales of my sundry Exploits and Capers... then perhaps in the End I lived as I was meant to.

speaker: Sailor
en: We kept the Watchfires burning, for the Day he'd sail again. But the Gallows claimed our Captain, though the People sang his Name.

speaker: Sharp
en: The Major... he's not coming, is he?

speaker: Edward
en: He is not. What's left of the Ship and Crew are yours now, Mister Sharp.

speaker: Edward
en: I've still got his Portrait. I will hang it proudly.

speaker: Edward
en: Bonnet... did he make it out of that Mess alive, after all?

speaker: Bernard Woodhouse
en: You've returned, Captain Kenway. How was the Reunion with your old Acquaintance?

speaker: Edward
en: There wasn't one.

speaker: Bernard
en: An exquisite Piece, Captain Kenway. I could find Buyers for it, should you wish to sell.

speaker: Edward
en: Some things hold more value than Gold, Silver, or Rum.

speaker: Edward
en: '"'Life can't be all Pleasure and Distraction", you told me.

speaker: Edward
en: I fear I led you astray, my Friend.

speaker: Edward
en: I would have liked to hear those wild Stories he promised.

speaker: Edward
en: Those Soldiers in Kingston thought him hanged. If he's managed to give the Crown the slip, Bonnet's become quite the Pirate.

speaker: Edward
en: The Embers are still hot.

speaker: Abel Galvao
en: I have heard of this Captain Bonnet. They said he was a bumbling Fellow, sent away from Blackbeard's Fleet on account of Softness and Ill-discipline.

speaker: Edward
en: Bonnet's still learning to wear the Captain Title. He'll need Time.

speaker: Abel Galvao
en: That is time he may not have. Laxity breeds Contempt in one's Crew. Spare them the discipline they long for and they will rise against you.

speaker: Edward
en: Lucky for the Jackdaw, you've made sure this Crew has not been spared.

speaker: Abel Galvao
en: I can give and take, both.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: Stede Bonnet. I've heard this Name of late.

speaker: Edward
en: I'd not thought I'd hear it again.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: Word was he won Fame sticking it to the English at Charles-Towne.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, I'll be damned.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: By all accounts the Townspeople took him in as one of their own. Damn near rioted when the Governor put him in Bilboes.

speaker: Edward
en: He might have wriggled free of them, judging from his Letter. We'll see.

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: Stede Bonnet. The rivermen of Charles-Towne know that name.

speaker: Edward
en: What have you heard?

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: He took on two English Sloops in the shallows of the River. Perhaps it was three. In any event, he scuppered one with Cannon Fire.

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: He did it alone. Was it Luck? No matter.

speaker: Edward
en: Doesn't sound like the Bonnet I knew.

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: Can we ever truly know someone?

speaker: Edward
en: Right...

speaker: Pirate British 04 Male
en: You'll pay for your Treason, I swear it.

speaker: Pirate British 03 Male
en: Swear on what? What do you even have to your name?

speaker: Pirate British 04 Male
en: I swear on me dead Nan!

speaker: Pirate British 03 Male
en: Sod your Nan!

speaker: Pirate British 04 Male
en: You'll pay for that!

speaker: Sharp
en: Mark how the King's Men now tremble where they stand. They're scared, Lads!

speaker: Pirate British 04 Male
en: Look at that, we've shaken the Powder from their Wigs!

speaker: Sharp
en: Come over here, Arse-kissers! I'll turn your Coats a deeper shade of red!

speaker: Edward
en: A Letter from Stede Bonnet. What's become of him?

speaker: Fugitive
en: Do not believe for a moment that I will drop my guard! I know you are out there somewhere! I know the Assassins have sent a man to end my life! Yes, a Templar knows always that his work incurs this risk! But I would not choose another life after this one! For I have tasted the fruits of the best the Templars have to offer! So come, whoever you may be! Wherever you are! Come strike me down! And collect the pittance promised you.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: Muito Obrigado (Thank you), Captain. I wasn't sure if I could do what had to be done.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Galvão
en: I can't say. How are my Villagers who joined you in Great Inagua? They must think poorly of me for becoming a Pirate again.

speaker: Edward
en: I am sure they do not.

speaker: Galvão
en: Thank you, Captain.

speaker: Edward
en: The Padre's People have been hard at Work.

speaker: Henry Congreve
en: Well, it's not quite the Cathedral of Saint Paul. We've little in the way of Ornaments.

speaker: Diana Calverey
en: We don't need those. You've turned a musty old Hut into a Place of Worship. You did well, Henry.

speaker: Edward
en: Mistress Calverley, how are you settling in?

speaker: Diana
en: This Place is livelier than what I am used to. I enjoy it, but I do miss the Padre's Cooking.

speaker: Edward
en: I am sure he can still host the odd Pig Roast.

speaker: Diana
en: Yes. If I know him, he still carries every one of us in his Heart. Be good to him, my Dear.

speaker: Edward
en: Impressive Work, we had little use for that Derelict.

speaker: Henry
en: Thank you. How is the Padre holding up?

speaker: Edward
en: The Work on the Ship gives him Purpose.

speaker: Henry
en: Hmm. Keep him busy, Captain.

speaker: Edward
en: They've settled in well.

speaker: Edward
en: Your People are in good Spirits. Even built a Church. Would you like to take a look?

speaker: Galvão
en: Perhaps, another Time.

speaker: Edward
en: Do you still see yourself as a Man of God?

speaker: Galvão
en: A Man of God? I am a Man of the Sea. A Man of the Sword. I am a Believer and I am a Killer. There is no Refuge for my Sort. This World does not forgive, nor does it forget. The Jackdaw is Home now.

speaker: Edward
en: You've met the Assassins. They're Killers too, and they wouldn't turn you out.

speaker: Galvão
en: I've had enough of Orders and Titles. The Ocean is a wide and wild Expanse. Perhaps God created it for Wanderers like you and me? Those caught between Heaven and Hell.

speaker: Bonnet
en: A fine night, don't you think? Join me for a drink, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: God sink me for this pittance. One thousand reales for those maps. That's what? A hundred pounds at most. How's a man supposed to become rich in these times with a miser like Torres running the world?

speaker: Bonnet
en: Have you ever, ah... you ever worked on a plantation before?

speaker: Edward
en: You know what I'm thinking? I'd like to see this Observatory the governor was going on about. He said it were like a device that could follow people around and show where they were.

speaker: Bonnet
en: A ludicrous idea! Imagine my wife with such an advantage over me.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, imagine what a thing like that would be worth. Sell that to the right person and I'd be the richest pirate—...privateer in the West Indies. I'll catch you up, Bonnet. There's a Sage in that house I must speak to. In private.

speaker: Torres
en: ¡Basta ya! (Enough!) What is your true name, rogue?

speaker: Edward
en: It's, ah... Captain Pissoff.

speaker: Julien
en: Rien qu'un pauvre paysan! (Nothing but a filthy peasant.)

speaker: Torres
en: Where is the Sage? Did you set him free?

speaker: Edward
en: I had nothing to do with that, much as I wish I did.

speaker: Torres
en: Take him to the ports. Send him to Sevilla (Seville) with the Treasure Fleet.

speaker: Edward
en: Wait now! I delivered your treasures, didn't I?

speaker: Torres
en: You did, yes. But you robbed us of Duncan Walpole.

speaker: Antó
en: I have a plan but it won't be easy. Abraham is well connected and his pockets are deep. But we have located a man in his inner circle. We will tail him until he reveals our target.

speaker: Edward
en: Let me bring him to his end.

speaker: Antó
en: Here he comes now.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Evening.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Sir.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Pleasant night for a ball.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Pleasant night to celebrate impending victory.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Our numbers are many. They will not stand a chance.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Pity they will not be invited, to see us celebrate before our victory.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Quite.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Officers, may I join you?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Evening.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: The more the merrier.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: I've just come from the barracks. I'm quite certain the new weapons shipments will end our Maroon problem once and for all.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: That is the plan! That is the plan.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Do you think they'll be expecting it?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Most likely. They always do somehow. But this time it won't matter. Now, if you'll excuse me. I have a private matter to attend before I make my entrance.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: As do I.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: We will see you there.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Good evening. Will the Commander be in attendance tonight?

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Yes, I was just speaking with him. He is here somewhere.

speaker: Edward
en: The prat was right under our noses the whole time!

speaker: Antó
en: I've never met a soldier as cunning as a Maroon. It's no mistake he's been harder to defeat than the weak who came before him. He's a slippery one. He won't behave like an ordinary soldier.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Cockpits, you say?

speaker: Soldier 5
en: The highlands, furrowed through.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Furrowed, now?

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Earthquakes, man. They attack from ravines and gaps and caves and fissures made by earthquakes.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: "Cockpits."

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Laugh all you want. It's your funeral. I've heard the stories. I'm not getting caught.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: My father fought the s. One of the few to live to tell the tale.

speaker: Soldier 7
en: That Cudjoe, is he all the warrior they make him out to be?

speaker: Soldier 6
en: I spit at his name. And his brothers, too. But our war will be different. In our time, we'll take this land.

speaker: Soldier 8
en: How can we lose? They're fighting with scavenged shot and living on plantains. It'll be over in an afternoon.

speaker: Soldier 9
en: Cheers, mate! That's the spirit!

speaker: Soldier 10
en: It's the lookout men you really have to look out for.

speaker: Soldier 11
en: Is that supposed to be funny?

speaker: Soldier 10
en: No man. You hear the Abeng Horn, you don't laugh, you run. See you coming from miles away, they catch you where you least expect it.

speaker: Soldier 11
en: Surely our superior weapons give us the upper hand.

speaker: Soldier 10
en: Maybe. Still, I say, you hear that horn, you're in trouble. Could we not simply starve them out?

speaker: Soldier 11
en: How? The land is full of boar and fruit, and we need the rivers as much as they do.

speaker: Soldier 10
en: Could we not take the land then?

speaker: Soldier 11
en: Not according to treaty.

speaker: Soldier 10
en: Treaty? That's rich.

speaker: Kenneth
en: Antó. How many years have we fought? Your men, in the mountains, with no weapons to speak of. And my army, resplendent. And yet you live, and I die...

speaker: Antó
en: You lacked the conviction to win.

speaker: Edward
en: C'mon boys. You're lagging.

speaker: Vane
en: It's this bloody hemp!

speaker: Captain
en: Leftenant!

speaker: Edward
en: Hsst!

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Aye, sir!

speaker: Captain
en: The Commodore fears a revolt is nigh. His orders are to sink every goddamned pirate ship now anchored in that harbour. Tonight.

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Despite the Governor's wishes, sir?

speaker: Captain
en: This is a direct order, soldier! You will take position on the grounded galleon, and await the Commodore's further orders. Is that clear?

speaker: Lieutenant
en: Aye sir!

speaker: Vane
en: That conniving bastard! Someone ought to slit the Commodore's throat before he gets a chance to bark those orders.

speaker: Edward
en: You think so?

speaker: Vane
en: We're dead in the water otherwise.

speaker: Edward
en: All right. I'll kill him.

speaker: Accomplice
en: Your brains are baked! I won't take no part of killing the Commodore! Not one of the King's men!

speaker: Vane
en: We can't risk our good fortune. Go on, I'll be waiting for you.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Sir! We have information for the Commodore. An urgent matter.

speaker: Guard
en: Carry on.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Lots of sour blood between them two, Rogers and Chamberlaine. What's the issue?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Commodore don't think much of civilians, I reckon. And there's a rumour going round that Rogers is some kind of Jacobite. Or worse, that he's a .

speaker: Soldier 2
en: O, I could think of worse!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Gather those two men there! You lads! Follow and lay aboard. The Commodore has a job for you.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Aye, sir! I heard the Commodore ranting and raving about Woodes Rogers, calling him a heathen and whatnot. What's happened to set them two off?

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Hush, man! You don't want the governor's ire brought down on you. He's a mysterious sort.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Well, I'm much more afraid of the Commodore, in truth. He's a serious chap. No sense of humour.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Take positions and prepare to decamp on the Commodore's orders!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Aye, sir!

speaker: Chamberlaine
en: Remember our object, lads. We're here to punch holes in every goddamned pirate ship anchored in the northern harbor! If you doubt the honour of our cause here... and if my disavowal of our coward Governor's wishes causes you anxiety, then you are free to debark my vessel and stay ashore! But I will not stand idle by as the rats scurrying about this island plot and scheme to do us direct harm! So tumble up there, men! Tumble up all! Prepare to loose the topsails! That's right! Lay aloft, quick as you please! Ready to loose the topsails on my signal. All ready forward? Wait for my signal, please!

speaker: Edward
en: The Governor's given us a pardon, Commodore. Don't a man's word mean anything in these times?

speaker: Chamberlaine
en: Has syphilis clouded your mind? Why scratch and claw to protect such squalor? You're parasites, feeding off the industry of honest men!

speaker: Edward
en: Much like King George in that respect.

speaker: Chamberlaine
en: Know your place, peasant! You may have taken my life, but you have not improved your own by any measure!

speaker: Edward
en: Does some purpose keep you talking?

speaker: Chamberlaine
en: If not for that heathen, Governor Rogers, I'd have seen you hanged from your own crosstrees, worm! All of you!

speaker: Contraband
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Let none say that the Templar's lack Style.

speaker: Barkeeper
en: More?

speaker: Edward
en: Bring a bottle.

speaker: Barkeeper
en: I'd see some Colour first.

speaker: Roberts
en: Will this do?

speaker: Roberts
en: In all your years out here, you could never achieve what I have done in one-fifth the time. Because you are a good man, Edward. See? Goodness is your disease...

speaker: Edward
en: That's my prize, Roberts. Give it here!

speaker: Roberts
en: Remember my creed, boy? A short life and a merry one. That is all. The world owes us nothing more than this. So take what you will, and then die before you live to see yourself made a fool.

speaker: Edward
en: Give it here!

speaker: Roberts
en: That's right, boy! Take it!

speaker: Edward
en: I'll sweeten you, maggot! I'll cut you down!

speaker: Roberts
en: Calm... little puppy. And slink back to your kennel. You haven't the mettle for my brand of madness.

speaker: Edward
en: Roberts!

speaker: Hornigold
en: Welcome aboard, Kenway! It's prizes, plunder and adventure ahead. Are you game?

speaker: Edward
en: Outta my way, Ben.

speaker: Thatch
en: Raise a glass to freedom, lads! Here's to gentlemen of fortune and women of leisure!

speaker: Mary
en: To a world full of rogues better than all the kings and queens that kick us about!

speaker: Roberts
en: As gentlemen of fortune we enjoy plenty and satisfaction, pleasure and ease, liberty and power... What man with a sensible mind would choose the former life? For I have dipped my hands in muddied waters, and withdrawing them find 'tis better to be a commander than a common man!

speaker: Rogers
en: Aesop once wrote of an eagle, soaring high above a shepherd's field, that swooped down on powerful wings to seize a grazing lamb and carry it off to her nest. Flying close by, a jackdaw saw the deed, and it filled his head with the idea that he too was just as strong and capable. So with a great flapping and rustling of feathers, the jackdaw came down swiftly and clutched at the coat of a large ram. But when he tried to fly away, he found he could not lift the animal, for his size and strength were not up to the task. And even as the jackdaw struggled, the ram hardly noticed he was there. Nearby, just across the field, the shepherd saw the fluttering bird and was quite amused. Running up, he captured the jackdaw and its wings. That evening he gave the jackdaw to his children as a gift. "What an odd little bird this is, father!" they laughed and shouted. "What do you call him?" "This is a jackdaw," the father said. "But if you should ask him, he would claim to be an eagle."

speaker: Caroline
en: No more than two years! You promised me

speaker: Edward
en: You left! When I needed you the most.

speaker: Caroline
en: But you had me! What keeps you wandering? Do I not make you happy?

speaker: Edward
en: I'm so close, Caroline! Please! Just let me do this!

speaker: Mary
en: Is everything you do out of spite, Edward?

speaker: Edward
en: It's not spite that's driving me Mary. It's courage!

speaker: Mary
en: Courage for what, man? There's no one left in your life to care!

speaker: Edward
en: God damn you all! I can handle this!

speaker: Mary
en: You lout! Always tearing down when you could be building things up. Or building yourself up, if nothing else!

speaker: Edward
en: Just leave me be!

speaker: Mary
en: Change course, Edward! Change your bloody course before it's too late!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Captain Kenway. You look like a bowl of .

speaker: Edward
en: Christ. I've got a head for ten.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: On your feet.

speaker: Edward
en: You put me on a spot, Adé. After you leaving me with Roberts, I should have hard feelings about seeing you here. But mostly, I'm bloody glad.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Me too, breddah. And you'll be chuffed to know your Jackdaw is still in one piece.

speaker: Edward
en: Shall we set sail for- You're leaving?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye, Edward. For I've another calling elsewhere.

speaker: Edward
en: Adé, listen...

speaker: Adéwalé
en: When your heart and your head are ready, visit the Assassins. I think you'll understand then...

speaker: Deserter
en: (I'll stay here, and nowhere else. And they'll look but they won't find me. Ha! No! Devil take them they're a band of monkeys scratching their arses. I'll never submit! They'll never find me. They never will, for I'm invisible to all but God's eyes.)

speaker: Edward
en: What the hell's happened here? Were you attacked?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Other way 'round. It were Blackbeard who struck first. Opened fire on a British Man O' War, the pillock!

speaker: Edward
en: What in God's name for?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Still searching for medicines. But he's gone barmy if you ask me.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll bring him home.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Leave him, man! He's heaped this trouble on himself!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Captain, there's a wreck yonder. Looks recent!

speaker: Edward
en: I see it. Let's hope Thatch hasn't come to the same end.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Another bit of wreckage, captain. This is looking grim.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Keep your eyes peeled. Blast! This is getting well out of hand.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: A dozen crates of medicine should not be so hard to come by.

speaker: Edward
en: That ain't my meaning. It's Thatch and Hornigold and this pointless feud of theirs. Can't you feel it?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I do, aye. But both men have their hearts in a good place. Both want the best for the people of Nassau.

speaker: Edward
en: But is that the best course for us? Saving a city that ain't worth much? We're not men made to govern. We take and spend, and live heartily... wherever we go.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What solution would you propose?

speaker: Edward
en: The answer's in wealth and power, not politics. If we found the Observatory, we'd see enough money to buy the whole of England. Or it might be... we'd lord over these kings and emperors like they was peasants themselves.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: A lot of large talk, captain. But is it your crew you sail for... or yourself?

speaker: Edward
en: I mean the best for these men, Adé. I do. But this don't sit right. I feel like I'm running errands, not living my life.

speaker: Edward
en: Adé. See there!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: It's her, captain! The Queen Anne's Revenge. And she's in a bad way.

speaker: Edward
en: There's no time for a vote. Thatch is outnumbered.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: The crew'll understand. Beat to quarters, lads! We're sailing into hell!

speaker: Edward
en: Thatch is overwhelmed. I'm going ashore.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I'll keep the Jackdaw circling.

speaker: Thatch
en: Did all your book-learning prepare you for a scuffle of this sort, Mister Bonnet?

speaker: Stede
en: Not in the least, no.

speaker: Thatch
en: For certain, there's more to be learned by doing than reading. Remember that!

speaker: Edward
en: You stirred up a nest of trouble, Thatch!

speaker: Thatch
en: In service of a noble cause.

speaker: Edward
en: Medicines, I hope you mean!

speaker: Thatch
en: Aye. A galleon nearby. And if we crack these lobsters quick, we might catch up to her.

speaker: Stede
en: Oh God! Some aid here! Edward! Please!

speaker: Edward
en: Hang in there, Bonnet! Keep your arms up and your back to the sea!

speaker: Edward
en: You don't do nothing subtle, do ya, Thatch?

speaker: Thatch
en: Legends ain't born from mildness.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah! Gentlemen, our galleon has reappeared!

speaker: Edward
en: Heads up!

speaker: Thatch
en: Back to my ship, quick as you please. It'll not slip away now!

speaker: Stede
en: Oh, this is too much!

speaker: Thatch
en: I'll see you back to your Jackdaw when the smoke has cleared. But for now I need a helmsman.

speaker: Edward
en: Call it out!

speaker: Thatch
en: Loose the mains! And head straight for that bloody ship. We'll have our medicines in little time at all!

speaker: Crewman
en: We're short on powder, Captain!

speaker: Thatch
en: Blast! And the galleon's all but sunk!

speaker: Edward
en: I'm seeing the devil you promised, Thatch.

speaker: Thatch
en: Argh... I'd have shown them my angel if they'd taken quarter. But there's no going back now! So ram that bastard! With all the wind you've got!

speaker: Thatch
en: She's cracked, lads! Send 'em to hell! Find the captain and END this.

speaker: Thatch
en: I'm not a man accustomed to murder, captain. And if you'd taken quarter, you'd not be seeping now.

speaker: Captain
en: Suck a muzzle, gobshite. You'll be hanged and sun-dried, just as them that were in Boston.

speaker: Thatch
en: The King's called for a pardon!

speaker: Israel
en: Captain... we've searched the hold. It's a middling take, but the medicine we found bears a Charles-Towne stamp.

speaker: Thatch
en: Thank you, Mr. Hands.

speaker: Edward
en: We cannot resupply Nassau out here by force and accident alone. We should go to Charles-Towne for the lot.

speaker: Stede
en: Hello! A-are we victorious? I fear I am not built for the fatigue and care required to live as a man of fortune.

speaker: Thatch
en: Meet me in Charles-towne. One month from today.

speaker: Anne
en: Another?

speaker: Edward
en: A rum this time.

speaker: Anne
en: And where'd I find fresh eggs in this wretched town? There's little else but piss and insects.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. We're working on that.

speaker: Rackham
en: Dear lady, what do they call you?

speaker: Anne
en: Anne, when they're sober. A jilt when they're sauced. But never Lady.

speaker: Rackham
en: Well, goodly Anne I—Ah!

speaker: Vane
en: Bag of shite! Do you hear me? It's a bag of bloody shite! It's a ruse to keep us soft before they attack Nassau! You'll see. Mark me.

speaker: Thatch
en: It's no ruse, Vane. I heard it straight from the mouth of a greasy Bermudan captain. There's a pardon on offer for any pirate that wants it.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Ruse or not, I think it's plain the British may return to Nassau. With arms no doubt. We'll need a plan.

speaker: Thatch
en: Walk with us, Kenway. There's trouble brewing...

speaker: Hornigold
en: In the absence of any clear ideas, I say we lay low. No piracies and no violence. Do nothing to ruffle the King's feathers for now.

speaker: Thatch
en: Preserving the king's plumage is no concern of mine, Ben.

speaker: Hornigold
en: It will be when he sends his soldiers to scrub this island clean of our residue! Look around you, man. Is this cesspool worth dying for?

speaker: Thatch
en: Aye! It's our republic! Our idea! A free land for free men, remember? So maybe it's filthy to look at. But ain't it still an idea worth fighting for?

speaker: Hornigold
en: I can't be sure. For when I look on the fruits of our years of labor, all I see is sickness... Idleness.. Idiocy.

speaker: Thatch
en: Not a sunbeam of difference between here and London then, eh?

speaker: Edward
en: Thatch is right, man. Taking a wide view, we're not doing so bad out here. There's sun, rum, and leisure as far as the eye can see.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Aye, Nassau may look fine from a distance, but at its core there's a disease I cannot stomach.

speaker: Edward
en: Sickness can be cured, Ben. If only you have the right medicine.

speaker: Hornigold
en: But a corpse cannot be reanimated!

speaker: Thatch
en: I can't believe the shite I'm hearing drop from your lips! Why not take the pardon now and be done with it!

speaker: Edward
en: Peace! Both of you. We can satisfy both aims if we work together. Find medicines to ease our burdens here, but in a way that don't attract the British.

speaker: Thatch
en: I'd wager the nearest doctor is sitting pretty in Havana. Not a place I mean to go.

speaker: Edward
en: The Spanish fleet that sunk two years back would have some medicine. All sealed up in glass vials.

speaker: Thatch
en: You'd need a diving bell to reach those depths.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. And with some coin and a few supplies, a diving bell won't be hard to come by.

speaker: Hornigold
en: This is a plan I can stand behind. Find medicines without stirring up trouble. Agreed, Thatch?

speaker: Thatch
en: Agreed, aye. I'll meet you near the wrecks as soon as you're able, Kenway.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Remember, Thatch! Keep your cannons corked!

speaker: Thatch
en: Piss off, Ben!

speaker: Edward
en: Devil in his hole, Thatch! This is a darling galley. Thirty-two guns, is it?

speaker: Thatch
en: I lost count at forty.

speaker: Edward
en: You've stepped up a rung. So... Any luck finding medicines here?

speaker: Thatch
en: Nothing 'round this spot, sadly. But there's a few wrecks yonder that haven't been scoured by nothing but crabs and coral.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll have a look.

speaker: Stede
en: Edward? Edward, is that you? My goodness, the West Indies is a compact place!

speaker: Edward
en: Allo, Bonnet. A surprise seeing you out here.

speaker: Stede
en: I met Mister Thatch a month or so ago and he offered to take me under his yardarms, so to speak. Says I must wash the hayseed from my hair before I'm a true pirate.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, good luck to you then. Worse men have become better under Blackbeard's watch.

speaker: Thatch
en: Ahoy! Any luck?

speaker: Edward
en: I found one crate hidden beneath a school of sharks. Sadly, the elixir inside is... quite spoilt.

speaker: Thatch
en: Plague and perish! Will we steal medicines now?

speaker: Edward
en: Remember the pardon, Thatch. We're to be subtle.

speaker: Thatch
en: Says Hornigold! A pirate now too proud to call himself one!

speaker: Edward
en: Ah, he prefers caution to cannons.

speaker: Thatch
en: Caution's nothing without charisma! For if a man plays the fool, then it's only fools he'll persuade. But appear to be the devil, and all men will submit.

speaker: Edward
en: And would you be the devil?

speaker: Thatch
en: For an audience, aye. It's all a big show. Give your quarry something to fear, some hellish thing from a fever'd dream, and men will drop to their knees pleading for their Lord before aught else!

speaker: Stede
en: Oh God...

speaker: Edward
en: Looks fine.

speaker: Thatch
en: Course it does. If you can find a quiet way to acquire medicines, tell me soon. Otherwise, I'll handle it meself.

speaker: Edward
en: Ahoy, Kidd. You missed quite a time.

speaker: Kidd
en: Aye. Pity about Nassau. And Blackbeard flying the coop.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh, we'll see about Thatch. Vane's off to see him now, and I'm following soon.

speaker: Kidd
en: This is what's left of your experiment in democracy?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, we do as we please here. And take our time doing it.

speaker: Kidd
en: For Christ's sake, Edward. Don't anything but the stink of riches wrinkle your nose?

speaker: Edward
en: What's got into you, man?

speaker: Kidd
en: Reality, mate. Reality.

speaker: Kidd
en: See that you ain't pulled into the drink by this drowning rat.

speaker: Edward
en: Oy! I've lived longer than most men who trod this path!

speaker: Vane
en: A great disappointment you are, Thatch! His mind's made up to stay, he says. So sod 'im! And hang all of you lot that follow this sorry bastard into obscurity!

speaker: Thatch
en: That man's a prick.

speaker: Thatch
en: I know you've come to call me home, Kenway. And your faith in me is kind. But with Nassau done in, I feel I'm finished.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm not of the same mind, mate. But I won't begrudge you the state of yours.

speaker: Thatch
en: You still looking for that Sage fellow?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye.

speaker: Thatch
en: Taking a prize a month back, I heard a man named Roberts was working a slave ship called the Princess. Might want to see about it.

speaker: Edward
en: The Princess. Cheers, Thatch.

speaker: Thatch
en: Now don't stand there like a barrel of wet fish. We're celebrating my retirement!

speaker: Thatch
en: Uncork this man's breakfast!

speaker: Edward
en: Save us a few bottles, eh?

speaker: Jenkins
en: Lads? Lieutenant? You out here?

speaker: Maynard
en: Stay here. Shoot anything that moves. Jenkins. What's the news?

speaker: Jenkins
en: What was that?

speaker: Maynard
en: You certain you didn't bring some of those sand rats in tow, Jenkins? Look sharp. Stevens, make certain there's no surprises.

speaker: Stevens
en: Aye, sir.

speaker: Maynard
en: Secure the other side and watch the path.

speaker: Stevens
en: Aye.

speaker: Jenkins
en: There was a deserter among them who recalled my face. I sliced into his gullet before any word left his lips.

speaker: Maynard
en: Anybody see you?

speaker: Jenkins
en: Don't think so, sir. But I reckon Kenway suspects something. He don't miss much.

speaker: Maynard
en: Tell me about the beach.

speaker: Jenkins
en: A fair gathering, sir. Most too drunk to stand.

speaker: Maynard
en: That will suit our purpose. Tell me about Edward Teach. What sort of man is he?

speaker: Jenkins
en: It's Thatch, sir. Least, that's what he calls himself. But he's a mad bugger, he is. Cracked as a glass teapot, sir.

speaker: Maynard
en: Details man! Stop talking in gibberish.

speaker: Jenkins
en: Well sir, he likes his drink for instance. Only he makes 'em queer. Takes the usual rum flip, and fills it with half a weight of gunpowder to top it off.

speaker: Maynard
en: Did I hear you aright? He DRINKS gunpowder?

speaker: Jenkins
en: Aye, sir. Just for show. And only last week he rounded up a score of his crew and bade us sit in the hold of his ship while he burnt off sulfur and other sickening minerals. We just sat there like it was one of a million pits of hell, and nothing less ordinary.

speaker: Maynard
en: Good GOD. What the hell for?

speaker: Jenkins
en: Likes to test his crew is all. Tease out their fitness and what. 'Course it always turned out he was the fittest of the lot. Thought for a moment I'd die there. Bloody savages.

speaker: Maynard
en: Have no fear, soldier. This will be the end of them. Come on. It's time. Quickly, send the signal. And remember always this day.

speaker: Edward
en: What the devil...?

speaker: Thatch
en: Where the hell is Kenway? Note the day, lads! Today we send the King's finest to their graves!

speaker: Thatch
en: We've knocked them on the heads except three or four. Let's jump aboard and cut 'em to pieces! Bury the lot, boys. Take no guff! I'll cleave ye lengthwise, maggots! How you be doing, Edward m'lad? I'll not fall here today, bastards! Come at me! Can you fight free, lad? Can ye make it clear? Here's the path to perdition!

speaker: Thatch
en: Kenway!

speaker: Edward
en: Here!

speaker: Thatch
en: In a world without gold, we might have been heroes!

speaker: Edward
en: THATCH!

speaker: Edward
en: Devil curse me... Where's the Jackdaw...!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What of Thatch, sir? Did he fall? Captain?

speaker: Edward
en: He drinks damnation.

speaker: Pirate
en: (Send word if you see anything. Anything at all. No treasure, no rest! Who has the map? I must see it for myself. This treasure had better be on the next boat to Seville, or you'll swim back to Havana!)

en: Hold fast! She's on us!

speaker: Edward
en: Can you see her?

speaker: Edward
en: Man the cannons!

speaker: Abel
en: Our helmsman's dead! Someone take the wheel! Kenway! Take the bloody wheel! Hughes is dead, Kenway! You'll have to steer this bastard!

speaker: Abel
en: Uncork the cannons, lad! Unload all the shot we have! Fire on those bastards! We'll give a good . Ready!

speaker: Abel
en: Bring us close, Kenway! We can scuttle her!

speaker: Crewman
en: The magazine! It's going up!

speaker: Abel
en: Douse the flames! Get in there, you mongrel!

speaker: Caroline
en: Is it dangerous? Edward?

speaker: Edward
en: Hm?

speaker: Caroline
en: Privateering. Is it dangerous?

speaker: Edward
en: Wouldn't pay so nice if it weren't.

speaker: Caroline
en: Why not sail with the king's navy? Earn a proper wage. Sail under gentlemen.

speaker: Edward
en: Sod the navy's gentlemen. For every shilling I'd earn, the captain'd get six hundred. That's no way to earn a fortune.

speaker: Caroline
en: We don't need a fortune.

speaker: Edward
en: It's not about need, Caroline. I want food that don't make me sick. I want walls that hold back the wind. I want a decent life.

speaker: Caroline
en: H-how long would you be gone with these privateers?

speaker: Edward
en: A year, I reckon. Two at the most.

speaker: Caroline
en: All right. No more than two... promise me...

speaker: Edward
en: Sod it.

speaker: Edward
en: Damn!

speaker: Edward
en: Was it good for you as well?

speaker: Duncan
en: Havana... I must get to Havana.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, I'll just build us another ship, will I?

speaker: Duncan
en: I can pay you. Isn't that the sound you pirates like best? One hundred escudos.

speaker: Edward
en: Keep talking.

speaker: Duncan
en: Will you or won't you!

speaker: Edward
en: You don't have that gold on you now, do you?

speaker: Duncan
en: Bloody fucking pirates!

speaker: Edward
en: I am on to you, sneaksby!

speaker: Edward
en: Come on, mate! We're off to a bad start! It's a hundred or more to Havana! Will you walk that distance?

speaker: Edward
en: Posh git. Where's he running to?

speaker: Duncan
en: Follow and I'll kill you!

speaker: Edward
en: We could work together on this!

speaker: Duncan
en: Keep your distance!

speaker: Duncan
en: Follow and I'll kill you!

speaker: Edward
en: Come on, mate! We're off to a bad start! We could work together on this! It's a hundred leagues or more to Havana! Will you walk that distance?

speaker: Duncan
en: Keep your distance!

speaker: Edward
en: Posh git. Where's he running to?

speaker: Edward
en: Forget what I said. We can start over.

speaker: Duncan
en: Shove off, you vulture.

speaker: Edward
en: This one vanishes into shadow.

speaker: Edward
en: Now we've drawn swords, mate. I'm beginning to think that you're not keen on my aid.

speaker: Duncan
en: My business bears greater purpose than a thief like you could comprehend.

speaker: Duncan
en: I warned you.

speaker: Edward
en: Why the ill temper? Hiding something?

speaker: Edward
en: We don't have to fight. Let's make a deal.

speaker: Duncan
en: Filthy cutpurse!

speaker: Edward
en: That looks painful.

speaker: Duncan
en: Die you leech!

speaker: Edward
en: Mr. Walpole... let's collect your reward.

speaker: Edward
en: That schooner'll do me just fine...

speaker: Edward
en: Now to find my way off this bleedin' rock.

speaker: Edward
en: That schooner'll do me just fine... if only I can preserve some of its crew.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Commodore's gone ahead to Kingston. We're to commandeer this lubber's ship and follow.

speaker: Stede
en: S-sorry, uh, Kingston? No, no... our destination is Havana. I'm just a merchant

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Quiet, you bleedin' pirate! You'll hang for the mess you made out there.

speaker: Stede
en: Sir, I had nothing to do with this attack. My crew and I had merely anchored to water and resupply!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Hold it! Stop them!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Give me one reason I shouldn't vent your skull.

speaker: Stede
en: Take my sugar! Take anything you like! I'll pay you! Anything you like! Oh God. Oooooh God! Ahhh! Ah!

speaker: Stede
en: By God's grace, sir, you saved me. A profusion of thanks!

speaker: Edward
en: Is that yours?

speaker: Stede
en: It is my vessel, yes. But, ah... here lies its poor captain. And I have no art for sailing.

speaker: Edward
en: I can pilot her myself. No mind.

speaker: Stede
en: You don't mean to abscond with my ship, do you?

speaker: Edward
en: I'm Duncan. What's your name, friend?

speaker: Stede
en: Stede. Stede Bonnet.

speaker: Edward
en: Well Mister Bonnet, let this stay 'twixt us... but I am on a secret errand for His Majesty the King, God save him, and I must get to Havana with speed.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah... that is a relief, sir. Havana is also my destination. Our ways lie together!

speaker: Edward
en: Natural allies then.

speaker: Stede
en: Oh, you put me at ease, sir. To think I took you for a pirate when you first appeared.

speaker: Edward
en: Did you?

speaker: Stede
en: Yes! You have an... uncommon way of handling yourself. Quick and easy, if I may say. Gave me quite a fright! But all things considered, I think it's turned out to be a rather fortuitous day, hasn't it?

speaker: Stede
en: Lacking a rowboat, I'm afraid we'll have to swim to my ship.

speaker: Edward
en: Hardly the worst thing to happen.

speaker: Stede
en: Oh... Oh, this is difficult. I should have taken the coat off!

speaker: Stede
en: Welcome aboard, Duncan. She's a modest schooner but well-suited to my purpose. Trafficking cargo from my plantation and such.

speaker: Edward
en: She'll do fine. There's a strong wind now. Let's strike to full, shall we?

speaker: Stede
en: Ah, there's a tug of the wind at my hair! I find a bracing comfort in the feel and smell of the ocean. The raw stink of... of possibility!

speaker: Edward
en: That's a top way of seeing it, mate.

speaker: Stede
en: We've really opened it up now, haven't we! Those sailors were quite animated by the idea of pirates roaming these waters. Is it a real danger, do you suppose?

speaker: Edward
en: A possibility. But most pirates stalk the windward passage between Cuba and Hispaniola.

speaker: Stede
en: Oh, I see. Yes, that is a bustling strait. But I shouldn't worry about being waylaid by pirates, truth be told. My ship is small and I have nothing of immense value. Sugarcane and its yields, molasses, rum, that sort of thing.

speaker: Edward
en: There's not a pirate living who'd turn his back on a keg of rum.

speaker: Stede
en: Well, yes... yes, I suppose that's true. You're a natural sailor, Duncan.

speaker: Stede
en: Twas no thanks to you lot that I'm back. You can thank Duncan, here.

speaker: Stede
en: Welcome aboard, Duncan. She's a modest schooner but well-suited to my purpose. Trafficking cargo from my plantation and such.

speaker: Edward
en: She'll do fine.

speaker: Stede
en: If you are so inclined, you may steer her yourself. My helmsman and quartermaster were among those killed.

speaker: Edward
en: Ready yourselves, lads. The Spanish Navy hunts in packs, and we make for Havana.

speaker: Sailor
en: Ahoy.

speaker: Edward
en: Has a good feel. We'll first strike to half-sail to get ourselves moving.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah, there's a tug of the wind at my hair! I find a bracing comfort in the feel and smell of the ocean. The raw stink of... of possibility!

speaker: Edward
en: That's a top way of seeing it, mate. There's a strong wind now. Let's strike to full, shall we?

speaker: Stede
en: We've really opened it up now, haven't we!

speaker: Stede
en: Oh! what a magnificent creature.

speaker: Stede
en: You're a natural sailor, Duncan.

speaker: Edward
en: I did a decent trick at the helm some time ago. Two years before the mast as a privateer.

speaker: Stede
en: Dash my buttons! Your life seems a grand one, if I may say. So full of adventure! How marvelous.

speaker: Edward
en: I have seen my share of strangeness, aye.

speaker: Anne
en: Kenway, you look a right mess.

speaker: Edward
en: Glad to know I can always rely on you to cheer me up.

speaker: Anne
en: You're very welcome. Now can you explain what that sour look is for?

speaker: Edward
en: That brute of a Spaniard, El Tiburón, gave me quite the wallop. I'm afraid my pride has been damaged.

speaker: Anne
en: Since when do you accept defeat?

speaker: Edward
en: When the man is draped in an inch of steel.

speaker: Anne
en: Every suit of armor has kinks. You just have to find them.

speaker: Edward
en: Then find them I will! After another pint.

speaker: Anne
en: Jaysus, Kenway, another pint and you won't be able to find your own boots.

speaker: Edward
en: Are the boots where the kinks are?

speaker: Anne
en: Off with you! Go sleep it off, Kenway. The Spaniard isn't going anywhere yet.

speaker: Edward
en: But... what about my pride?

speaker: Anne
en: You're in no state to be proud of anything. Reclaim your pride in the morning.

speaker: Anne
en: You look even worse than before.

speaker: Edward
en: He's made a fool of me yet again.

speaker: Anne
en: Perhaps you should give up this grudge.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll not give it up. I'll just ignore it for a while longer.

speaker: Anne
en: With the aid of ale?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, and plenty of it.

speaker: Anne
en: Welcome back, Kenway. You certainly seem in a better mood than earlier.

speaker: Edward
en: I am. El Tiburón has received his comeuppance.

speaker: Anne
en: So rather than drowing your sorrows, you are here to celebrate your victory.

speaker: Edward
en: Exactly. A pint, if you will.

speaker: Anne
en: Just one?

speaker: Edward
en: For now. The day is still young.

speaker: Edward
en: Gentlemen. How do you find it here?

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: It will work for us. But our goal must be to scatter our operations. To live and work among the people we protect, just as Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad once counseled.

speaker: Edward
en: Well until that time, it's yours as you see fit.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Edward... Captain Woodes Rogers survived his wounds. He has since returned to England... shamed and in great debt, but no less a threat.

speaker: Edward
en: I will finish that job when I return. You have my word. Evening, Anne.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll be sailing for London in the next few months. I'd be a hopeful man if you were beside me.

speaker: Anne
en: England's the wrong way 'round the globe for an Irishwoman.

speaker: Edward
en: Will you stay with the Assassins?

speaker: Anne
en: No. I haven't got that kind of conviction in my heart. You?

speaker: Edward
en: In time, aye... when my mind is settled and my blood is cooled.

speaker: Sailor
en: Sail ho! Coming into the cove!

speaker: Anne
en: You're a good man, Edward. And if you learn to keep settled in one place for more than a week, you'll make a fine father too.

speaker: Anne
en: Of all the money that e'er I had, / I spent it in good company. / And all the harm that e'er I've done, / Alas! it was to none but me. / And all I've done for want of wit / To mem'ry now, I can't recall / So fill to me the parting glass / Good night and joy be with you all. / Oh, all the comrades that e'er I had, / They're sorry for my going away, / And all the sweethearts that e'er I've loved, / They'd wish me one more day to stay, / But since it falls unto my lot, / That I should rise and you should not, / I'll gently rise and softly call, / Good night and joy be with you all.

speaker: Anne
en: What's this Torres doing looking for the Observatory when you're holding the treasure yourself?

speaker: Edward
en: Torres doesn't know I have it.

speaker: Anne
en: So why bring it to him, and risk its capture?

speaker: Edward
en: I'd like him to know I have it, just before he dies.

speaker: Anne
en: Edward, there's a fleet blocking the cove we want.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. The armada. That's Torres and his men.

speaker: Anne
en: And you're going to do what exactly?

speaker: Edward
en: Find our way past them.

speaker: Anne
en: Who's this Torres? And what's your man done to earn a death sentence?

speaker: Edward
en: He's a Templar, like Rogers and Hornigold. Men cooking up schemes to use the Observatory for ill purposes. For power and control. The violence he'd cause with this thing would be subtle, but heavy. Deadly, yet leaving no mark. Does that make sense?

speaker: Anne
en: Like if there was a drought, and people was thirsty, and one man had a large cask of water but gave a sip to none. He'd be a killer with no blood on his hands.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, like that.

speaker: Anne
en: Fair enough.

speaker: Anne
en: Lord, there's a bit of chill, isn't there? Hm. Thought we might see some soldiers and the like. Maybe they've gone?

speaker: Edward
en: No. They're here. Deep in the jungle.

speaker: Anne
en: Soldiers, just there! What should we do? Jaysus, look at all this! Corpses for miles.

speaker: Edward
en: They brought every ounce of menace they had.

speaker: Anne
en: Do you see them, Edward? There's Spaniards up ahead.

speaker: Anne
en: It's all so strange. What is it?

speaker: Edward
en: Later, Anne. I'll tell you when all this is finished.

speaker: Anne
en: Holy Mother of God. Is this the place we've come to see?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Stand watch here, and let none follow.

speaker: Anne
en: Fit for another dozen fights, aye. Go on, you! There's not much time.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: (Please! Please don't leave me! He's here! The pirate is here! Spare me... please! I do not want to die.)

speaker: Soldiers
en: (Don't get near that!) (Be careful!) (God, no..!) Aieeeee! (Help!) (Jesus, help me!) (God no! No!)

speaker: Torres
en: We could have worked together, Edward. We could have taken power for ourselves! And brought these miserable empires to their knees! There is so much potential in you. So much you have not yet accomplished! I could show you things. Mysteries beyond anything that you could imagine!

speaker: Torres
en: Captain Kenway. Ever a splinter in my side. Does this murder fulfill you?

speaker: Edward
en: I'm only seeing a job done, Torres. As you'd have done with me.

speaker: Torres
en: As we have done, I think. You have no family anymore, no friends, no future. Your losses are far greater than ours.

speaker: Edward
en: That may be. But killing you rights a far greater wrong than ever I did.

speaker: Torres
en: You honestly believe that?

speaker: Edward
en: You would see all of mankind corralled into a neatly furnished prison, safe and sober, yet dulled beyond reason and sapped of all spirit. So, aye... with everything I've seen and learned in these last years, I do believe it.

speaker: Torres
en: You wear your convictions well. They suit you...

speaker: Edward
en: Torres awakened something fierce! Are we safe?

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: With the device returned, I believe so.

speaker: Anne
en: What d'ye call this place?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Captain Kenway's folly.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: We will seal this place, and discard the key. Until another Sage appears, this door will remain locked.

speaker: Edward
en: There were vials when I came here last. Filled with the blood of ancient men, Roberts said. But they're gone now.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Then it's up to us to recover them. Before the Templars catch wind of this. You could join us in that cause.

speaker: Edward
en: I will. But... only after I fix what I mangled back home.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: It arrived last week.

speaker: Leader
en: I've a here, only one of a different sort, lads. No country or king bids us fight today... it's a secret Order of well-to-do aristocrats who'd pay better than any monarch or governor.

speaker: Privateer
en: Who do you mean, Captain?

speaker: Leader
en: I'd wager he were a Templar, but I can't rightly say, for I only met him once. Be that as it may, his orders are clear and strict, and his pay is frightful good.

speaker: Privateer
en: What's he asking?

speaker: Leader
en: He wants that we should sail to a small village near Yucatán, where we'll find all manner of heathens hopping around in hoods and robes. Says he'll give us a fortune to do any kind of damage we can.

speaker: Privateer
en: That suits me! The natives of these lands never put up no fight we can't manage.

speaker: Eye for an Eye
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus Omega.

speaker: Edward
en: Our merchant friend has earned himself some serious enemies.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye, captain. They seem rather committed to his capture.

speaker: Edward
en: Christ! This reward had better be worth it.

speaker: Edward
en: The Commodore's dead. Are we ready?

speaker: Vane
en: We're close. We got a problem with the galleon as a couple of dozen- Bloody hell.

speaker: Vane
en: You'd raise a cloud here, ya lout? You're sitting on enough gunpowder to blow New Providence off its rocks!

speaker: Rackham
en: Lay off me, mate! I'm well chafed!

speaker: Vane
en: As I was telling, a squad of lobsters has commandeered our galleon. We're going to have to clear it out before we use them cannons to break the blockade.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Stay near the fire ship, Captain. Keep it afloat! Don't let them sink our fire ship. That's our ace. The Brits are on to us! Look there!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: The fire ship's about to blow! Steer clear, captain!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: We broke through! Get clear of the fleet now, and we're home free. No preshah, eh Kenway? The (black magic) comes natural to us.

speaker: Edward
en: We ain't out of this yet.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: A mighty mess there.

speaker: Vane
en: Ha ha ha! Burn you bastards! The pardon up your ARSE, Governor!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Prancing about like they took a prize... hmph.

speaker: Rhona
en: Edward, we've reduced that Templar cad, Flint, to a fraction of his power. The only thing standing between you and your key now is Flint himself.

speaker: Edward
en: You have an approach in mind?

speaker: Rhona
en: I'll engage him in combat. And you circle around - carefully - and well, you know the rest.

speaker: Edward
en: Suddenly squeamish, Rhona? Can't quite bring yourself to kill him?

speaker: Rhona
en: Of course not! I just don't want you to feel like I'm telling you what to do.

speaker: Edward
en: I think that injury must have left you with a touch of fever.

speaker: Rhona
en: Can we go now?

speaker: Edward
en: Let's.

speaker: Rhona
en: Oh, he won't be hard to find, the cheeky bastard, strutting about like the cock of the walk.

speaker: Edward
en: Admit it, Rhona. Deep down, you like the walk of that cock.

speaker: Rhona
en: I can arrange to have you in thummikins if flogging's too kind, Kenway.

speaker: Flint
en: What I miss the most is the fox hunt. Of course, there's plenty of other game to be found. One needs only be creative. I like mine with teeth. The chase is more fun when the prey bites back. Of course it's not the same here as home in England, but there's a wild quality I've come to enjoy.

speaker: Rhona
en: I'll distract him. You circle around for the kill.

speaker: Rhona
en: Hey Flint! Hah! Not much of a shot, are you, Flint?

speaker: Flint
en: You should know, Dinsmore.

speaker: Rhona
en: I should, after studying you for so long.

speaker: Flint
en: Then you finally admit your obsession with me!

speaker: Rhona
en: And how many men have you sent after me, just this week, Flint?

speaker: Flint
en: What did you expect? That I would come in person? You overestimate your importance.

speaker: Rhona
en: You're a pig, Flint.

speaker: Flint
en: Oh... don't be stroppy, Dinsmore.

speaker: Rhona
en: Oh, don't be such a beard splitter.

speaker: Flint
en: Is that what you tell all the lads at the punch house?

speaker: Rhona
en: I would, but you always beat me to it.

speaker: Flint
en: Ape leader.

speaker: Rhona
en: Dandy prat.

speaker: Flint
en: Addle-plot.

speaker: Rhona
en: Catch-fart.

speaker: Flint
en: Stop! I'm blushing.

speaker: Rhona
en: Oh, you make me ill. Catch me if you can! Over here! Ha! Missed again! Who trained you? And you call yourself a gunner. You couldn't hit the broad side of a barn.

speaker: Flint
en: I knew we would end in fire, but I always thought our positions would be reversed. I should have died happier, knowing there was one less Assassin in the world. What a pity, we could never fight together on the correct side of things.

speaker: Edward
en: Would, uh... you two, like a moment alone?

speaker: Rhona
en: No. It's too late.

speaker: Rhona
en: Take it. His charm's all used up. Let the memory of him be locked away for good.

speaker: Tavern Keeper
en: The men do sorely lack a Place to do their Wenching and Debauching. With a little coin-ed 'couragement, I'd have the old Place Bristol fashion! An' a flow o' rum fit to 'bliterate a good Tar proper like.

speaker: Harbourmaster
en: I be needin' Coin to set up the Shipyard Cap'n. The faster I have the needful Gold, the sooner our Ships will rule the Waves!

speaker: Shopkeeper
en: I'll not play Duck and Drake with ye Cap'n, I need Coin to build a little Emporium. I'd be ever obliged... and a local Shop would bring in many a useful Ware for you as Repayment.

speaker: Retired harpooner
en: I got a Proposal for you, Cap'n. Help rebuild this here Wharf so my Boys can get back to fishing. In return, we'll provide Fish to your Crew. Heck, we find anything useful in our Nets, we'll give ye that too. Whaddya say, Cap'n?

speaker: Treasure Dealer
en: Captain Kenway! If you seek Treasure, I can help.

speaker: Brothel Keeper
en: A good Capitaine, he takes care of his Men, yes? The Sailors are un peu dissatisfied that there are no Women of comfort here. I know just where to find them, but we need to build them a Home.

speaker: Drunken master
en: Been thinking Cap'n, why not build ourselves a grand old Bonfire by the Beach? The Lads'd be o'better Cheer if they had such a Spot to let loose, ye savvy?

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: This still doesn't quite feel like home...

speaker: Edward
en: It's still missing a little something...

speaker: Edward
en: Now what could I add to make it perfect...

speaker: Edward
en: I did it. I turned this place into a home. I wonder what Caroline would think of it...

speaker: Edward
en: Bernard!

speaker: Bernard Woodhouse
en: Marveling at the result of your work, Captain Kenway?

speaker: Edward
en: Making Tally of what this Compound has cost me so far.

speaker: Bernard
en: Great Inagua is whole again, made so by your Hand, Captain Kenway.

speaker: Edward
en: I did it so that I might return to a Place that isn't rife with Disease and Misery. Still, it feels good to have a hand in all this.

speaker: Bernard
en: I'll leave you to your Thoughts, Captain Kenway. I think I hear the Passion Flowers calling me. Goodbye.

speaker: Vane
en: So this is the new Libertalia, eh? Stinks the same as every other squat I've robbed this past year.

speaker: Rackham
en: Oy! Why the long face? You falling in love?

speaker: Edward
en: With your blouse. You're welcome to Nassau, gents. Everyone is that does their fair share.

speaker: Vane
en: Fair share? What is this, a fucking monastery?

speaker: Rackham
en: We was lead to believe Nassau was a place where men did as they pleased.

speaker: Thatch
en: Save keeping others from doing the same, aye.

speaker: Vane
en: Captain Thatch, as I live and breathe. And what is this magnificent muzzle you've cultivated?

speaker: Thatch
en: Why fly a black flag when a black beard will do? What brings you two gents this far north?

speaker: Vane
en: The word is the Cuban governor himself is fixing to receive a mess of gold from a nearby fort. Until then, it's just sitting there, itching to be took.

speaker: Edward
en: Governor Torres himself, eh? Sounds promising.

speaker: Thatch
en: Welcome to Nassau, Captain Vane. Mister Rackham.

speaker: Rackham
en: Now, where... Where can a man find a bit of ruff. D'ya know what I mean?

speaker: Edward
en: So what'll you do with your share of the gold we take from governor Torres? Return to Africa? Prince among men?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I cannot return to a place I have never been. I was born in Trinidad, a slave from my first breath.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah. But wouldn't you feel... I don't know... More welcome there?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: As you might feel more welcome in (Paris)?

speaker: Edward
en: Fair point.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: With this skin and this voice, where can I go in the world and feel at ease? This country here is my best chance. This country called Jackdaw, where I know the names of all citizens, and they know mine, and we work together. Not always out of love, but to keep our country afloat.

speaker: Edward
en: I think I understand ye. Let's take her, then. For the citizens of Jackdaw!

speaker: Edward
en: Well hello, your Excellency. I'd got word you might be here.

speaker: Torres
en: I know your face, pirate. But your name was borrowed the last time we spoke.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah, yes. I recall... Mister Duncan Walpole, I miss that one. So... What's a Templar Grand Master doing so far from his Castillo?

speaker: Torres
en: I'd rather not say.

speaker: Edward
en: And I'd rather not cut your lips off and feed 'em to you.

speaker: Torres
en: Two years ago we offered a reward for the Sage's recapture. Today someone claims to have found him. This gold is his ransom.

speaker: Edward
en: Who found him?

speaker: Torres
en: A slaver by the name of Laurens Prins. He lives in Kingston.

speaker: Edward
en: We like this story, Torres. And we want to help you finish it. But we're going to do it our way. Using you and your gold.

speaker: Edward
en: I know my targets by sight well enough. But how will I find them?

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: We have spies and informants in every city. Visit our bureaus, and the Assassins there will guide you.

speaker: Edward
en: That fixes Torres and Rogers... but Bartholomew Roberts won't be near any city. Might take months to find him.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Or years. But you are a man of talent and quality, captain Kenway. I believe you will find him.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: And if you're at a loss, do not be afraid to call on your quartermaster for aid.

speaker: Edward
en: Quartermaster. What's our present course?

speaker: Anne
en: Due west, captain. If it's still Kingston we're sailing for.

speaker: Edward
en: It is indeed, Miss Bonny. Call it out.

speaker: Anne
en: Weigh anchor and let fall the courses, lads! We're sailing for Jamaica!

speaker: Edward
en: How does it feel to bark so loud?

speaker: Anne
en: I've barked louder, and to men twice as rough.

speaker: Edward
en: Tending bar at the Old Avery, you mean?

speaker: Anne
en: Among other places. And I sailed with Mary and Rackham for a time, remember?

speaker: Edward
en: Of course.

speaker: Anne
en: Mary did most of the captaining. Jack did most of the drinking.

speaker: Edward
en: Did Mary... did she ever tell you who it was that fathered her child?

speaker: Anne
en: It was a young fella. Sailed with us on that last voyage. Poor lad was killed fighting beside us. The only man not too drunk to stand up for himself.

speaker: Edward
en: There was so much about her I didn't know. I called her a friend. But was I one in return?

speaker: Anne
en: She thought the world of you, Edward. Have no worries about that.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, that's good to hear.

speaker: Antó
en: Captain Kenway.

speaker: Edward
en: You have something for me?

speaker: Antó
en: The present whereabouts of the Templar Woodes Rogers. He's attending a small political function, so do it clean.

speaker: Edward
en: The word is King George is calling Rogers back to London.

speaker: Antó
en: Aye, not happy with his progress in Nassau.

speaker: Anne
en: Still too many pirates roaming about, from what I hear.

speaker: Antó
en: You'll need a disguise to fool the powderheads at this party. I suggest the visiting diplomat, Ruggiero Ferraro. He's been on our lists for some time.

speaker: Edward
en: Understood. Will you send this to England for me?

speaker: Antó
en: Aye. A ship leaves tomorrow.

speaker: Edward
en: Caroline Scott-Kenway. Hawkin's Lane, Bristol.

speaker: Ruggiero
en: Stop pestering me, English dogs! Are you my escorts or my captors! We'll go when I'm damned good and ready! Va bene (Very well) I am ready. We go. There is no beauty to this city. No expression of joy. No aesthetic plan! Ugh. You walk your streets like animals! Like cattle with no sense of decorum! Idiots! You're all idiots! How you English believe you can subdue the world is beyond me! Ah! Praise God for imported wines. Who can drink rum more than once a month? (My God)! It is revolting. Bastardo! (Bastard!) Now I am lost! How preposterous this city is! All straight lines and rigid blocks, and still no sense of order! Oh, how I miss the warm and winding streets of Firenze. How I miss culture! Damn this sweltering heat. Another quaff, I think. Ah! That hits the right note. Mm... , the finest grape in the world. Ah ha! Hide your liquor and lock away your women! Ruggiero Ferraro is here, and he means to make a damned fool of himself!

speaker: Edward
en: Salve. (Hello.) Forgive the lateness of my arrival. I am Ruggiero Ferraro.

speaker: Soldier
en: Aye, Mister Ferraro. Not a problem.

speaker: Lady 1
en: You are mister Ferraro, I take it? I do adore your frippery. Such elegance and colour.

speaker: Edward
en: I should say the same of you. So beautiful.

speaker: Man 1
en: I say, that's a smart looking outfit. But it can't be comfortable in this heat.

speaker: Edward
en: Si, (Yes,) but for men of good taste as ourselves, form must always take precedence over function. Good day, friends. Carry on. Pardon. Another engagement commands my attention. Let us continue this at another time. Excuse me.

speaker: Rogers
en: Ladies and gentlemen, a toast to my brief tenure as governor of the Bahamas! For, under my watch, no less than three-hundred avowed pirates took the King's Pardon and swore fealty to the crown! And yet, for all my successes, his Majesty has seen fit to sack me! And call me home to England. Brilliant! God bless the fucker! Therefore, hooray! Hooray for the ignoble and ignorant prigs who rule the world with sticks up their arses! Hooray!

speaker: Rogers
en: Thank you for hosting my little send-off, Simpkins. I haven't been too rambunctious, have I?

speaker: Simpkins
en: A little free with your speech today, but nothing to be hanged for.

speaker: Rogers
en: Why, then how's this: soon all the monarchies of the world will be obsolete. And when that day comes, men like Torres and myself will reveal ourselves as the architects of their undoing.

speaker: Simpkins
en: Oh, Christ, Rogers. You're a bold one.

speaker: Rogers
en: I brought those brutes in Nassau to heel, by God. And this is the thanks I get? Unbelievable.

speaker: Man 2
en: Damned right, you did, Rogers! And if it's a character witness you need back home, I'd gladly tender a letter in support.

speaker: Lady 2
en: Any regrets, captain Rogers? Any business left unfinished?

speaker: Rogers
en: Yes. That I paid for Nassau's restoration with my own money. Fully three-fourths of the improvements made to that bloody island, I funded by my fortune. And if that doesn't spell out my commitment, then the King is a fool.

speaker: Man 3
en: Damn shame about your dismissal, Rogers. You had my confidence. Still do!

speaker: Rogers
en: Well, it's not a done deal, by any means. When the King hears my complaints, I'm sure he'll come to a more sensible conclusion.

speaker: Man 4
en: Word going around, Rogers, is that you're comfortable friends with the Spaniard, Laureano Torres. Is that true?

speaker: Rogers
en: It is, I am proud to say. Torres was a governor too and, like me, had a firm commitment to seeing justice done.

speaker: Lady 3
en: And how is Missus Rogers these days?

speaker: Rogers
en: I haven't the faintest idea, and I don't intend to inquire any further. We separated almost five years ago, and both our lives have been the better for it.

speaker: Lady 3
en: Forgive my curiosity, governor.

speaker: Rogers
en: Perhaps I'll be more candid later, when the remainder of my reason has left me. I'm confident I can sway the King back to my position. When he sees the efforts I have made on his behalf. Give my thanks to the host, will you? This is as fitting a send-off as any man could hope for. Is this the only wine available? Nothing from France? Wonderful weather we're having here. I almost prefer it to New Providence. Common men of genius and wit so rarely see their efforts rewarded. I hope to change this one day.

speaker: Edward
en: You was a privateer once. How is it you lack so much respect for sailors only trying to make their way in this world?

speaker: Rogers
en: You couldn't possibly understand my motives, cretin! You, who've spent a whole lifetime dismantling everything that makes our civilization shine.

speaker: Edward
en: But I do understand. I've seen the Observatory, and I know its power. You'd use that device to spy and blackmail and sabotage.

speaker: Rogers
en: Yes, and yet all for a greater purpose. To ensure justice. To snuff out lies and to seek truth.

speaker: Edward
en: There's no man on Earth who needs that power.

speaker: Rogers
en: Yet you suffer the outlaw Roberts to use it!

speaker: Edward
en: No. I'm taking it back. And if you tell me where he is, I'll stop the man.

speaker: Rogers
en: Here at the edge of a blade, I find a friend in you at last! Príncipe, you mad bastard. Our best sources say Príncipe...

speaker: Man 5
en: That man there! The Italian! He did it!

speaker: Lady 4
en: What's happened? Is captain Rogers hurt? Is it a revolt? What's happened?

speaker: Edward
en: It's done.

speaker: Anne
en: Where now?

speaker: Edward
en: Grab your kit and pack well. We're sailing for Africa.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I've heard it said our commander calls Captain Woodes Rogers a friend as well.

speaker: Guard 2
en: The man who rescued ? That Captain Rogers?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Aye. A sailor to his bones. And he's a hard man, he is. Earned a large scar down his left cheek after taking a pellet to the face. Lodged in his palate for a couple days.

speaker: Guard 2
en: By Christ! And the man lived?

speaker: Guard 1
en: Aye. Broke to stride, in fact, and continued barking orders until the next morning when he took a splinter to the heel. That took him off his feet for a day.

speaker: Guard 2
en: And this is a living, breathing man we're talking about?

speaker: Guard 1
en: He's a man of many talents and incredible charisma. I only wish he was enlisted so that I could serve under him.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Isn't that the truth. Pass the bottle, will you?

speaker: Vane
en: Look at them turncoats. Makes me bloody ill to think how many times I put up with Hornigold and his self-righteous shite.

speaker: Rogers
en: Verily, you are a man of principle, Captain Hornigold. A man I believe I can trust with my best ideas.

speaker: Edward
en: Faith, and we'll survive this, Charles. With our pride intact.

speaker: Vane
en: Well, that's confidence. You brewed a plan I might get a taste of?

speaker: Edward
en: Nassau is over, that's plain to see. I say we skip out tonight, and regroup at my compound.

speaker: Vane
en: Fair enough. What's your angle?

speaker: Edward
en: The Brits have brought their supplies ashore, see? If we nick some gunpowder and pine pitch, we can build a fire ship and send it straight at the blockade, blasting it to smithereens.

speaker: Vane
en: Aye. We'll use Rackham's ship. He ain't a capable captain.

speaker: Edward
en: My conscience is clear.

speaker: Vane
en: Right. While you get up the gunpowder, I'll secure the pine pitch.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Father... did you always know how to sail a boat?

speaker: Edward
en: The Jackdaw is a ship, Jenny. Not a boat.

speaker: Jennifer
en: But did you always know?

speaker: Edward
en: No. No, I learned after leaving Bristol.

speaker: Jennifer
en: After you left mother?

speaker: Edward
en: Well, I didn't leave your... I didn't leave without saying goodbye, that is. It was an arrangement, you see? Between your mother and me.

speaker: Jennifer
en: She said you left her. She said you always talked about sailing a boat and making money in the New World.

speaker: Edward
en: I did always want to sail a ship, that's true. But not for a lark. To support us. To take care of her... and you.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Not me. Mother said you didn't know about me. She said you wrote only once a year, and that she never knew where to find you.

speaker: Edward
en: That's all true. And I'm sorry for that. If I had known earlier... I don't know. I might have come home. I hope that I would have.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Well... you were busy. That's what I think.

speaker: Edward
en: I was. But... that wouldn't have mattered.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Can I steer your boat?

speaker: Edward
en: Boat? I see no boat here. Do you?

speaker: Jennifer
en: Ugh. I mean ship, obviously. I don't see the difference anyway.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah! It's a very simple one, Jenny. A ship can carry a boat, but a boat cannot carry a ship.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Why, then everything is a ship, large and small, but for my toy boat. The one I take into the bath with me.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a clever way of seeing it. Is it hard to talk about Caroline, Jenny? About your mother?

speaker: Jennifer
en: Hmmm... no. She passed some years ago. I miss her, but it's all right.

speaker: Edward
en: Was she in pain?

speaker: Jennifer
en: I don't know. I don't think so. She was very happy for quite some time. Then not so happy. I didn't see her much after that. Then she was gone.

speaker: Edward
en: I... I'm sorry. I'm sorry I wasn't there for you.

speaker: Jennifer
en: It's all right. You're here now. And we're on an adventure!

speaker: Edward
en: Only a little one, I hope. I can't handle too many more surprises.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Do you think we'll see a whale?

speaker: Edward
en: Yes. There's a very good chance.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Hm! And what about pirates? Will I see pirates?

speaker: Edward
en: No. There's not much chance of that, I think.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Oh. That's rather sad. I should have liked to have seen one.

speaker: Edward
en: Tell you what, Jenny. As soon as these winds die a little bit, I'll let you steer the Jackdaw. One little trick at the helm before sundown.

speaker: Jennifer
en: Yay!

speaker: Suitor
en: Miss Jennifer Kenway. May I introduce myself...

speaker: Jennifer
en: Jennifer Scott, if you please.

speaker: Suitor
en: I'm sorry. I- I...

speaker: Edward
en: My daughter was raised by her mother, Caroline, until she passed away some years ago. Jenny prefers to use her surname to mine.

speaker: Suitor
en: Ah. Forgive my ignorance.

speaker: Edward
en: I will. She may not.

speaker: Haytham
en: Father, help me!

speaker: Edward
en: This little rascal, however, IS a Kenway. What's wrong, Haytham?

speaker: Haytham
en: I can't see the stage!

speaker: Edward
en: Up we go. How's that?

speaker: Haytham
en: Fine. But won't your arms tire?

speaker: Edward
en: Hey, I'm not so old as that! But if they do, then we shall quit this posh gig and go and meet your mother for some chocolate at . How's that sound?

speaker: Haytham
en: Yes, please!

speaker: Edward
en: Ok. Hush now...

speaker: Hunter Gatherer
