en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate
en: Captain! We got Word the Shipwright found Maynard's Treasurer. She's awaiting us at Nassau.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Nassau. Redcoats everywhere.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: Captain! You took your time. I'm drunk.

speaker: Lucy
en: We were right. Maynard does have a Treasurer, and he's had the Cojones (balls) to show up at Nassau.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: It burns me to see the Place like this, swarming with Redcoats.

speaker: Lucy
en: As you see, Maynard's recruiting. His Big Wig's here offering Gold to all who join him.

speaker: Edward
en: It's not a bad Likeness.

speaker: Lucy
en: I wager he's paying more than you. I might sign up myself.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll go and find this Treasurer before you do. Meet back at the Jackdaw when you're done drinking.

speaker: Lucy
en: Maybe one more, then.

speaker: Treasurer
en: The Captain barely even takes to Sea. He's soft, and likes the Comforts of his Lodgings too well. Who took Blackbeard? It wasn't the Captain, as we all know. It was Lieutenant Maynard, and he did it alone. Think on that. And while you do, consider that the Lieutenant is generous to those who serve him.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh, this is good! Maynard's moved his Warchest. Back to the Jackdaw.

speaker: Edward
en: The Treasurer was uncooperative, but he carried a Letter from Maynard. It mentions a Villa he keeps at the... Beckford Estate.

speaker: Lucy
en: I know it. That's at Tortuga. I went there once with Grandad. Nice. It's not Black Island, mind...

speaker: Edward
en: He's moved his Warchest there, and he's gone somewhere else. It's unguarded.

speaker: Lucy
en: Our Quartermaster's not going to like this.

speaker: Edward
en: Mum's the Word, then. She'll come around when she sees the Gold.

speaker: Lucy
en: I might not have to join Maynard to get Paid after all.

speaker: Edward
en: My Master-at-Arms will be waiting at Santanillas.

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: Cannons upgraded. Them fire not once, but twice.

speaker: Edward
en: I see your Renown is earned! Do you never sleep, Smith?

speaker: Tobias
en: My long sleep is coming.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Abel Galvão
en: We must be swift or they will slip away.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: Forgive me, Father.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: We could dock over there.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward Kenway
en: What is it, Galvão?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: I have a lead on Du Casse's men. Their new Leader has them holed up in Cape Bonavista. We should strike now.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: New Leader, you say? I know the Place.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: The Scoundrels will flee an honest Fight. While you hunt them down, I'll come from behind and block any escape.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: A fine Plan, but I'll be doing most of the hunting. Are you sure?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: These Men are Cowards. I'll have my chance with the Runners.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: Edward, I'll meet you inland.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Aye, watch yourself now.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Mostly empty. Not much has changed here.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 1
en: Did you ever imagine that we'd be the ones doing the hanging? I'd sooner stick to smuggling.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 2
en: I'll do whatever the Boss wants. He pays us a damn sight more than Du Casse ever did.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 3
en: Keep it down. You're scaring off the Animals.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 4
en: Oi! Kill him.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Many have tried.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: I wonder how the Padre's getting along.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: Captain, over here.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Is that all of them?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: There's more inside the Cave. No Mercy.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Step softly now. Don't want to alert them.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: If they run, I'll chase them to the Gates of Hell.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 5
en: First, the Bishop has us killing Villagers. Now, it's back to smuggling Guns. I'm confused.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 6
en: What's there to understand? We sap his Coin 'til it runs dry. Then find us another .

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 5
en: It just don't sit right with me. A Man like him, don't they take Vows of Poverty?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 6
en: Aye, Vows of Celibacy too. That's why I never joined 'em.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Let's see if anything here points to their new Leader.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: A Letter from Bishop Ravenscroft. Shite. It was the Bishop who ordered the Attack.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: That Bastard. I should have seen it... but I couldn't let myself imagine he could be so Evil.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: These are Du Casse's Guns.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: Perhaps. But that Mark is the Bishop's.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: This Wine doesn't come cheap.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: It's from the Bishop's Cellar. Bears his Stamp.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: One moment.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: And if thy right Hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 7
en: No more.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: The Bishop ordered you to kill my People. Why?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Pirate 7
en: I don't know. Please...

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: You would beg for Mercy?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: He's had enough, Man. Look.

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Edward
en: Now, who is this Bishop?

scene: If Thy Right Hand Offend Thee
speaker: Galvão
en: My Mentor. Two Years ago he tried to build a Cathedral in Kingston. The there refused it. Things turned bloody. The Bishop lost his mind. He said we had a Catholic duty to go to War over it. It was madness. I refused. He saw it as . I hid my People, and tried to protect them. I never imagined the Bishop would murder them! He will die for what he has done. We must make for Kingston, and cut the Head off this Snake.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Stealing a fishing schooner single handed? Damned canny, captain.

speaker: Edward
en: As is taking back my brig from this pillock. Once again, I thank you both.

speaker: Kidd
en: This billy-huff didn't last two months with your ship before he came limping back to Nassau. Took the pardon straight away.

speaker: Rackham
en: I had to, lads! That Rogers was on to me from the first.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Hold your tongue, Rackham!

speaker: Kidd
en: So what now? Still chasing your elusive fortune?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. And I'm close. I've heard the Sage is sailing out of Kingston on a ship called the Princess.

speaker: Kidd
en: Put your ambition to better use, Kenway. Find the Sage with US.

speaker: Edward
en: I've no stomach for you and your mystics, Mary. I want a taste of the good life. An easy life.

speaker: Kidd
en: No one honest has an easy life, Edward. And it's aching for one that causes the most pain. All right, Rackham. Back to retirement.

speaker: Edward
en: What news Adé?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: This bahjohn works for the Royal African Company. Tell him what you told me.

speaker: Slaver
en: I haven't seen the Princess for eight weeks or more. Meaning she may soon be back.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What else?

speaker: Slaver
en: I thought this buck belonged to the other men who was asking about the Princess this morning so I told him that

speaker: Edward
en: What other men?

speaker: Slaver
en: Haughty sailor in plain rags. And a gent with a scar just here.

speaker: Edward
en: Where have they got to?

speaker: Slaver
en: Staying just 'round the corner, they said.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I grow tired of chasing these fantasies of yours, Edward. As does the crew.

speaker: Edward
en: Hang in there, man. We're getting close.

speaker: Rogers
en: Have you alerted the men? We're short on time.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Aye, there'll be two soldiers waiting for us at the crossroads.

speaker: Rogers
en: Very good.

speaker: Hornigold
en: If you don't mind me asking, Sir. What's the meaning behind these blood samples we're taking?

speaker: Rogers
en: Torres tells me that blood is required for the Observatory to properly function.

speaker: Hornigold
en: How do you mean, sir?

speaker: Rogers
en: If one wishes to use the Observatory to, say... spy on King George, then one would require a drop of the king's blood to do so. In other words, a small sample of blood gives us access to a man's everyday life.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Does Torres mean to spy on me then? For I've just given him a sample of my blood.

speaker: Rogers
en: As have I, Captain Hornigold. As will all Templars. It is a measure of insurance.

speaker: Hornigold
en: And trust, I reckon.

speaker: Rogers
en: Yes, but fear not. Torres has shipped our samples to a Templar safehouse in Rio de Janeiro. We will not be the Observatory's first objects, I assure you.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Aye, sir. I suppose it's a small price to pay for what the Templars have given me in return.

speaker: Rogers
en: Precisely.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Governor, when you hunted pirates in Madagascar, what methods worked best?

speaker: Rogers
en: I believe it was my charisma that persuaded them. Violence and threats should always be a last resort. In Madagascar, I offered those pirates a choice... take a pardon and return to England penniless but free men, or be hanged by the neck until dead.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Just as you did in Nassau.

speaker: Rogers
en: Precisely. A pity Commodore Chamberlaine did not live to see my thorough success.

speaker: Hornigold
en: It's not like you to gloat, Rogers.

speaker: Rogers
en: We all deserve a moment, don't we?

speaker: Rogers
en: Grand Master! Welcome.

speaker: Torres
en: What have you learned?

speaker: Rogers
en: The Princess was taken by pirates six weeks ago. And so far as we know, the Sage Roberts was still aboard.

speaker: Torres
en: Very good. It is something, no? And what measures are we taking to recover the Princess from these pirates?

speaker: Rogers
en: Captain Hornigold has dispatched some of his best men to ensure the Sage's capture.

speaker: Torres
en: Hm. What of the Sage's present location. Do we know?

speaker: Rogers
en: Africa, your excellency.

speaker: Torres
en: Africa? By God, the winds do not favor that route.

speaker: Rogers
en: I concur, Grand Master. I should have sailed there myself. One of my slave galleys would be more than capable of making a swift journey.

speaker: Torres
en: Slave Galley? Captain, I asked you to divest yourself of that sick institution.

speaker: Rogers
en: I fail to see the difference between enslaving some men and all men. Our aim is to steer the entire course of civilization, is it not?

speaker: Torres
en: A body enslaved inspires the mind to revolt. But enslave a man's mind, and his body will follow on naturally. Efficiently.

speaker: Rogers
en: A fair point, Grand Master.

speaker: Torres
en: Eh, remind me... where in Africa are we looking?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Príncipe, Sir. A small island.

speaker: Rogers
en: We've sent two of our best men. Burgess and Cockram. Privateers with fast ships and firm hearts.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Edward Kenway! Imagine my surprise at seeing your Jackdaw anchored there. Have you heard all you came to hear? Will you now go rescue the Sage from our clutching hands?

speaker: Edward
en: A pox on you, traitor! You sold us down river!

speaker: Hornigold
en: Because I found a better path! The Templars know order. Discipline. Structure. But you never could fathom these subtleties. Goodbye, old friend! You were a soldier once! When you fought for something real. Something beyond yourself!

speaker: Guard 1
en: (Aye. Some nights, I can barely sleep for imagining all them down there in the inky depths. Gripping their prey in their tentacles, slowly digesting whole ships, crew and all...)

speaker: Agent
en: (I sent over a cart of and they thought nothing of it. Mark my words, they will be plenty drunk before long. Then, we attack. All we need do is bide our time, and the fort will easily return to our control.)

speaker: Anne Bonny
en: I never tire of the Sight of this Place.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Aye. The one the Crew are calling Deadman is still alive at least. Some time on our Island might agree with him.

speaker: Anne
en: I don't care for that Nickname.

speaker: Edward
en: When he's able to tell me, I'll get his proper Name and his Story.

speaker: Anne
en: This is nice. It's good to see the Crew at Ease. I expect there'll be precious little of it ahead.

speaker: Edward
en: If that poor Sod's correct and Maynard's building an Armada, I'd wager you're right.

speaker: Anne
en: We've a brave Crew, but we don't stand a chance against an entire Armada. I'll put Word out. When we know where Maynard is, we take him before he has the Advantage.

speaker: Edward
en: I'd like to know more of his Purpose first, find out what he's planning.

speaker: Anne
en: You don't fool me, Edward Kenway. You want to figure out a way to get your Hands on his Gold.

speaker: Edward
en: And why not? We can deal with the Bastard, Rob him Blind and make ourselves rich at the same time. Thatch would approve.

speaker: Anne
en: Oh, that's sly! Thatch indeed! I'll tell you why not. The longer we take, the more dangerous Maynard becomes.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm afraid you speak Truth, Anne. Let me talk to my Officers.

speaker: Anne
en: Don't take too long.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: Captain! I could use your aid in carrying this Rum. The Crew has the thirst of Whales, and they're not the most patient Lot.

speaker: Edward
en: You should take it to the Men yourself. There are few things that earn their Respect more than Rum.

speaker: Galvão
en: Respect is for the Captain. Fear better suits a Master-at-Arms. But I'm glad for your help. I had a terrible weakness for Rum once. I won't be partaking myself.

speaker: Edward
en: Devil take me, you're a Pirate man!

speaker: Edward
en: The man we pulled out of that Box was being pressed into Crew by Maynard. He's building an Armada.

speaker: Galvão
en: If true, that is not good News, Captain. We won't survive against an Armada. Few could.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. I was hoping my Master-at-Arms might have some thoughts about what we could do about it.

speaker: Galvão
en: I may. Let me think on it.

speaker: Galvão
en: My thanks for your help, Captain. Just here will do. The men will find it.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 1
en: I'm weary of chasing our Tails across the Seas, looking for a Fight that could be our last.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 2
en: I don't mind if there's pay at the end of it. But it's been too long, that's certain.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 1
en: The Captain and Quartermaster are to blame. Blackbeard's gone. Finding this Lieutenant Maynard won't bring him back.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 2
en: Aye. If they want revenge, take as many fat Merchant ships as we can, I say. That's what Blackbeard would want.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 1
en: Leave off Lads! It's the Master at Arms.

speaker: Galvão
en: No no! Don't stop on my Account! If you want to fight, fight us! What say you, Captain? Care to test your Grit against your own Men?

speaker: Edward
en: Let's just try not to damage them permanently. We need them able.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 2
en: You heard the Captain, Lads! No permanent Damage. That don't mean we can't make 'em hurt!

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 3
en: Oh, that don't look Good! Get one back! Put your shoulders into it!

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 3
en: They can't take all of us!

speaker: Edward
en: Pull your Weight, Master at Arms! You've got me doing all the Work.

speaker: Galvão
en: Keep up the Talk, Captain. I'll let my Fists speak for me.

speaker: Edward
en: Looks an even Fight now. I can finish it if you're winded.

speaker: Galvão
en: If it's all the same to you, I'll see it through.

speaker: Galvão
en: Nice Hook, Captain!

speaker: Edward
en: It's the Jab that does the real work!

speaker: Galvão
en: A good Contest, and an agreeable End! My thanks for your help, Captain.

speaker: Edward
en: You're a cheeky Sod.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: Get up you Swabs! Let's see which of you can shoot to save yourselves. What about you, Captain? Think you can best me?

speaker: Lucy
en: Walk with me, Captain.

speaker: Edward
en: Where to, Shipwright?

speaker: Lucy
en: You'll see.

speaker: Edward
en: The Crew is calling the one we pulled out of that Box "Deadman". They say he's likely an uncommon Criminal.

speaker: Lucy
en: The same could be said of any of us, and has been at every Establishment I've visited... or the ones I remember.

speaker: Edward
en: Some are afraid he's afflicted with a spreading Sickness, a Plague.

speaker: Lucy
en: I say the only Sickness lies with those who locked him in that damned Box.

speaker: Edward
en: What have we here?

speaker: Lucy
en: The Rules are easy. I call out a group of Dummies. You hit the ones I call. You keep doing that 'til I stop. Got it? Let's start.

speaker: Lucy
en: Middle!

speaker: Edward
en: Deadman's said Maynard was pressing him into service for an Armada he's building.

speaker: Lucy
en: An Armada? Christ! He'd need a lot of coin for that.

speaker: Edward
en: A thought that's crossed my Mind as well.

speaker: Lucy
en: Left!

speaker: Lucy
en: If Maynard's got that kind of Coin, there'll be a Big Wig with a Ledger close behind him. There always is.

speaker: Lucy
en: Right!

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. If I find this Treasurer, I might find his Gold. Maynard can't build an Armada if he can't pay for it.

speaker: Lucy
en: Find Maynard's Gold to stop the Armada. Right.

speaker: Lucy
en: Just the kind of shooting that might win you the Competition.

speaker: Lucy
en: Speaking of the Deadman, last I saw he was heading to the Beach, and didn't look well.

speaker: Tobias "Deadman" Smith
en: I'm here.

speaker: Edward
en: Is that Hole for someone you know?

speaker: Tobias
en: The Grave is for me.

speaker: Edward
en: Come now. It looks as if our Island is doing you some Good.

speaker: Tobias
en: Appearance only. My Wounds won't be cured. I will be dead soon.

speaker: Edward
en: You say you are dying, I say we all chance Death at every Turn. I'm in need of a Master Gunner with your Skill. Join us, for as little or as long as may be. You might live longer than you expect.

speaker: Tobias
en: That is True.

speaker: Edward
en: But I should know your real Name. I can't have my Master Gunner answering to "Deadman".

speaker: Tobias
en: Tobias. My Name was Tobias Smith.

speaker: Edward
en: Smith, then. Now let's get back to the others. I do not share your fondness for... Graves.

speaker: Galvão
en: Hear me, all! Gather round!

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 4
en: Let's hear a word from our Captain!

speaker: Edward
en: You all know our Purpose is to find Maynard, and relieve him of both Life and Fortune.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 5
en: Sack the Bastard!

speaker: Edward
en: He is canny, and our Task is neither simple nor easy. But we have his Measure. Maynard's building an Armada against us. That takes a lot of Coin. If we find the one who keeps his Ledger, we can stop his Gold. Shipwright, here's your Chance to even the Score with the Lobcock for locking you up. Search out this Treasurer. Send Word when you find him.

speaker: Lucy
en: I'll get him.

speaker: Edward
en: To our Master-at-Arms falls the Task of the Armada itself, a Problem for which I confess I have no Answer.

speaker: Galvão
en: To this I have already given some Thought. I ask your leave to go to my old Spanish Crew at Santanillas, and gain their Aid.

speaker: Edward
en: You have it. Only be sure of their good Faith. In looking for Friends, we don't want to increase our Enemies. Last, I am happy to tell you that the good repair of the Armaments rests with our new Master Gunner, Mister Smith. I am assured he is well suited to the Task. We can but take him at his Word, and prove him, false or true. With that, I declare the Jackdaw and her Crew ready. What say you, Quartermaster?

speaker: Anne
en: It's a Start. And a good one! So say I!

speaker: Bernard Woodhouse
en: You Lot behave yourselves. It took me all Day to get this Place tidy for your Celebrations. There's no need to undo it with Tomfoolery.

speaker: Jackdaw Pirate British 01 Male
en: I don't know about that Padre. A Pirate Ship's no Place for a Man of the Cloth, if you ask me.

speaker: Jackdaw Pirate British 02 Male
en: Padre... he's no more a Man of God than I'm Lord of the Manor.

speaker: Jackdaw Pirate British 03 Male
en: The new Shipwright's out there calling all and sundry to match her at skill with Pistols.

speaker: Jackdaw Pirate British 01 Male
en: She's got Guts, that one. Aye, that's the Kind of Woman you want standing beside you in a Scrap.

speaker: Jackdaw Pirate British 03 Male
en: Hey! You know the Code as well as me. She's one of us, and that's it. No funny Business.

speaker: Jackdaw Pirate British 01 Male
en: I never said any different, did I?

speaker: Galvão
en: Jump in Lads, if you dare! There's only the Two of us!

scene: A Last Drink for the Road
speaker: Businessman 1
en: (Then again, if old Tom keeps paying, what's to stop them coming after all of us?)

scene: A Last Drink for the Road
speaker: Arispe
en: (All I ask is a reasonable royalty. Sixty percent should suffice.)

scene: A Last Drink for the Road
speaker: Tom
en: (It's too high! I must maintain my business if my children are to eat.)

scene: A Last Drink for the Road
speaker: Arispe
en: (If you mean to keep your children and your business you'll pay. Now.)

speaker: Torres
en: Come to kill an old man, have you ?

speaker: Edward
en: The threat posed by a man like you isn't restrained by age.

speaker: Torres
en: How thought provoking! I didn't know the Assassins were recruiting philosophers.

speaker: Edward
en: My philosophy has been shaped by you and your associates.

speaker: Torres
en: Strange. All I've seen is an excess of murder.

speaker: Edward
en: I prefer to call it conviction.

speaker: Torres
en: You speak of conviction. My conviction would have saved these people! None would have had to die! And then you tossed that all away.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll do my own saving, if you don't mind.

speaker: Torres
en: A pointless effort. Fine. If you are so hell-bent on violence, then I challenge you to find me.

speaker: Torres
en: You have failed yet again, Kenway. I wonder how long you will persist with this nonsense.

speaker: Edward
en: I will persist until it is done.

speaker: Torres
en: You show such dedication to your murders! It is almost impressive.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. And I'll be back for you as soon as I'm able.

speaker: Edward
en: Anne. A word?

speaker: Anne
en: What is it, Kenway?

speaker: Edward
en: What do you know about this Dutchman, Laurens Prins?

speaker: Anne
en: Enough to know you're wasting your time.

speaker: Edward
en: The man trades in slaves, Anne.

speaker: Anne
en: That's just a rumor and you know it.

speaker: Edward
en: Torres seems to believe it. He was planning to buy Bartholomew Roberts from Prins.

speaker: Anne
en: You've some coin, don't you? Why don't you just buy him like Torres was set to?

speaker: Edward
en: I prefer the direct approach.

speaker: Prins
en: What's this? Didn't expect an old man to still be spry?

speaker: Edward
en: Slippery codger! Just give me Roberts and I'll leave you to be.

speaker: Prins
en: Afraid not. That man's worth quite a bit of coin to me. I wonder; might there be a price on your head, pirate?

speaker: Edward
en: Damn, he's called the guards. I'll be back for you, Prins!

speaker: Prins
en: I recognize you. You're the one who was following that fool Torres.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. And if you'd handed over Roberts then, I wouldn't have had to do this now.

speaker: Prins
en: What do you want with Roberts?

speaker: Edward
en: With the knowledge inside his head, I could become a very wealthy man.

speaker: Prins
en: So it's just coin that drives you?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. It seems so.

speaker: The Law of the Ocean
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah... lively Havana! I've been here once before. It was a truly awe-ful pleasure.

speaker: Edward
en: See someone you know?

speaker: Stede
en: No, no, no. Just putting on a friendly face. I shouldn't want to be mistaken for a pirate again.

speaker: Edward
en: Right. Flash rogue like yourself must be cautious.

speaker: Stede
en: It's mad to think Spain and England were at war two years ago, isn't it? Here I am, bartering with Spaniards like they were my cousins. Something wrong, Duncan?

speaker: Edward
en: No. It's nothing. Sand in my hampers. So where's the best squat in town? I'm dying for a quick kip. Or a siesta, should I say?

speaker: Stede
en: Um... I'm just headed to a ... a public house now to meet some merchants. I could... I could show you the way.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, lead on.

speaker: Stede
en: I hope you'll tarry a bit while I conduct my meeting. It would be a great relief to have a man of your stature nearby. In case of a... misunderstanding.

speaker: Edward
en: I can hang about. I might have a drink.

speaker: Stede
en: Splendid. A drink.

speaker: Stede
en: Gracious! What a revolting sight!

speaker: Edward
en: Well they don't take kindly to pirates here, do they? Wonder how many stolen reales bought these men this perch?

speaker: Edward
en: Hola (Hello) ladies.

speaker: Stede
en: You don't know these women, do you?

speaker: Edward
en: No, they charge money for that kind of privilege. Few dozen reales for every hour of knowing. Keen to meet them?

speaker: Stede
en: No! Goodness no. I am a married man!

speaker: Edward
en: Married men are their forte, mate.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah! Here's a purveyor of personal defences! I should acquire a blade for myself, Duncan. Just as you have.

speaker: Edward
en: This rusty razor's nothing to admire.

speaker: Stede
en: Even so, I appear a mere kitten walking so close upon you. Perhaps a small dagger would suit me. Let's see what he's selling.

speaker: Edward
en: Maybe I'll buy a sword too, we'll both jump rank.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah, we'll be quite the pair, you and I. Twin devils!

speaker: Stede
en: I should acquire a blade for myself, Duncan. Just as you have. Perhaps a small dagger would suit me. Oh, we'll be quite the pair, you and I! Twin devils!

speaker: Edward
en: Maybe I'll buy a sword too, we'll both jump rank.

speaker: Edward
en: Lend us a few reales then. I did save your skin.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah, uh... of course!

speaker: Edward
en: Cheers.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a better fit for me. How'd you fare?

speaker: Stede
en: I had only enough for a small knife, sadly. Still, it'll do in a pinch. Oh, puffer-duff... I have led us astray, Duncan.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh, no matter. I'll get us a better view. What are we looking for?

speaker: Stede
en: Uh, a tavern! With a sort of courtyard interior.

speaker: Stede
en: My goodness, you are an agile chap!

speaker: Edward
en: Every finger's a fishhook! That's how you tell a true sailor.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah ha! Yes. A fine way to put it.

speaker: Edward
en: I think I see the place! We're not far.

speaker: Stede
en: Ahh! Stop!

speaker: Robber
en: Ah! ¡No te resistas, gordinflón! (Stop struggling, fatman!)

speaker: Stede
en: ¡Para! ¡Para! (Stop! Stop!) Oh! He's robbed me blind! Good God, what do I do?

speaker: Edward
en: Hang tight!

speaker: Stede
en: Oh, I can't breathe. I think my heart has stopped.

speaker: Edward
en: Stop or I'll break your knees when I catch you! I'm close at heel, shitbird! Here I come! Don't make me chase you into the harbor!

speaker: Edward
en: You robbed the wrong man, mate. A fellow with dangerous friends.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a heavy purse, Mister Bonnet.

speaker: Stede
en: Duncan, by Jove, you're alive.

speaker: Edward
en: Of course I am. That filch was no fuss.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah, we've arrived.

speaker: Stede
en: Ah! Did you catch that rogue?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. And I'll be buying the first round with the money I pulled off him.

speaker: Stede
en: Oh! Ah... wonderful. First my ship then my purse. It's twice you've saved me now, Duncan.

speaker: Edward
en: Don't forget your skin, I saved that too.

speaker: Stede
en: Thrice then! Very good!

speaker: Civilian
en: Out of the way!

speaker: Stede
en: My word! Havana grows livelier all the time.

speaker: Edward
en: Each funster we meet makes me more impatient to drink. Come on.

speaker: Stede
en: This is the spot.

speaker: Edward
en: The sea has much to offer, but a popping tavern always draws me back to shore.

speaker: Stede
en: Popping... yes. I would normally prefer to conduct my affairs somewhere quieter...

speaker: Edward
en: Take your time. I'll be just here.

speaker: Patron
en: Fancy meeting a Welshman deep in country. I'm English meself. Biding my time 'til the next war calls me to service.

speaker: Edward
en: Lucky King George having a piss-pot like you flying his flag.

speaker: Patron
en: Oy! Skulk! I seen your face before. You's mates with them pirates down in Nassau.

speaker: Edward
en: Shut your fucking gob or I fill it with shot. You hear me?

speaker: Patron
en: Edward, is it?

speaker: Man
en: You bastard!

speaker: Edward
en: Hey, I warned him...

speaker: Edward
en: You want a dust-up, I'll give you one. Come on lads! I've seen bigger arms on a bird! One more! Come on!

speaker: Edward
en: You'll have to hit harder than that! One more! Come on! Come on lads! I've seen bigger arms on a bird! You want a dust-up, I'll give you one. I'm still standing, lads!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: ¡Despejad la zona! (Clear the road!)

speaker: Citizen 1
en: ¡Vienen soldados! (Soldiers are coming!)

speaker: Citizen 2
en: ¡Corre! (Run!)

speaker: Stede
en: You—You're not leaving me?

speaker: Edward
en: I'll catch you up!

speaker: Soldier 2
en: ¡Perro inglés! (English dog!)

speaker: Edward
en: I've had all I can drink at present, lads. You go on without me. Look again, lobcocks.

speaker: Edward
en: Hopefully Stede wasn't pinched by those guards.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: If Du Casse's Men are pestering a Village, then they have fallen far indeed.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: The Padre's Trust will be worth far more than any stolen Reales.

speaker: Edward
en: And if the Men have no ill Intent, will the Padre join up?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: One can hope.

speaker: Edward
en: That's the Island. But where are the Ships?

speaker: Pirate 1
en: Lay off me, you drank your Fill. Now we're both paying for it.

speaker: Pirate 2
en: You think they'll hand us our Share when they return?

speaker: Pirate 1
en: Didn't you read the Letter? Them's a spiteful Lot.

speaker: Edward
en: Pirates write each other Letters now?

speaker: Edward
en: They've left for the Padre's Village.

speaker: Edward
en: Du Casse's Men have already left for the Padre's Village. Man your Stations, get us moving!

speaker: Edward
en: Those Ships belong to Du Casse. What have they done?

speaker: Dinah Calverley
en: The Padre hasn't moved since we buried them.

speaker: Henry Congreve
en: I tried to offer him his favorite fried Fish. He kept on praying as if I weren't there.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners...

speaker: Galvão
en: ...now and at the hour of our Death. Amen.

speaker: Edward
en: Who did this?

speaker: Galvão
en: This is my fault. Bishop Ravenscroft was the man who led me to God. He was like a Father to me. He believed in me. It was he who entrusted me with the care of the People here. When trouble with the began at Kingston, he wanted more there. He called on us to join him, but I argued against it. With Du Casse gone, I thought we were safe. We were only here because I disagreed with the Bishop! It was them. Du Casse's Men. They made me watch... The Lord is merciful and just. But my Heart is deceitfully wicked.

speaker: Galvão
en: I know Vengeance belongs to God alone, but I cannot turn away from this. Du Casse's Men must pay for what they've done. Will you help me?

speaker: Edward
en: My Offer still stands. Join me on the Jackdaw and we will hunt Du Casse's Men. We have a Compound at Great Inagua. Your people will be safe there.

speaker: Galvão
en: I will join you as Master-at-Arms. And when the Time comes, I will avenge my people.

speaker: Edward
en: Lads, this is our new Master-at-Arms. He calls himself Padre, but I advise you call him Sir if you don't want your Heads knocked together.

speaker: Galvão
en: You know the Job. As your Master-at-Arms, I require three things from each of you. Loyalty, Discipline and Courage. Display them and I will have you toppling Man o' Wars twice our Size, and Holds to match.

speaker: Galvão
en: You have a sturdy Vessel. I'll teach the Crew some new Maneuvers.

speaker: Edward
en: What did you have in Mind?

speaker: Galvão
en: Work the Sails and Rigging perfectly, and we can ram into our Foes.

speaker: Edward
en: I like where you're going with this.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Ah, Duncan! Hello.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Good morning, Duncan. Just over here...

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Stede
en: Edward! Hello, Edward! I found a man to purchase my remaining sugar! Quite a coup, I must say!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: He just called you Edward.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Oh, that's the merchant who sailed me here. Out of caution, I gave him a false name.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Ah... well done.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: We'll catch up, Bonnet! Later.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Very punctual, Duncan. This way.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Here he is, a man both Templars and Assassins have sought for over a decade. I am told your surname is Roberts. Is this so? You recognize this, I think.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: According to the old tales, the blood of a sage is required to enter the Observatory.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: We have the key. Now we need only its location. Perhaps mister Roberts will be eager to provide it. Transfer him to my residence.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Such a fuss over one man. Is the Observatory really such a grand prize?

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Sí, sin duda. (Yes, indeed.) The Observatory was a tool built by the Precursor race. Its worth is without measure.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Precursor race... I see.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: One of your early letters mentioned the desire to kill the Mayan Mentor, Ah Tabai. Were you able to carry out this contract before coming here?

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: I... I was not, no. Too many... complications along the way.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: A pity. But the maps you delivered with this vial will see that job finished.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Aye. That's the idea.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: It's too quiet.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: I don't like this route, Torres. We're exposed.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Something is wrong. Stay close, Grand Master!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: I feel it too. Do not let them get their hands on the Sage! At whatever cost!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Assassins! Above! They're on the rooftops! Crossing me is fatal, cur! Don't expect mercy. I've survived much worse than you! To action then. It ends now! You're consigned to oblivion.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Watch the streets and alleys. They could be anywhere!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Torres
en: Protect the Sage!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Assassins!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Assassins! Malédiction! (Shit!)

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Torres
en: Guard the Sage! ¡Proteged al Sabio, vamos! (Guard the Sage! Quickly!)

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: There! Protect the Governor!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Une deuxième tempête se lève. (A second storm beckons.) To the Governor's Residence, quickly! Watch the streets and alleys. They could be anywhere.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Assassins! (Assassins!)

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Above! They're on the rooftops!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Triple the shipment of firearms, Julien. These attacks will escalate.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Oui (Yes.) We do well to brace for further troubles.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Whatever they try, we won't be caught unprepared again. The Governor's Residence is near! Come!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Another wave!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: To arms!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Protect the Sage!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: Morbleu! (Fuck!) We need to move, now!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Guard
en: Ah!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Stop him!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: You're a nimble one, I'll give you that.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Roberts
en: Whelp! You curs are on a course you'll sorely regret!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Roberts
en: Blast! Is there no way out of this dust bowl?

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Hah! Nowhere to run.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Roberts
en: Have you ever been flayed, boy?

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: They could never catch me.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Got you!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Roberts
en: Well done, lap dog.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Quiet!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Julien
en: We'll see him to the prisons, Grand Master.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Double the watch.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: Well, I'll be buggered. What an active day we've had, gents!

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: Sí. (Yes.) Beset on all sides by our enemies. We must be more cautious.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: I do wish I could remain to see our drama done, but I must avail myself of these winds and sail for England.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: By all means, Captain. Speed and fortune to you.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Woodes
en: With luck, I'll return myself a governor. And with my idiot King's blessing, no less. ¡Adiós! (Goodbye!)

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: As for you, Mr. Walpole... I consider this the first payment in a long-term investment. Gracias. (Thank you.)

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Obliged.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Laureano
en: I would like you to be present for the interrogation tomorrow. Call around noon.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: Yes, sir.

scene: A Man They Call the Sage
speaker: Edward
en: All that toil for this pittance? Jaysus.

speaker: Antó
en: What do you want, Englishman?

speaker: Edward
en: Edward Kenway. I'm here to warn you of danger. And I'm Welsh.

speaker: Antó
en: You all look the same to me. Why should I need your warning? My life is all danger.

speaker: Edward
en: I may have brought it on you.

speaker: Antó
en: This means you owe me. As it happens, I could use a man, to help free some of my friends.

speaker: Edward
en: Slaves, you mean?

speaker: Antó
en: Brothers, warriors, the hope of the Maroons.

speaker: Edward
en: Doesn't sound like my business, mate.

speaker: Antó
en: All I need is for you to mingle with your countrymen. Listen to hints for where my friends are held.

speaker: Edward
en: Fine. I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Guard 1
en: And then he dismissed me. Without pay! For drunkenness! Alleged drunkenness. All I had to do was escort the man north, no south, no. North. Definitely north.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Towards the warehouse.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Right, the warehouse. In any case, he's a slave! He's in bilboes. Not like he's going to get away.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Let's have another round and we'll think this through.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Are you buying? I just lost me job?

speaker: Guard 3
en: They're holding the cur nearby.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Whatever for?

speaker: Guard 3
en: I don't know. To make an example of, or some such.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Well what did he do?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Does he need to do anything? Sometimes examples just have to be made.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Now isn't that just the truth?

speaker: Guard 3
en: I wouldn't linger here. The walls have ears, if you know what I mean.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Are we followed?

speaker: Guard 3
en: We must warn the others!

speaker: Edward
en: You've got the information I need, mate.

speaker: Guard
en: No! I've heard of your kind... Ass- Assassin. Don't hurt me.

speaker: Edward
en: All I want to know is where this slave is. Do you know of anyone being held... specially like?

speaker: Guard
en: Please! Let me live. My wife and children

speaker: Edward
en: Come on then, out with it.

speaker: Guard
en: Look near the windmill.

speaker: Edward
en: See, was that so hard?

speaker: Vane
en: Keep still now! I'll take these oysters you've hoarded.

speaker: Edward
en: You mad sap. This island's crawling with food if only you'd care to look for it.

speaker: Vane
en: I am looking, lout. I found some just here. Don't! Don't come following now! You hear me! Don't come looking for me!

speaker: Edward
en: Wretched fool.

speaker: Vane
en: Here's a health to the king and a lasting peace / To faction an end, to wealth increase. / Come, let us drink it while we have breath. / For there's no drinking after death. / And he that will this health deny, Down among the dead men, / Down among the dead men, / Down, down, down, down, / Down among the dead men let him lie. Go dance with the fisherman and their dories, Kenway! This island's mine! Come at me and I'll cap you, bastard! It were your bloody imagination that landed us here, Kenway! I'll be damned if I let that mind make one more decision for me!

speaker: Edward
en: Will you not talk to me, Vane? Are you fixed on this madness?

speaker: Vane
en: Madness? Nothing mad about a man fighting to survive, is there!

speaker: Edward
en: I mean you no harm, you corker! Now let's work this out like gentlemen!

speaker: Vane
en: Ah. God I've got a bleeding headache on account of your jabbering. Now stay back and let me live in peace!

speaker: Edward
en: I would if you stopped filching the food I gather and the water I find!

speaker: Vane
en: I'll stop nothing 'til you've paid me back in blood. You was the reason we were out looking for slavers. And you was the reason Jack Rackham took my crew!

speaker: Edward
en: VANE! Face me, man!

speaker: Vane
en: Ah! I said not to follow!

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus! You've lost your head, man!

speaker: Vane
en: It's a fair exchange for finding these flintlocks and grenadoes!

speaker: Edward
en: Listen Vane! We could hunt with those guns!

speaker: Vane
en: And I mean to! You and your bloody fairy stories got us into this mess, Kenway. And I'll be damned if I let you drag me into another!

speaker: Edward
en: You keep this up, and I'll have to kill ya, Vane!

speaker: Vane
en: Bloody try! By all means! I see you coming, curl! I see you plain and clear! It's either you or me who's leaving this island alive, Welcher! 'Cause I'm not gonna sail again in a world cursed by your ugly mug! Not dead yet? Here! I'll blow you to hell! I'll flush you out! You can't hide, Kenway! Not escaping me! Blow off some limbs! Bloody rags will be all that's left of you, Kenway!

speaker: Edward
en: You god damn fucking knave, Vane!

speaker: Vane
en: N-nancy boy. Y-you only done half of the fucking job!

speaker: Edward
en: Fucking hell. Is this my reward for believing the best about men? For thinking that a bilge rat like you could muster up some fucking sense, once in a while! Maybe Hornigold was right. Maybe the world does need men of ambition to stop the likes of you from mucking it all up.

speaker: Vane
en: Or maybe you just don't have the stones to live with no regrets.

speaker: Edward
en: Don't save me a spot in hell, shanker. I ain't coming soon.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: This Place is ancient.

speaker: Edward
en: This must have been something to seen when it was new built.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Oh yeah.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: It fits well.

speaker: Edward
en: ¡Buenos dias! (Good Morning!) Mister Duncan Walpole of England to see the Governor, I believe he is expecting me.

speaker: Guard
en: Sí, señor Walpole. Entre, por favor. (Yes, Mister Walpole, Please enter.)

speaker: Soldier 1
en: ¿Ese es el hom bre? El... ¿Cómo lo llamabas? ¿Asesino? (Is that the man? The... what do they call him, Assassin?)

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Sí. Duncan Walpole. Debería haber llegado hace muchos días. (Yes. Duncan Walpole. He should have been here many days ago.)

speaker: Soldier 1
en: No me gusta que los extranjeros se paseen por nuestra ciudad. No me fío de ellos. (I don't like these foreigners strolling about the city. I don't trust them.)

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Cállate. ¡El gobernador tiene invitados! ¡Todos franceses e ingleses! (Hold your tongue, man. The governor has guests! From France and England alike!)

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Parece un hombre rudo. Le suponía un aspectos más... respetable. (He's a rough looking man. I assumed he might look... respectable.)

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Lleva meses en alta mar. Sé indulgente con él. (The man's been at sea for months. Be easy on him.)

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Parece un hombre rudo. Le suponía un aspectos más... respetable. (He's a rough looking man. I assumed he might look... respectable.)

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Lleva meses en alta mar. Sé indulgente con él. (The man's been at sea for months. Be easy on him.)

speaker: Soldier 5
en: No me gusta que los extranjeros se paseen por nuestra ciudad. No me fío de ellos. (I don't like these foreigners strolling about the city. I don't trust them.)

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Cállate. ¡El gobernador tiene invitados! ¡Todos franceses e ingleses! (Hold your tongue, man. The governor has guests! From France and England alike!)

speaker: Woodes
en: Good morning, Sir! Would I be correct in thinking you are Duncan Walpole?

speaker: Edward
en: I am indeed.

speaker: Woodes
en: I thought as much. Woodes Rogers. A pleasure.

speaker: Edward
en: The same.

speaker: Woodes
en: I must say, my wife has a terrible eye for description.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm sorry?

speaker: Woodes
en: My wife. You met her some years ago at the Percys' masquerade ball.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah! Quite...

speaker: Woodes
en: She called you 'devilishly handsome'. Obviously a lie to stoke my jealousy. Julien! Our guest of honor has arrived, Mister Duncan Walpole.

speaker: Julien
en: Ah... Julien du Casse. I hope your conversion to our Order is an honest one. I have no love for Assassins, but even less for liars.

speaker: Edward
en: I have not come to disappoint.

speaker: Woodes
en: Up for a bit of sport, Duncan? The old man isn't ready just yet.

speaker: Woodes
en: You've got my two best pairs of matched pistols, Duncan, so handle with care.

speaker: Edward
en: If I had eight, I'd treat each as my own son.

speaker: Woodes
en: Pull off a few shots, if you like. Get a feel for it.

speaker: Julien
en: I once fought beside a man who carried nine on his person. They were a boon in battle but hindered his ability to swim, sadly.

speaker: Woodes
en: Quite. Has a good kick, yes?

speaker: Julien
en: I long for the day where one firearm carries four bullets, and not the opposite.

speaker: Woodes
en: I have a friend in England you may like to meet, Julien. James Puckle... he's working on something extraordinary.

speaker: Julien
en: Magnifique! (Wonderful!)

speaker: Woodes
en: Enough amusements, Duncan. How about a true challenge? All right. Here's a simple challenge. Try to strike every target before this hourglass empties. Remember, hit every target within the allotted time.

speaker: Woodes
en: Yes!

speaker: Woodes
en: Ah! Bad Luck. Try again. Rotten Luck, eh?

speaker: Woodes
en: Pull off a few shots, if you like. Get a feel for it. You've got my two best pairs of matched pistols, Duncan, so handle them with care.

speaker: Edward
en: If I had eight, I'd treat each as my own son.

speaker: Woodes
en: Quite.

speaker: Julien
en: I once fought beside a man who carried nine on his person. They were a boon in battle but hindered his ability to swim, sadly.

speaker: Woodes
en: I have a friend in England you may like to meet, Julien. James Puckle... he's working on something extraordinary.

speaker: Woodes
en: All right. Here's a simple challenge. Try to strike every target before this hourglass empties. Remember, hit every target within the allotted time.

speaker: Woodes
en: Has a good kick, yes?

speaker: Julien
en: Magnifique!

speaker: Woodes
en: Excellent. A good hit!

speaker: Woodes
en: Wonderful. You're a crack shot, Duncan! As good with a pistol as with your wrist blade, I imagine.

speaker: Julien
en: Duncan. Where are your wrist blades? I have never seen an Assassin so ill equipped.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah. Damaged, sadly. Beyond all repair.

speaker: Julien
en: Hm. Have your choice.

speaker: Edward
en: Where did you find all these?

speaker: Julien
en: I did not find them. I took them. These are souvenirs.

speaker: Julien
en: Two blades, as is the custom, oui (yes)?

speaker: Edward
en: Custom, aye.

speaker: Julien
en: Duncan, would you indulge us with a demonstration of your techniques?

speaker: Edward
en: Well I, uh...

speaker: Woodes
en: You must! We put together a training course in anticipation of your arrival. It would be a shame to leave here without seeing you in action.

speaker: Edward
en: Yes, of course... I mean if there is time I would gladly, uh... show you what I know.

speaker: Julien
en: Here, you see... Situations well suited for your skills.

speaker: Woodes
en: Have a go! A blade in a crowd is always the simplest. Nothing grandiose. Just quick and clean.

speaker: Julien
en: Show us another technique!

speaker: Woodes
en: Quite ingenious to use bales of hay as cover, don't you think?

speaker: Woodes
en: God! That's the spirit! Secrecy.

speaker: Woodes
en: The advantage of surprise cannot be overstated, isn't that so? Especially around a blind corner.

speaker: Woodes
en: God blind me, that's a clever trick.

speaker: Julien
en: Your aerial kills have a poetic beauty, despite their conspicuous quality. Would you show us?

speaker: Julien
en: Magnifique! (Magnificent!)

speaker: Julien
en: Is it also possible to deliver a killing blow at high speed?

speaker: Julien
en: Mon Dieu! (My God!) Such a powerful strike!

speaker: Woodes
en: Fascinating.

speaker: Julien
en: The Assassins have trained you well, Duncan. You chose a perfect time to leave them behind.

speaker: Woodes
en: At great risk, I imagine. Betraying the Assassins is never good for one's health.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, neither is drinking liquor, but I am drawn to its dangers all the same. And what is your business here, Sir? Are you an associate of the governor's? Or a pending acquaintance like myself?

speaker: Julien
en: Guns, blades, cannons, grenadoes (grenades)... Anything that may kill a man, I am happy to provide.

speaker: Woodes
en: A smuggler of sorts.

speaker: Edward
en: And how is your wife these days, Captain Rogers? Is she, ah, here in Havana?

speaker: Woodes
en: I trust she's well. But I wouldn't know. I have been in Madagascar some fourteen months, hunting pirates. It took some work to dislodge the criminals there, but we managed it. In future, I hope to use these same tactics throughout the West Indies.

speaker: Edward
en: And how did you deal with their kind?

speaker: Woodes
en: Very simply. Most pirates are as ignorant as apes. I merely offered them a choice... take a pardon and return to England penniless but free men, or be hanged by the neck until dead.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah, I imagine Nassau would be your next target?

speaker: Woodes
en: Very astute, Duncan. Indeed.

speaker: Edward
en: Best of luck with that.

speaker: Woodes
en: Grand Master Torres. Mister Duncan Walpole has arrived.

speaker: Laureano
en: Sí... (Indeed...) You were expected one week ago.

speaker: Edward
en: Apologies, governor. My ship was set upon by pirates. We were scuttled. I arrived only yesterday.

speaker: Laureano
en: Unfortunate. Forgive my caution, but were you able to salvage from these pirates the items you promised me?

speaker: Edward
en: Ah, yes Sir, I was.

speaker: Laureano
en: Increíble (Incredible.) The Assassins have more resources than I had imagined but... not nearly enough to deter us. It is a pleasure to meet you at last, Duncan. You are most welcome. Come gentlemen. We have much to discuss.

speaker: Laureano
en: Convened at last. And in such continental company... England, France, Spain... Citizens of sad and corrupted empires. But you are Templars now. The secret and true legislators of the world. Please, hold out your hands. Mark and remember our purpose. To guide all wayward souls 'til they reach a quiet road. To guide all wayward desire 'til impassioned hearts are cooled. To guide all wayward minds to safe and sober thought. By the Father of Understanding's Light, let our work now begin. Decades ago, the Counsel entrusted me with the task of locating in these West Indies a forgotten place our precursors once called the Observatory. See here... Look upon these images and commit them to memory. They tell a very old and important story. For two decades now I have endeavored to locate this Observatory... a place rumored to contain a tool of incredible utility and power. It houses a kind of armillary sphere, if you like. A device that would grant us the power to locate and monitor EVERY man and woman on Earth, whatever their location. Only imagine what it would mean to have such a power. With this device, there would be no secrets among men. No lies. No trickery. Only justice. Pure justice. This is the Observatory's promise. And we must take it for our own.

speaker: Woodes
en: Do we know its whereabouts?

speaker: Laureano
en: We will soon. For in our custody is the one man who does. A man named Roberts, once called a Sage.

speaker: Julien
en: It has been forty-five years since anyone has seen a true Sage. Can you be sure this one is authentic?

speaker: Laureano
en: We are confident he is.

speaker: Woodes
en: The Assassins will come for him.

speaker: Laureano
en: Indeed they will. But... thanks to Duncan and the information he has delivered, the Assassins won't be a problem for much longer.

speaker: Laureano
en: All will be made clear tomorrow, gentlemen, when you meet the Sage for yourselves. Until then... let us drink. Let us find the Observatory together. For with its power, kings will fall, clergy will cower, and the hearts and minds of the world will be ours.

speaker: Laureano
en: Rest well, Duncan. Tomorrow the Treasure Fleet arrives, and with it your reward. After which, we will discuss further schemes.

speaker: Edward
en: I look forward to it.

speaker: Laureano
en: ¡Excelente! (Excellent!) Meet me down at the docks, first thing tomorrow morning.

speaker: Guard
en: Governor Torres requests your presence at the docks near the Castillo, first thing tomorrow morning.

speaker: Guard
en: Governor Torres requests your presence at the docks near the Castillo, first thing tomorrow morning.

speaker: Edward
en: I'd like to have a closer look at this strange diagram.

speaker: Bartender
en: You! Not again.

speaker: Edward
en: Have you any room? I can pay.

speaker: Bartender
en: What? And have another brawl wreck the place? Out with you!

speaker: Edward
en: Your loss, mate. I know where to find some privacy. What he can't see won't trouble him.

speaker: Edward
en: They've no room for a scoundrel like you either eh?

speaker: Edward
en: This could be the key to my fortune.

speaker: Edward
en: Can you feel it, Adé? We're moments away from the grandest prize of all.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I feel nothing but a hot wind in my ears, captain.

speaker: Edward
en: Come on, man. When we take this treasure, we'll be set for life. All of us. Ten times over.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: As you wish.

speaker: Edward
en: Ahoy, Roberts! We'll cast anchor and meet ashore.

speaker: Roberts
en: You were followed, captain Kenway. How long for, I wonder?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: It's Hornigold.

speaker: Edward
en: Burn and flay that turncoat.

speaker: Roberts
en: Deal with your old friend in haste, captain. Before I regret my favor to you.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Captain, think carefully about what you mean to do here.

speaker: Edward
en: What are you grousing about, Adé? It's Ben Hornigold come to kill us out there!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye, and the traitor needs to die. But what then? Can you say with certainty that you deserve the Observatory more than he and his Templars?

speaker: Edward
en: No, I can't! And I don't care to try. But if you've a better idea, by all means tell me.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Forget working with Roberts! Tell the Assassins. Bring them here and let them protect this place.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, I'll bring them here! If they're willing to pay me a good sum for it.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Bah... We'll have a hard fight if Hornigold draws us any deeper into this fog. We're nearing "The Devil's Backbone".

speaker: Edward
en: You mean them crags that look like the backbone of a beast?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye. (The Devil's Backbone) the Spaniards call it.

speaker: Edward
en: There's Hornigold. Get in close.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: We're in close quarters here, captain. Careful you don't run us aground. Can you do this Breddah? Is your heart up for it?

speaker: Edward
en: Truth be told, I was hoping the sea would swallow him up, and see the job done for me.

speaker: Edward
en: I will be coming back.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Some mighty piss-poor sailing back there, lads! And if we live out this day, by God, I'm flaying every last bitch of you! Steady up! And keep your backs together, lads! This fight ain't over! I know this bastard, and I've seen what he can do. He'll be after me, sure as I'm standing here! Hold your ground, and be ready for anything!

speaker: Hornigold
en: You could have been a man who stood for something. But you've a killer's heart now. With nothing but mettle to show for all your blunders.

speaker: Edward
en: A damn sight better than you have, Ben. The heart of a traitor, who thinks himself better than his mates!

speaker: Hornigold
en: Aye, and proven true! What have you done since Nassau fell? Nothing but murder and mayhem!

speaker: Edward
en: You threw in with the very kind we once hated!

speaker: Hornigold
en: No! These Templars are different. I wish you could see that. But if you continue on your present course, you'll find you're the only one walking it! With the gallows at its end.

speaker: Edward
en: It may be. But now the world has one less snake in it. And that's enough for me.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: I didn't take you for a petal-picking sort.

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: To pluck is to end. You Love. You lose. I mentioned a Commander. Did I? No matter.

speaker: Edward
en: The Man who put you in a box? Vile business, Tobias.

speaker: Tobias
en: So it goes. Should I be spared? When others face the Box, should I stand aside and tinker with Cannons?

speaker: Edward
en: Well, there are no Boxes here and we hoped you would help us with some improvements on the Jackdaw.

speaker: Tobias
en: My knobby Hands once fashioned deadly instruments, to be sure. I can't be sure. Can I trust Memory? I see the Mortars I made for the Commander, stout and of uncommon Strength and Quality.

speaker: Edward
en: Well then, I would like to have a look at those. Where are they now?

speaker: Tobias
en: A dark Place. A place of Screams. A Theatre of Cruelty. The Seas of Punta Guarico, on an Island called Petite Caverne. If the Mortars are to be found, they are there, or thereabouts.

speaker: Edward
en: The sooner we find this Cave, the better the Jackdaw will be for it.

speaker: Edward
en: I expect it won't be as easy as sailing in and taking the Weapons.

speaker: Tobias
en: Who can know. If much is as it was, Petite Caverne is well-guarded. The Commander keeps the Weapons under Lock and Key.

speaker: Edward
en: Hmm. Not exactly ripe for the picking, then.

speaker: Edward
en: How did you discover you had a knack for tinkering? Was it with the Privateers?

speaker: Tobias
en: Yes.

speaker: Edward
en: All right, then.

speaker: Tobias
en: We're here.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll wait outside the Cavern.

speaker: Tobias
en: Expect me, shortly.

speaker: Edward
en: Lads, keep the Jackdaw out of Sight. Find us when we're done!

speaker: Edward
en: You stayed in this dank Place? Tell me there was somewhere to call Home before this.

speaker: Tobias
en: There was an Island where I felt warmth. Contentment? I was a different man.

speaker: Edward
en: We all were, Mate. What was this Island called?

speaker: Edward
en: How long must we wait?

speaker: Tobias
en: They come after dark. It will be worth it. The Commander hungers for Power. My Guns sate his Appetite.

speaker: Edward
en: Two there. Careful, now.

speaker: British soldier 1
en: Where is the Commander?

speaker: British soldier 2
en: Up ahead, on the Dock. Best not bother him, he's busy with his... Tests.

speaker: British soldier 1
en: That's the problem. We're running out of Boxes for the Bodies.

speaker: British soldier 2
en: I'm bettin' he goes for the left Arm on the next.

speaker: British soldier 3
en: Jaysus, Man. Careful you don't take on the Commander's cruel indifference.

speaker: British soldier 2
en: Or will it be an Eye?

speaker: British soldier 3
en: You're hopeless.

speaker: Tobias
en: At last.

speaker: Edward
en: So much for a quiet approach. Aim true, Smith!

speaker: Edward
en: Easy, Man! Christ!

speaker: Tobias
en: A Debt was owed. No more.

speaker: Tobias
en: The Commander is ahead if I'm right.

speaker: Edward
en: You don't seem too concerned with the Weapons. That's why we're here.

speaker: Tobias
en: It is a hateful and wicked Bargain but it is ours.

speaker: Edward
en: Smith, I took you to be caught in Death's Shadow. Now I see you're the one casting it.

speaker: Pirate
en: No, no! Please, I don't want to go in there!

speaker: British Officer 1
en: Shut your mouth and do what you're told.

speaker: Pirate
en: Tobias? Brother! It's you!

speaker: Tobias
en: Hurry. The Ship outside. Go.

speaker: Tobias
en: On. Moving on. We must move on.

speaker: Commander Cyrus
en: Bring another one in and clear the Mess of the last.

speaker: British Officer 2
en: There was a nice Ring on that one.

speaker: Cyrus
en: Yes, leave it, that's mine.

speaker: British Officer 2
en: Ugh, the Stench...

speaker: Tobias
en: That's him.

speaker: British Officer 3
en: The Devil? Who are you?

speaker: Tobias
en: Memory fading. Mind failing. What else?

speaker: British Officer 3
en: Are you simple?

speaker: British Officer 4
en: Why are you here? Filthy Rat!

speaker: Tobias
en: Why am I here? No matter. What will I do? That is the Question.

speaker: British Officer 5
en: Who are you? Stop!

speaker: Tobias
en: A mere bag of Bones and Dust. As are we all. Let us hasten your Decay.

speaker: Cyrus
en: Who are you?

speaker: Edward
en: He's yours, Smith.

speaker: Cyrus
en: You.

speaker: Cyrus
en: What? All of this for some Flowers? Maybe I should have looked closer at you. And taken more.

speaker: Cyrus
en: You piece of Shit. That's all you are, Dirt and Water.

speaker: Cyrus
en: I broke you open and looked inside. And you know what I found? Nothing. You're empty. You're a Puppet! A Nobody! You're Nothing!

speaker: Tobias
en: There is no Box dark enough. But this will do.

speaker: Edward
en: What? Not even a Smile? We exorcised your Demon! Live a little, Man.

speaker: Tobias
en: He is gone. Yes. But the Shadow on my Soul remains.

speaker: Tobias
en: I need to see Crooked Island. There's a Village there. After that, the Mortars.

speaker: Edward
en: Are there more parts you need at Crooked Island.

speaker: Edward
en: What is it Smith? What is there that you need?

speaker: Tobias
en: Love. Long dimmed, nearly gone. Not gone.

speaker: Edward
en: We are bound for Crooked Island, then. But I need those Mortars to be set right after our visit.

speaker: Officer
en: (Up! Up! Stand up!) (Here's to riches and wealth, all mine in abundance today!) (Long live tax day! Long live tax collectors!) (Here's to the people of Havana, who work hard so that I may live well!)

speaker: Anne Bonny
en: Finding Maynard in Kingston will be like looking for a Needle in a Bottle of Hay.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: He's no shrinking Violet. He will have made certain everyone in Town knows he's there.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: I was only in Kingston once. It all got a bit blurry after the second Bottle.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: I know Kingston well enough. If you ask me, Maynard will be with his Military Friends on the western side.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a lot of soldiers for an old Barn. It looks like Padre was right.

speaker: British officer
en: This Lot here belongs to Lieutenant Maynard. I have a Letter in my Hand saying it goes out on the next Transport.

speaker: British officer
en: Report!

speaker: British soldier
en: Sir! Transport has informed us there will be a delay.

speaker: British officer
en: Well how long did they say! I'm not going to be the one to tell the Lieutenant he can't have his Stuff!

speaker: British soldier
en: They didn't say, Sir!

speaker: British officer
en: Damn it! What with the HMS Demolition getting away late for Eleuthera Today as well... You better hope that Transport arrives, or he'll have both our Heads.

speaker: Edward
en: Blast! Maynard's not here. He's left for Eleuthera.

speaker: Edward
en: The Bastard's not even a real Captain.

speaker: Edward
en: A Pirate Master Gunner. This could work in our favor.

speaker: Edward
en: Silverware from Thatch's Revenge, and his other Treasures. Maynard's been helping himself to Pirate Holds.

speaker: Edward
en: Anne will be wondering where I am.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: Captain!

speaker: Galvão
en: I've good News, Captain. My Spanish Friends have agreed to help us. Indeed, they have pursued Maynard themselves for some time. His Armada has been seen at Fort Serranilla. They've already begun shipping out.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Tell me of these Friends of yours, Padre. What am I sailing into?

speaker: Galvão
en: Consorts of my old Crew. I will not lie to you, Captain, they are not our natural Allies. If it favored them, they would just as soon hunt us.

speaker: Edward
en: Do you trust them, then, not to turn once the Fight is won?

speaker: Galvão
en: I trust they hate Maynard, and they are not without Honour. They will see this done.

speaker: Edward
en: Good enough.

speaker: Edward
en: Of how much Benefit do you think these Spaniards will be to us?

speaker: Galvão
en: If measured by their Hatred of Maynard, considerable. He took some of their Number, and what is worse, he stole what was in their Holds.

speaker: Edward
en: Maynard is gathering quite the Fortune to himself.

speaker: Galvão
en: He could not have made a graver Mistake. I know of Nothing more vindictive than a robbed Spaniard.

speaker: Galvão
en: This does not bode well. They should be here.

speaker: Edward
en: I hope you were right about this.

speaker: Galvão
en: There! They have come at Last. Thank the Almighty.

speaker: Edward
en: We go for Maynard! Full Sail!

speaker: Pirate 1
en: A fine Fleet we make! But you will have to Fly to beat us to Maynard!

speaker: Edward
en: I can't figure how Maynard has gathered so many Ships and Crews at his Rank.

speaker: Galvão
en: The Spaniards tell me his Captain is a Waister who won't even go to Sea. He leaves all Commands to Maynard. The Crews follow Maynard because he uses the Gold he takes to buy their loyalty.

speaker: Edward
en: That is a waste of good Gold.

speaker: Pirate 2
en: ¡Allá vamos, Maynard, cabrón de mano larga! (Here we come Maynard, you thieving Whore!) ¡Nos llevaremos lo que es nuestro y también tu cabeza! (We will take back what is ours, and then your Head as well!)

speaker: Galvão
en: We have the Victory!

speaker: Pirate 3
en: ¡Chúpate esa, idiota! (Take that, Fool!)

speaker: Edward
en: There are more! We're not done yet.

speaker: Galvão
en: To Hell with you, you Bastards. Forgive me, Father... But it's true.

speaker: Pirate 4
en: Bravo! To Hell with our Enemies, and Blessings on our Allies. Ole! (Hurray!)

speaker: Edward
en: That can't be all there is to Maynard's Armada.

speaker: Galvão
en: It is a good Victory, but we have wounded him only.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. This was but few of his Ships, I think. The rest of the Armada is still out there.

speaker: Edward
en: The Spaniards were brave. They gave their Lives rather than suffer Defeat.

speaker: Galvão
en: Aye, Adios mis Amigos (Goodbye my Friends). They would be glad for our Victory.

speaker: Edward
en: They helped us take a Bite out of Maynard's Armada. I am sorry I doubted them.

speaker: Assassin 1
en: The Mentor bids us be ready for anything. The Templars may know our whereabouts now.

speaker: Assassin 2
en: It was Walpole, isn't that right? The Englishman?

speaker: Assassin 1
en: Aye. He played us from the start... betrayed our confidence.

speaker: Assassin 2
en: How could we have known? Even Ah Tabai was taken in by his charms.

speaker: Assassin 3
en: I saw a ship pass this way, close upon the shore, then gone.

speaker: Assassin 4
en: Ah Tabai warned us to be vigilant. The Templars have been closing in for well on a year now.

speaker: Assassin 3
en: Indeed. But Templars make noise with their comings and goings. I've not heard a thing just yet.

speaker: Assassin 4
en: You will.

speaker: Assassin 7
en: (An imposter wears the costume of a traitor. How much lower can one fall?)

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus, Kidd! You led me into a mess. Is it these monks guarding the treasure you promised me?

speaker: Kidd
en: I told you I had a secret to share... but I didn't say it would be easy. Now let's get this door open and I'll show you what's inside.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah! We're on to something. I can feel it...

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Captain Kenway.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah!

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Where is the Assassin, Duncan Walpole?

speaker: Edward
en: Dead and buried. After he tried to kill me.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: We are not sorry to see him gone. But it was you who carried out his final betrayal. Why?

speaker: Edward
en: Money was my only aim.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Should I find comfort in that? You murdered our brothers and sisters in Havana!

speaker: Kidd
en: He has the Sense, Mentor.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: James tells me you treated with the Templars there. Did you see the man they call The Sage?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Would you recognize his face if you saw it again?

speaker: Edward
en: I reckon so...

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: I must be certain.

speaker: Kidd
en: Not a word. Come on.

speaker: Thatch
en: Go on, Captain Queernabs! Tell me I'm under arrest! Tell me!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Them your breds (brethren)?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Fly away, boyo! Back to your master!

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. We was privateers together, before the wars ended. I'll see you ashore.

speaker: Hornigold
en: By God, you're a sight for salty eyes! Come you in and have a drink.

speaker: Edward
en: Morning, all.

speaker: Thatch
en: Ahoy, Kenway. Who's this?

speaker: Edward
en: Adéwalé, the Jackdaw's quartermaster.

speaker: Thatch
en: Jackdaw? You named your brig after a poxy bird?

speaker: Edward
en: Adé, these lads are the better part of our growing confederacy here. Ed Thatch, Ben Hornigold, James Kidd.

speaker: Hornigold
en: You let him carry a pistol, do ye?

speaker: Edward
en: Peace, Ben. Adé saved my life. And now we're looking for a crew to fill out the rest of my ship.

speaker: Thatch
en: Well, there's scores of capable men about. But use caution. A shipload of the King's sailors showed up a fortnight back, causing trouble and knocking about like they own the place.

speaker: Edward
en: Right. I'll see who I can muster.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Send any men you find to the Jackdaw. I'll put them to work.

speaker: Edward
en: Cheers Adé.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: What's all this pissing and moaning about? Has something happened?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Soldiers have come, that's what's happened. Sent by the King himself.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: If a lobster sticks his nose in my business, I'll slice it off.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: I'm with you, mate. True hearted!

speaker: Civilian 5
en: What'll we do, Lizabeth? I'll be hanged for piracy if them soldiers catch hold of me.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Stand your ground and give'em a whallop, then! You got naught else to live for!

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Captain Kenway, come fast! There's soldiers that clapped a man in irons. They mean to hang him!

speaker: Hornigold
en: Now you'll want to sail somewhere rich with plunder.

speaker: Edward
en: Have you heard of a place called the Observatory?

speaker: Kidd
en: Aye. It's an old legend. Like , or the Fountain of Youth.

speaker: Edward
en: What have you heard?

speaker: Kidd
en: It's meant to be a temple or a tomb. Hiding a treasure of some kind.

speaker: Edward
en: That's it! You see here.

speaker: Thatch
en: Ah, rot! It's fairy stories you prefer to gold, is it?

speaker: Edward
en: It's worth more than gold, Thatch. Ten-thousand times above what we could pull off any Spanish ship.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Robbing the king to pay his paupers is how we earn our keep here, lad. That ain't a fortune, it's a fantasy.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Is that pirate hunter dead?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. By my own hand. Why is it you alone can find what so many want?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: I was born with memories of this place. Memories of another time entirely, I think. Like a... like another life I have already led.

speaker: Edward
en: Curse you for a lurch, man, and speak some sense.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Not today. After you captain. The path ahead is dangerous. The men native to this land will put up a fight, Edward. Are you willing to push back if necessary? To kill if needed?

speaker: Edward
en: You'll hear from me soon.

speaker: Edward
en: Are we close, God dammit?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Somewhat. The path winds further still, beset by more unruly men. Go...

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Ah, you see here? The handiwork of men born and bred to protect this place. The Guardians of the Observatory.

speaker: Edward
en: How long have their kind been here?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Oh, at least a thousand years or more. Dedicated men. Very deadly.

speaker: Edward
en: Is this the Observatory? All this?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Aye. An almost sacred place. All it needs is a drop of my blood... and the door opens, after almost eighty thousands years.

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus, Roberts! Have you gone mad?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Quite the contrary, Edward. These wags would have gone mad at seeing what lies beyond this gate. But you, ah... I suspect you're made of sterner stuff. Now, pick up that chest, and carry it hither.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Dirty and decrepit. Not quite as I remember. But it has been over 80 millennia.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh rot. That's impossible.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Step as if on thin ice, captain. I must say, I am quite taken by this new vocation of mine. And it may amuse you to know that I have authored my own articles of conduct.

speaker: Edward
en: A creed of your own, eh?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: To keep the peace, yes. I forbid all gambling upon the deck, for instance, for it leads to more conflict than camaraderie. Desertion during battle is forbidden. And I require that all men keep their pieces and cutlasses clean and fit for service at all times...

speaker: Edward
en: Sensible.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: And punishable by death if disobeyed.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a step further than I'd go.

speaker: Edward
en: Look at this place!

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Beautiful, isn't it?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Like something out of a fairy tale, or one of them old poems.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: There were many stories about this place once. Tales that turned into rumors, and again into legend. The inevitable process of facts becoming fictions, before fading away entirely.

speaker: Edward
en: More blood vials.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Yes. These cubes contain the blood of an old and ancient people. A wonderful race, in their time.

speaker: Edward
en: The more you talk, man, the less I understand.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: I don't expect you to. Only remember this; the blood in those vials is not worth a single reale to anyone anymore. It may be again, one day. But not in this epoch. Here we are. Place the chest just there.

speaker: Edward
en: What's that noise?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Ah yes. A security measure. Just a moment.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: There we are.

speaker: Edward
en: So what is this place?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Think of it as a large spyglass, such as we sailors carry. A device capable of seeing great distances.

speaker: Edward
en: This is bloody witchcraft.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: No. This is mister Jack Rackham. Somewhere in the world, at this moment.

speaker: Edward
