en: Nassau. This is happening right now? We're seeing through his eyes?

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Aye.

speaker: Anne
en: I don't know, Jim. I haven't the faintest idea how to pilot a ship. That ain't work a woman does.

speaker: James
en: Tosh! I've seen a score of ladies who can reef a sail and spin a capstan.

speaker: Anne
en: And would you teach me to fight? With a cutlass, like? And maybe handle a pistol?

speaker: James
en: All that and more. But you have to want it. And work for it. There's no stumbling into true success.

speaker: Jack
en: Oy! Lad! That's my lass you're making love to! You lay off or I'll cut ya!

speaker: James
en: Up your arse, Rackham. Lad is the last thing you should be calling me.

speaker: Jack
en: Oh! Oh, is that right, is it? LAD!

speaker: Bartholomew
en: A curious bunch. Let's try another. Governor Woodes Rogers.

speaker: Woodes
en: You have a bold idea. But I must think it carefully through.

speaker: Laureano
en: A simple pledge of loyalty is all you need suggest to the . An oath, a gesture, and a simple ceremonial dram of blood taken from the finger. That's all.

speaker: Woodes
en: The ministers may give me trouble, but it should be easy enough to convince the . They do adore an excess of pomp and circumstance.

speaker: Laureano
en: Exactly. Tell them it's a show of fealty to the king... against those Jacobites.

speaker: Woodes
en: Yes. Indeed.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Ah, these Templars.

speaker: Laureano
en: The crucial detail is the blood. You must get a sample from each man. We want to be ready when we find the Observatory.

speaker: Woodes
en: Agreed.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: A precious tool, you see?

speaker: Edward
en: Sorcery. That's what it is.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Not so. Every mechanism that gives this device its light is a true and physical thing. Ancient yes, but nothing supernatural or strange.

speaker: Edward
en: We'll be masters of the ocean with that.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Oh... Such ambition.

speaker: Bartholomew
en: There's nothing in my code about loyalty, boy! You played your role, but our partnership is done!

speaker: Edward
en: You're a dead man, Roberts!

speaker: Edward
en: Roberts!

speaker: Bartholomew
en: Oh, your Jackdaw has flown, Edward, eh? That's the beauty of a democracy... the many outvote the one. Aye, you could sail with me, but... with a temper as hot as yours, I fear you'd burn us all to cinders. Luckily, I know the king's bounty on your head is a large one. And I... intend to collect. Have you... have you ever seen the inside of a Jamaican prison, boy? Have you?

speaker: Edward
en: Travers?

speaker: Vance
en: What tide brings you? You dress the part of an Assassin, yet I don't know your face.

speaker: Edward
en: Name's Kenway. I'm here to warn you of a threat to your Bureau.

speaker: Vance
en: Yes, I have noticed some suspicious men lurking about. I believe they work for a noted Templar, called Upton. Could you... eliminate them for me?

speaker: Edward
en: Oh, I may be persuaded, for a price. You wouldn't happen to know anything about a Templar key, would you?

speaker: Vance
en: I'm sure you can find it among Upton's men, IF I tell you where they are.

speaker: Edward
en: You've got yourself a deal.

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: He wanted the goods transported to his residence instead.

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: But why? What's he going to do with them?

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: I don't know. Store them? Smuggle them?

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: Smuggle them away from his own smuggling operation?

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: I know it sounds ridiculous, but a job's a job.

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: I suppose you're right. Smuggling from a smuggler.

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Hey, did you ever think about that word? "Smuggler?" Rather funny, isn't it?

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: Who ever thinks about words?

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Well, not me, certainly, but say it: "smuggler."

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: Smuggler.

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Smuggler!

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: You're right. It does have king of a funny ring to it. Smuggler!

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Wait, mate. Maybe we shouldn't be saying it quite so loud though?

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: On account of it being smuggling?

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Right.

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: Right.

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Will the others be waiting for us when we get there?

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: Yes. This should be easy.

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: So we move the goods. Then we go to the inn.

speaker: Smuggler 2
en: Oh, we should be so lucky!

speaker: Smuggler 1
en: Smuggler. Oh, look. There they are. Hello!

speaker: Upton
en: Who sent you? Why are you dressed like that, Templar?

speaker: Edward
en: I'm no such thing.

speaker: Upton
en: You're no Assassin. I run the bureau. I'd know if you were one of us.

speaker: Edward
en: That's rich, I've met the leader. You're not him.

speaker: Upton
en: Stop! I am Upton Travers. Bureau leader.

speaker: Edward
en: What? Is Vance your...

speaker: Upton
en: My blood brother! We work together. And those were not Templars that you killed! They were my workers!

speaker: Edward
en: Don't blame me. Your brother ordered it.

speaker: Upton
en: Does he mean to usurp me?

speaker: Edward
en: I don't know, mate, I'm only after a Templar key.

speaker: Upton
en: A what? Please, I need for you to tell me everything.

speaker: Edward
en: And why should I trust you?

speaker: Upton
en: Meet me at the Bureau. And I will show you.

speaker: Edward
en: Bother.

speaker: Upton
en: My lovesick idiot of a brother has misled you.

speaker: Edward
en: Start from the start, mate.

speaker: Upton
en: Recently, our trade introduced us to a formidable woman - Jing Lang, a pirate from the farthest seas of the Orient.

speaker: Edward
en: Intriguing.

speaker: Upton
en: She and Vance quickly became inseparable.

speaker: Edward
en: Any reason he should have thought your men were spies?

speaker: Upton
en: Well, there is the treasure.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh?

speaker: Upton
en: A pirate sold us a map. We each kept half. Come. I will meet him now. If you follow with discretion, you may hear it for yourself. Follow me at a distance. If anyone sees you, tell them you are my bodyguard. There are thieves about who would stop at nothing to secure either half of the map. Hide until Vance arrives. Hide there. Follow me when Vance arrives. Go. Hide. When he arrives, follow me. Hide! He'll be here soon.

speaker: Vance
en: Good day, my brother.

speaker: Upton
en: Good day, "brother" if I may still call you that.

speaker: Vance
en: Why, what else would you call me?

speaker: Upton
en: Stranger, perhaps? I barely know you anymore. And if the whispers around town are to be believed you would have me gone and done away with.

speaker: Vance
en: Upton, come, you know better than to give in to gossip. Nassau is too small. Local tongues turn everything to sentimental comedy.

speaker: Upton
en: It's domestic tragedy I'm trying to avoid.

speaker: Vance
en: Well said, brother. No stronger bonds than family -- except business and goodness knows we have more than enough of that between ourselves.

speaker: Upton
en: That is true, brother. That is very true. And what a business it is! I'm sure neither of us would ever do anything to upset the balance of things.

speaker: Vance
en: Quite. Quite. Now tell me. Have you brought it?

speaker: Upton
en: It? My half of the map, you mean?

speaker: Vance
en: The map, the map, of course the map!

speaker: Upton
en: The map to the treasure? To our legacy?

speaker: Vance
en: That very one. I have mine. Where is yours?

speaker: Upton
en: Vance, you know I feel we must protect that treasure with utmost caution.

speaker: Vance
en: On the contrary! That map IS our protection; its treasure, our freedom.

speaker: Upton
en: All the more reason to keep it buried. Safely.

speaker: Vance
en: But have you no imagination? Can you not imagine the luxurious life that awaits us once we unearth its bounty?

speaker: Upton
en: I really don't think

speaker: Vance
en: The Travers Estate and Plantations. No more smuggling. No more organizing men. No shipments. No risk. Why not begin now?

speaker: Upton
en: But Vance, are you sure your future will unfold so easily?

speaker: Vance
en: What do you mean? What are you implying?

speaker: Upton
en: I am not implying. I am merely asking. Do you really imagine Jing as the lady of the house? Mistress of servants, brood mother?

speaker: Vance
en: Why should I not imagine it? Do you question her love? Her fitness?

speaker: Upton
en: Of course not. But knowing her as you do, you must appreciate that she is a woman of action. She needs the sea, a challenge. How will she adapt to a quiet, domestic life?

speaker: Vance
en: Jing is none of your concern.

speaker: Upton
en: Vance, do you intend to marry her?

speaker: Vance
en: Of course.

speaker: Upton
en: It pains me to tell you, but I do not believe she will consent to it.

speaker: Vance
en: Oh? And what gives you such insight into her heart?

speaker: Upton
en: In addition to her nature, I simply do not believe she is exactly what she says she is.

speaker: Vance
en: You're jealous.

speaker: Upton
en: Jealous? No

speaker: Vance
en: Yes!

speaker: Upton
en: I only worry for your safety, brother.

speaker: Vance
en: You always had to be the favored child, the golden boy. You can't stand it that she would give her heart to me, when she can't even give you a second glance! So you hate her!

speaker: Upton
en: I have no hate. Only concern.

speaker: Vance
en: I'll tell you this: I will marry her. I will kill you if I must, I will have your half of the map. And then the world will see which brother has more honour. I bid you good day!

speaker: Vance
en: My love.

speaker: Jing
en: Do you have the map?

speaker: Vance
en: Not yet. Not yet.

speaker: Jing
en: What am I to tell my Order? You know we can't leave until I have it!

speaker: Vance
en: I am taking care of it. Give me time.

speaker: Jing
en: More time? Your loyalty makes you soft. I think you are not man enough to see it through.

speaker: Vance
en: My flower, it is all but done. I have hired a man. In moments, Upton's life will be over and the map will be ours.

speaker: Jing
en: You hired a man? In your scriptures, did Cain hire a man? No, Cain was a man. "Come to the field" he said to Abel and he did it himself. He did not require a third man to carry the axe.

speaker: Vance
en: He did not have so many witnesses as we do in Nassau. Trust me. He is doing it now.

speaker: Jing
en: Right this moment?

speaker: Vance
en: Nothing can save him now.

speaker: Upton
en: Edward?

speaker: Edward
en: I believe I just saved your life, mate.

speaker: Upton
en: Vance. He said he would kill me. I thought it was bluster. He is my brother. Despite what you told me, I thought it meant something.

speaker: Edward
en: You're safe for now. But perhaps a trip away from Nassau would do you some good.

speaker: Leader
en: Nothing but lobcocks running this shantytown nowadays. It's time for us to make our move. Take back what we fairly built up. Aye. No more knocking about the empty barrel. Nassau should be ours, plain as the nose on my face.

speaker: Edward
en: What the hell did I just see back there? Jim!

speaker: Kidd
en: Quiet!

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: The statue in the temple. Was that the man you saw in Havana?

speaker: Edward
en: Spitting likeness, aye.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: It seems another Sage has been found, the race for the Observatory begins anew.

speaker: Edward
en: Is that why we're whispering?

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: This is your doing, Captain Kenway. The maps you sold to the Templars have led them straight to us. And now the agents of two empires know exactly where we operate.

speaker: Kidd
en: Leave this to me, Mentor.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: They have taken Edward's crew as well. I wonder what their lives are worth to him?

speaker: Kidd
en: Take this. You'll attract no attention, and take fewer lives.

speaker: Kidd
en: Use them darts on this one coming now. Quick! Quiet and effective, see?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: You seen this temple here? It's massive.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Aye. I'm wondering if it's full of gold and jade and the like.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Has to be, don't it? Where else would the Dagos get it?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: They're pulling it out of the ground, aren't they?

speaker: Crew members
en: Ease off, mate. You ain't got nothing on us. I was a navy man once, but I found a better life sailing under a black flag. And you could too, mate.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Looks to me like a crew of pirates here.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Aye. Mixing with these heathens. Makes me bloody sick.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: God's truth, I can't fathom why.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Can't handle living among men, can they? Can't handle the Christian life. So they come here.

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Who's this Dutch fella we brought here? What a sourpuss he is.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: A slaver named Prins. I'm told he has a letter of marque from Governor Hamilton. And that we're to afford him every courtesy.

speaker: Soldier 5
en: That's a queer combination.

speaker: Assassin 3
en: (You walk the dark road to Xibalba, soldier. May you turn back before your life is corrupted.)

speaker: Soldier 6
en: All I know is that he's looking for someone and we're to help him find it.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: If only you lads knew what was coming to you, I think you'd pack your kits and run.

speaker: Assassin 4
en: (Leave while you can, English man. Death is certain, otherwise).

speaker: Soldier 7
en: Gah! Carting old misers around ain't what I signed up for.

speaker: Soldier 8
en: You were pressed into service, you nob!

speaker: Assassins
en: Many thanks, but no forgiveness. It was a slaver who brought these soldiers. Laurens Prins himself. I may thank you later, if you manage to live through this. Is it out of kindness you do this, or guilt?

speaker: Crew members
en: Plague and perish if this ever happens again. Death and disease to these slavers. Christ. What a mess, eh? Cheers, captain.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Many thanks, breddah.

speaker: Edward
en: Who's out there?

speaker: Kidd
en: See that mangy old codger? He's a Dutch slaver called Laurens Prins. Living now like a king in Jamaica. Bastard's been a target for years. Bloody hell, we nearly had him!

speaker: Edward
en: By God, you bravos are a cheery bunch eh. All frowns and furrowed brows.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Captain Kenway. You have remarkable skills.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah, thanks, mate. It comes natural.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: But you are churlish and arrogant, prancing around in a uniform that you have not earned.

speaker: Edward
en: Everything is permitted. Isn't that your motto?

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: I absolve you of your errors in Havana and elsewhere, but you are not welcome here.

speaker: Kidd
en: Sorry, mate. Wish it were otherwise.

speaker: Edward
en: Cheery bunch of mates you've got.

speaker: Kidd
en: You deserve scorn, Edward. Prancing about like one of us, bringing shame to our cause.

speaker: Edward
en: And what is that? Your cause?

speaker: Kidd
en: To be blunt... we kill people. Templars and their associates. Folks who'd like to control all the empires on Earth... claiming it's in the name of peace and order.

speaker: Edward
en: Sounds like Du Casse's dying words.

speaker: Kidd
en: You see? It's about power really. About lording over people. Robbing us of liberty.

speaker: Edward
en: That another message from one of your friends?

speaker: Kidd
en: Aye. I'll show you. I know you ain't exactly impressed by our Creed. So would the sight of money make you more friendly to our ways?

speaker: Edward
en: As ever.

speaker: Kidd
en: Then work these contracts around the West Indies for us, and we'll pay you. As simple as that. Now follow on. I have one last secret to share.

speaker: Edward
en: How long have you been one of these Assassins, eh?

speaker: Kidd
en: A couple years, now. I met Ah Tabai in Spanish-Towne, and there was something about him I trusted. A sort of... wisdom.

speaker: Edward
en: Is all this his idea? His clan?

speaker: Kidd
en: No, sir. The Assassins and Templars have been at war for thousands of years, all over the world. The natives of this new world had a philosophy like our creed for as long as they've been here. And when Europeans arrived, our groups sort of... matched up. Cultures and religions and languages keep folks divided. But there's something in the Assassin's Creed that crosses all boundaries. A fondness for life and liberty.

speaker: Edward
en: Sounds a bit like Nassau, no?

speaker: Kidd
en: Close. But not quite. Here we are. Take that stone you discovered from the Mayan stele, and put it there.

speaker: Kidd
en: That's one. Couple dozen more and you're in.

speaker: Edward
en: And what will all this effort gain me?

speaker: Kidd
en: Respect, for a start. From the men and women you put in danger here. And if that ain't enough, there's a treasure behind that door. Something many centuries old. I reckon if you made the effort to find every last one of those, it'd be worth your while.

speaker: Edward
en: So, you sailing back to Nassau?

speaker: Kidd
en: When I have another contract there, aye. But this is my home for now.

speaker: Papers, Please
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: A Personal Matter
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Mancomb
en: I'll rise up when I'm good and ready, take the island for myself. Then all the world will know my name. Captain Mancomb Seepgood, terror of the high seas. Don't nobody mess with Mancomb Seepgood, for I'm the fiercest rogue to sail these West Indies. Captain Seepgood's coming! The women'll say with a trill sounding somewhere's between fear and lust. Oh yes. I'll never surrender, and never back down. And these shankers who think they run the island, do so only because I haven't yet objected. Who'd dare challenge me? I can't imagine such a man. I don't believe such a one exists.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: You know how he killed Grandad? Shot him with his own gold Pistols. Can you believe that? I don't understand what my Mother ever saw in him.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: What happened to your Mother?

speaker: Lucy
en: Dead since I was young. Poisoned. Grandad had a lot of enemies. They couldn't get to him, so... they got her. She always wore a Gold Locket with a Likeness of me in it. It was gone when they found her. Whoever killed her took it. It was a paltry Trinket, and had no value. They didn't even leave me that.

speaker: Edward
en: That's cold, even for a Pirate.

speaker: Lucy
en: I tell you what, this Rum's given me a fierce taste for some Plantain.

speaker: Edward
en: That I can remedy.

speaker: British civilian 1
en: Miss Lucy! Glad to see you back.

speaker: Edward
en: You seem to be settling in.

speaker: Lucy
en: People like me.

speaker: British civilian 2
en: Lucy! Come drink with us.

speaker: Lucy
en: Next time. I'm with the Captain.

speaker: Lucy
en: I hear you're a Climber.

speaker: Edward
en: What are you getting at?

speaker: Lucy
en: A small Wager. A race to the Villa.

speaker: Edward
en: So long as you're not averse to being embarrassed... hey!

speaker: Edward
en: You're faster than you look.

speaker: Lucy
en: Keep your sideways Insults. You're slower than you look. You're going to lose this one.

speaker: Edward
en: Almost there!

speaker: Lucy
en: All right. You won.

speaker: Edward
en: You weren't so bad.

speaker: Lucy
en: Don't.

speaker: Edward
en: A fair Win. Though I took too much Rum.

speaker: Lucy
en: That's what it was. The Rum.

speaker: Edward
en: Food and a View. A just Prize.

speaker: Lucy
en: This whole place reminds me of...

speaker: Lucy
en: Grandad owned a lot of Stuff in his Day. But these he prized above all else. Is it not strange that the things he treasured most were what killed him?

speaker: Edward
en: I didn't peg you as Sentimental.

speaker: Lucy
en: You can't deny the devilish Symmetry. My Father killed Grandad, I killed him... all of it done with these.

speaker: Lucy
en: Here. You earned them.

speaker: Edward
en: I won't take your Grandfather's prize Pistols.

speaker: Lucy
en: Will you not? I trust you know the difference between won't and can't, because I can't.

speaker: Lucy
en: Take them! You'll never find better. Try not to be a Baby about it.

speaker: Master
en: Caught filching the very produce you've been charged to gather! Damn you, brutes.

speaker: Slave 1
en: No disrespect, sir!

speaker: Master
en: By God, I'll sweeten you, boy. I'll sweeten you good and proper!

speaker: Slave 2
en: Please, sir. I meant nothing by it.

speaker: Master
en: Cast your eyes off me, cur. I'll not be stared at by the likes of you.

speaker: Slave 2
en: God, keep you, sir.

speaker: Master
en: What shall we do with you lot, eh? What indeed?

speaker: Slave 1
en: Begging your pardon.

speaker: The Poachers
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Private Escort
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Thatch
en: Morning, Kenway.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Not a bad looking tinderbox you got there.

speaker: Edward
en: You sound a bit green, Hornigold. Is it envy? Because mine's bigger than yours?

speaker: Hornigold
en: No, I reckon it's this Jamaican funk. I prefer the Spanish stuff. So you've got yourself a fancy brig now. Fine. Well I'm going to teach you how to sail her right, and how to take a prize the proper way. Thatch, we'll catch you up at the old fishing village.

speaker: Thatch
en: Aye.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Where's your helmsman, Kenway?

speaker: Edward
en: I take pride in piloting my own ships, Ben. Keeps me alert.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Let's make some headway, shall we?

speaker: Edward
en: I've no need for schooling. How many prizes did we take together as privateers?

speaker: Hornigold
en: There's a chasm of difference between joining a raid, and captaining one. We're looking out for merchants, boys. Them that's fat with cargo. Find us a schooner with that spyglass, Kenway. You'll get yourself a glimpse of what sort of cargo they're shipping, and a general idea of their toughness. You won't find nothing squinting into the sun like that. Use your glass. Take out you glass, Kenway. Schooners are too small to peep with a naked eye. Are you trifling with me, lad? Take out your spyglass.

speaker: Edward
en: There's a prize worth taking.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Good! Take us in close. After you subdue a prize, project authority and demand respect that you would never give yourself. This weaves a spell over soft minds. For your victims must always have in the back of their minds the uneasy idea that you could snap at any moment and unseam them from prick to sternum. Fire what cannons you will, and land a few strikes if you must. But for God's sake don't sink her. It's no fun fishing cargo out of the sea. Although it can be done.

speaker: Hornigold
en: She's disabled now and taking on a decent amount of water. So keep your cannons quiet, and take care not to sink her. Ho ho! She's dead in the water. Steer up along side her. Lay up alongside her.

speaker: Hornigold
en: ¡Que tanga un buen día, señor! (Good day to you, sir!) I am Captain Hornigold and this is my crew. We're sailors like yourselves, but quite unalike in our purpose. For we intend to take all that you own. Yet no harm shall befall any man, so long as he remains at ease. Is that clear?

speaker: Soldier
en: ¡No me mate, señor! Tengo familia. ¡Se lo suplico! (Don't kill me, sir! I have a family. Please!)

speaker: Hornigold
en: Anyone speak English? ¿Inglés? (English?)

speaker: Soldier
en: Little bit.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Tell your friends we're stealing your goods. And we won't hurt nobody if everyone stays as still as a sandbar. You got that?

speaker: Soldier
en: Ah... uh... Please to repeat?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Oh, for fuck's sake. Lock 'em in the hold, and take everything that isn't nailed down.

speaker: Edward
en: It's a shaky feeling sailing around with this much stolen cargo.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Get used to it. We'll need to take a few more prizes to make this a profitable day.

speaker: Hornigold
en: A good take today, Kenway. Half-a-dozen scores of that size and you'll be set for a year. Now let's sell this cargo and fix up your Jackdaw with a few more trinkets.

speaker: Edward
en: Sod a year. I'm looking for a prize that'll set me up for life. I'll be king of the West Indies then.

speaker: Hornigold
en: We came to Nassau to get away from the likes of kings.

speaker: Edward
en: Well... I'll be a man of property and promise anyway.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Jaysus, let that dream go, lad. Nassau is the place to be, not England.

speaker: Edward
en: Do you ever dream of the big score? A ship so full of gold and silver you just split it and sail home?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Sure, but it's only a dream. Every man hopes to find a dozen chests of gold with no owners, but they're as rare as an honest king.

speaker: Thatch
en: Here's to our pirate republic, lads. We're prosperous and free, and out of the reach of kings, clergy, and debt collectors.

speaker: Kidd
en: Near five-hundred men now pledge their allegiance to the brethren of the coast in Nassau. Not a bad number.

speaker: Thatch
en: Truth. Yet we lack sturdy defences. If the King were to attack the town, he'd trample us.

speaker: Edward
en: Then let us find the Observatory. If it does what these Templars claim, we'll be unbeatable.

speaker: Thatch
en: Not that twaddle again, Kenway! That's a story for schoolboys. I mean proper defences. Steal a galleon, shift all the guns to one side. Would make a nice ornament for one of our harbours.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: It will not be easy to steal a full Spanish galleon. Have you one in mind?

speaker: Thatch
en: I do, sir. And I'll show you. She's a fussock she is. Fat and slow.

speaker: Thatch
en: Your Jackdaw handles nice. Pinched her from the Spanish, was it?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, in the midst of a hurricane.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Just before the treasure fleet was smashed against the shore.

speaker: Thatch
en: Was the haul aboard as rich as men are saying?

speaker: Edward
en: A thousand times that. I reckon a million pounds worth of reales were sunk that day.

speaker: Thatch
en: Devil love a hurricane! Might have a dive there one day. See what we can rummage up.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Diving them wrecks would be a nice change of pace for us. No need for violent actions against merchants and such.

speaker: Thatch
en: Well! That's some soft talk coming from a pirate. And as it happens... I mostly agree. We'll save the clashing of cutlasses for the military, and them that get in our way. Easy as she goes. No telling what you may find out here.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Like staring through a waterfall.

speaker: Edward
en: Don't soil your breeches, lads. I got this.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: That ship's a monster! Look at the size of her!

speaker: Thatch
en: Aye. And we'd not last long face to face with her. You hear that, Kenway? Keep your distance, and we'll strike when fortune favors us.

speaker: Edward
en: Under cover of darkness, most likely.

speaker: Thatch
en: Aye, it may come to that.

speaker: Thatch
en: Charles Vane. He's as reckless as they come.

speaker: Edward
en: An old friend of yours?

speaker: Thatch
en: Not a man I'd call a friend. But we've been doing this kind of work for so long, I can't help but respect the man.

speaker: Thatch
en: Charles Vane, slinking off with his tail between his legs. That's good news for us.

speaker: Thatch
en: Bleeding bastards! We'll have to deal with this skirmish fast. Forget the galleon and send these interlopers to hell.

speaker: Edward
en: She's sailing for that island.

speaker: Thatch
en: I know the place. A natural stronghold used by a French captain named Du Casse.

speaker: Edward
en: Julien du Casse? The Templar?

speaker: Thatch
en: Name's right. Didn't know he had a title.

speaker: Edward
en: I know the man. And if he sees my ship, he'll know it from his time in Havana. Meaning he may wonder at who's sailing her now. I can't risk that.

speaker: Thatch
en: And I don't want to lose that galleon. Let's think on it... and maybe wait till it's dark before hopping aboard.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Edward
en: Hm, you're looking better than last we met.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Upton
en: As I sobered up, I began to see it more clearly. Jing has led my brother astray, and must be killed. But Vance has also betrayed me. As an Assassin his treachery must be punished by death.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Edward
en: So either way, one of them has the Templar key. You're obviously distraught. Let me take care of it.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Upton
en: I will tell you where to find them.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Vance
en: Traitor!

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Edward
en: It takes one to know one.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Edward
en: Jing Lang, as I live and breathe!

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Jing
en: I told him not to hire you! You traitor! I will not meet the same fate.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Jing
en: Imagine. The Queen of Pirates, Jing Lang, defeated for a fake map. I have been arrogant.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Edward
en: Really?

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Jing
en: Yes. I stole the real one. Both halves. My husband has it.

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Edward
en: Your husband?

scene: Queen of Pirates, King of Fools
speaker: Jing
en: A better man than these fools.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Not a bad take today. Keep this up and Nassau'll be the first city where men and women may live as God made them: easy and free. All it takes is a few drops of blood, sweat and a swath of cloth.

speaker: Thatch
en: We fly no colours out here, but praise the lack of 'em. So let the black flag signal nothing but your allegiance to man's natural freedoms. This one's yours. Fly it proud.

speaker: Edward
en: I will.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Hand over the docket I lent you. If we're to keep our republic afloat, we'll need guns as well as gold.

speaker: Edward
en: That means attacking the Navy.

speaker: Hornigold
en: So long as they're flying King Philip's colours, we'll not offend our own monarch.

speaker: Hornigold
en: As you've likely seen, the number of merchants roving these waters is three score the number of military ships.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Easy purchase, but in small doses.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Right. So to lure the Navy out of hiding, it's best to cause a bit of mischief.

speaker: Edward
en: Catch a few small fish to attract the big ones.

speaker: Hornigold
en: That's right. So plunder and pillage as you see fit, Captain Kenway.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Sail ho! Military-class brig on the horizon.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Good eye, man. Are you ready for this, Kenway? For she won't go down without an honest fight.

speaker: Edward
en: Who's up for taking that brig, lads! Shout "Aye"! That's a sound I like to hear. Pipe to quarters! All hands to cannons!

speaker: Hornigold
en: Careful around the Navy. They're as likely to ram you as fire a broadside.

speaker: Edward
en: Let's test those powder barrels against them, shall we?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Aye. Good thinking.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Over the top, lads! Kick 'em in the hams and give 'em a taste of British steel!

speaker: Edward
en: That was a rumble, by God. How'd we fare?

speaker: Hornigold
en: A fine purchase, no mistake! Now I think it's time to lay low and bribe our way back into secrecy.

speaker: Edward
en: Agreed. So how do we get rid of this notoriety we've stirred up?

speaker: Hornigold
en: Money, my boy. A well placed bribe to the right government official will see the military off your tail.

speaker: Edward
en: Right. Let's do that. I'll need to meet these good Samaritans at some point.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Smart thinking.

speaker: Hornigold
en: You're a wonder, Kenway. You've a knack for this kind of work.

speaker: Edward
en: It ain't work if you love it.

speaker: Thatch
en: Ah! Ah! Tosh!

speaker: Edward
en: But I ain't doing this forever, lads. Only until I get enough coin to buy some land and influence back home.

speaker: Hornigold
en: Jaysus, will you listen to your tripe? Still dreaming on about that strumpet back in England, when you could have any Betty you wanted, here and now.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah, such lofty goals for you gents. And here I thought I was in the company of scoundrels. A fine purchase today. What's the crew's mood?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: All smiles and no teeth. And there's a few talking about meeting with Master Kidd to steal from a nearby plantation.

speaker: Edward
en: A plantation? That's ambitious.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Profitable too, if we can manage it.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. It's a good idea.

speaker: The Realities of War
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Edward
en: I found your men.

speaker: Antó
en: And I found where his brothers are kept. Help me release them.

speaker: Edward
en: No, mate. I've settled my debt. Meddling with slaves is none of my affair. I doubt there's even a Templar behind it all.

speaker: Antó
en: All affairs of freedom are Assassins' affairs! What is your price?

speaker: Edward
en: What?

speaker: Antó
en: A man without principle must be moved by coin. How much do you need?

speaker: Edward
en: There is a key I'm looking for. Belongs to a set I've been stripping off Templars.

speaker: Antó
en: The Templar keys? I thought they'd been destroyed.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm not the only one who knows about them, then?

speaker: Antó
en: If we find it, it's yours.

speaker: Edward
en: You have a deal. Let's go get your friends.

speaker: Antó
en: The drunks and whores you call friends might help you now. Look for a hole in the fence. We'll catch them unawares.

speaker: Guard 1
en: What's this? Only survivor?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Only captive.

speaker: Guard 1
en: You didn't... lose... the battle then?

speaker: Guard 2
en: How can we win when the dogs hole up in the mountain? They just hide in caves and wait. See us coming every time.

speaker: Guard 1
en: I hope commander Abraham knows what he's doing.

speaker: Guard 2
en: I've no doubt he'll win in the end. I'll follow him to my death!

speaker: Slave
en: Thank you.

speaker: Antó
en: Hurry! To my bureau.

speaker: Guard 3
en: We had a hundred men, and they... we couldn't even see them to count them.

speaker: Guard 4
en: What kind of weapons they got in them there caves?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Knives and axes mostly. A little gunpowder, not much. Barely more than sticks and rocks.

speaker: Guard 4
en: And yet this is the only man you could capture.

speaker: Guard 3
en: The only one!

speaker: Guard 4
en: They must be backed by some strange African magic. Curses and voodoo.

speaker: Guard 3
en: It's just not Christian.

speaker: Slave
en: At last.

speaker: Antó
en: Go to the bureau.

speaker: Antó
en: You must exercise caution. The area will be well-guarded. You know how this works. Take your position. Over here! Hey! Ho there!

speaker: Slave
en: Thanks.

speaker: Antó
en: Meet me at the bureau.

speaker: Edward
en: Where to, next?

speaker: Antó
en: That's enough work for one night. Or do you grow fond of it?

speaker: Edward
en: That's it? No Templar? What about the key?

speaker: Antó
en: The Templar did not show himself. You will have your key next time.

speaker: Edward
en: No, Antó, there is no next time.

speaker: Antó
en: When you discover your conscience or admit how badly you want the key, there will be a next time.

speaker: Opía
en: Were you successful?

speaker: Edward
en: I kept overhearing this name - Márquez. Friend of yours?

speaker: Opía
en: Her name matches that of the man who destroyed our village. We fought and lost, but the leader did not live to enjoy his victory.

speaker: Edward
en: You think this woman is related?

speaker: Opía
en: If she is, we are not safe.

speaker: Edward
en: The bill of sale we stole gives the address of a man in her employ, Vargas.

speaker: Opía
en: I saw. I know where it is.

speaker: Edward
en: Let's pay the bait boy a visit and find out what he knows.

speaker: Opía
en: Follow us. You must try to understand what it is at stake.

speaker: Edward
en: I've got some idea...

speaker: Opía
en: No. It's more than your key. There are those who say the Taíno are already extinct. But we will never be extinguished. Our fight continues.

speaker: Opía
en: Here it is. The home of Vargas. Hide. We'll use the element of surprise to our advantage. Get out of sight. (Hello!)

speaker: Vargas
en: State your business.

speaker: Opía
en: I hope for an audience with Señorita Márquez.

speaker: Opía
en: Chase him!

speaker: Opía
en: We're coming with you! He's getting away! Hurry, keep after him! Don't let him get away! Don't sink him! We need the man and the ship intact. If he drowns we'll lose Márquez! We've got him! Board his ship! Board him, and make him talk! What are you waiting for? Board it!

speaker: Edward
en: Out with it, lad. Where's Márquez! Why's she here?

speaker: Vargas
en: She's already left for Juventud. Find her there if you must. Her army will teach you a lesson.

speaker: Opía
en: Juventud is the island of our enemies. If Lucia Márquez has gone there, it is certain we are her target.

speaker: Edward
en: How many enemies do you have?

speaker: Opía
en: When you are hunted, it sometimes seems that every stranger is an enemy. On Juventud, we have been at truce since the death of the first Márquez, but this woman could re-ignite our dispute, if her price is high enough.

speaker: Edward
en: Uh, can't have that.

speaker: Opía
en: I'll take this ship. Meet me there, if you still want your key.

speaker: Anne
en: Captain! Here's one still kicking!

speaker: Edward
en: Who did this?

speaker: Sailor
en: It were a large vessel. The Royal Fortune.

speaker: Edward
en: Roberts.

speaker: Sailor
en: Offered no quarter. Didn't say nothing.

speaker: Roberts
en: Why, who chases me now, eh? Is it a specter come to spook me? Or the gaunt remains of a man I sent to hell!

speaker: Anne
en: Come on now! Captain's aboard! Man all canvas! Let's move!

speaker: Anne
en: The way is blocked, captain! We'll have to find another path! Steer clear of that, captain! Edward! There's crosstrees on the horizon!

speaker: Crew
en: Flying British colours!

speaker: Anne
en: There's Spanish ships there, captain! This'll be a mess if we don't hurry. We're in a maelstrom, captain!

speaker: Edward
en: Beats working behind a bar, don't it?

speaker: Anne
en: Shall we sink his ship, captain? We've a better than even chance!

speaker: Edward
en: No. There's a device with him that needs taking. I'll have to board her myself.

speaker: Roberts
en: Man the guns! There's more fodder for ya coming!

speaker: Roberts
en: By jove, Edward Kenway! How can I not be impressed by the attention you've paid me! May the best of we two sing praises of the second!

speaker: Roberts
en: A merry life and a short one, as promised. How well I know myself. And what of you, Edward? Have you found the peace you seek?

speaker: Edward
en: I'm not aiming so high as that. For what's peace but a confusion between two wars?

speaker: Roberts
en: You're a stoic then! Perhaps I was wrong about you. She might have had some use for you after all.

speaker: Edward
en: She? Of whom do you speak?

speaker: Roberts
en: Oh... she who lies in wait. Entombed. I had hoped to find her, to see her again. To open the door of the temple and hear her speak my name once more. Aita...

speaker: Edward
en: Talk sense, man.

speaker: Roberts
en: I was born too soon, like so many others before.

speaker: Edward
en: Where's the device, Roberts?

speaker: Roberts
en: Destroy this body, Edward. The Templars... if they take me...

speaker: Edward
en: You walked me blind and backwards into this mess, Kidd! Who the hell was that jester back there?

speaker: Kidd
en: Ah Tabai, an Assassin. And my Mentor.

speaker: Edward
en: So you're all part of some daffy religion?

speaker: Kidd
en: We're Assassins and we follow a Creed, aye. But it does not command us to act or submit... only to be wise.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh. Do tell. I'd love to hear it.

speaker: Kidd
en: "Nothing is true, everything is permitted." This is the world's only certainty.

speaker: Edward
en: "Everything is permitted?" I like the sound of that. Thinking what I like, and acting how I please.

speaker: Kidd
en: You parrot the words... but you do not understand them.

speaker: Edward
en: Don't get haughty with me, Kidd. I followed you as a friend, and you tricked me.

speaker: Kidd
en: I saved your skin bringing you here, man. These men wanted you dead for what you did in Havana. I talked 'em out of it.

speaker: Edward
en: Well cheers for that.

speaker: Kidd
en: Aye. Cheers.

speaker: Kidd
en: Ah! The way forward's blocked.

speaker: Edward
en: That's a door, I reckon.

speaker: Kidd
en: Aye. And there should be some way to open it. A mechanism somewhere...

speaker: Edward
en: Like a capstan?

speaker: Kidd
en: Hm. Those blocks up there. Try moving them.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah! Dammit!

speaker: Kidd
en: Easy, Kenway! This ain't like climbing ratlines! Those blocks up there seem like they might move with a bit weight.

speaker: Edward
en: So it's you lot them Templars have been chasing, then?

speaker: Kidd
en: Until you came along and mucked things up, it was us chasing them. We had them running scared. But they have the upper hand now. The door's mechanism seems to be broke. Let's find another way 'round. Follow on, man! Jump!

speaker: Kidd
en: You still drawing breath?

speaker: Edward
en: Enough to curse you with, Kidd!

speaker: Edward
en: Must be a great treasure beyond.

speaker: Kidd
en: Treasure. Right.

speaker: Edward
en: Whatever is waiting at the end of this path had better be worth my time.

speaker: Kidd
en: That'll depend on you.

speaker: Edward
en: How's that?

speaker: Kidd
en: What I'm taking you to see may spin your head right 'round. I only hope you can take the shock of it.

speaker: Edward
en: I can handle myself.

speaker: Edward
en: Is this IT then? The grand prize your Mentor asked me to see? Looks nothing like the man they called the Sage, I'm sorry to say.

speaker: Kidd
en: Keep your trousers tied up. We've one more riddle to solve. These statues are like the ones we've seen before, but with pictures carved on them.

speaker: Edward
en: There's pictures carved on the floor as well, but not of the same sort.

speaker: Kidd
en: There's a correspondence then. But what...? There's a difference between them animals on the statues and them on the floor. Dor you see it?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. One group is predators, the other is prey.

speaker: Kidd
en: Which predator goes with this prey, that's the question.

speaker: Edward
en: Right. There's your correspondence. Match a predator with its prey.

speaker: Kidd
en: Might be you can use the lever to move them drawings on the ground.

speaker: Edward
en: I was just about to say the same.

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus. That's him. The Sage. But this thing must be hundreds of years old.

speaker: Kidd
en: Older still. You're certain it's him?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. It's the eyes that mark him.

speaker: Kidd
en: Did the Templars say why they wanted this Sage?

speaker: Edward
en: They drew some of his blood into this small glass cube.

speaker: Kidd
en: Like this one?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. They meant to ask him about the Observatory too, but he escaped.

speaker: Kidd
en: Hm. We're finished here.

speaker: Shady Business
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Associate
en: (It's Dutchmen we're expecting today, so don't imagine they'll be on time! Ah, if only Torres could have been here to conduct this himself... Move your feet faster than your lips, you lazy donkeys! Tidy the place up! Come, now!)

speaker: Edward
en: Heyo, Bonnet. Flying your own flag at last!

speaker: Stede
en: Yes... Yes, Blackbeard cut me loose sadly. Time to have a go at this myself.

speaker: Edward
en: Well, that's grand!

speaker: Stede
en: Yes, it's for the best, I think. I should have some wild stories when next we meet. Edward... your constant friendship has been my most treasured find on these seas. Well above gold and silver and rum, I... I prize the courage you have inspired in me this year. Thank you, Sir! A fair good morrow to you!

speaker: Thatch
en: Are you not loved at home? Are you not wanted by your wives and families and countrymen? How else to explain your government's complete disinterest in your well-being? Hostages for medicines, these were my only terms! And yet, six days of pure fucking silence! So I must conclude that you men are the pariahs of Charles-Towne, and I would profit better by using your organs for chum and your bones for char! By Christ! This is my predicament: to kill ya, or to press you into my service. It's a decision I'll make hardly, but not with remorse. Ahoy, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: What the hell are you doing, man? All of Charles-Towne can see this mess.

speaker: Thatch
en: It's the idea. Out of range but well in sight.

speaker: Edward
en: So where's the medicine?

speaker: Thatch
en: I sent a party ashore to barter with the . That were a week ago. No noise since.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll handle it. Give me a day.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: There's movement up ahead. Is it soldiers?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, and in something of a hurry. I propose we follow... else they spring something we ain't ready for.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What's your thinking?

speaker: Edward
en: Blackbeard's been at this eight days already, so it's a good bet someone out there has prepared the medicines, just in case.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Ah. But they're stalling, thinking up ways to avoid paying it out.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. So let's find where they've gathered and hope for the best.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Careful, captain. We're drifting close to a watchtower.

speaker: Crew
en: The Jackdaw's got no business sailing such shallow waters.

speaker: Crew
en: It'll be a bloody miracle if we ain't spotted.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: There's another watchtower.

speaker: Crew
en: What's the captain thinking? If this fog shifts, we'll have nowhere to turn.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Keep her at half-sail, captain. Speed'll do us no favors here. Careful with the banks. We cannot pass them undetected, captain. And there is no other way.

speaker: Edward
en: There's always another way.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: All stop!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I see them. Over there! Let us hope the river remains this wide.

speaker: Crew
en: This ship's built for the open ocean, not stalking bayous.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: If we run aground here, we may never get out. Be sure they don't spy us trailing them. Steady as she goes, captain. They're getting away, captain!

speaker: Edward
en: Then I'll have to go on without her. I'll be back with the medicines.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye, sir!

speaker: Ryder
en: It's your turn at the oars.

speaker: Soldier
en: The devil it is. I rowed last time.

speaker: Ryder
en: Aye, and wagered your next turn on a poor hand of cards, as I recall.

speaker: Soldier
en: Blast! So I did.

speaker: Ryder
en: Come on then. The captain's waiting. If heat or the reptiles don't finish us, it'll be these damnable insects.

speaker: Soldier
en: Aye, the mosquitoes'll sup every last ounce of vitality from us. You think it's true what they say about Blackbeard? That fire strikes out from his head? As if some volcano?

speaker: Ryder
en: If he's not the devil himself, then surely he's made some pact with hell. Only be thankful his ship remains anchored, and hasn't torn a path into the heart of Charles-Towne.

speaker: Soldier
en: Bloody pirates. Someone ought to do something.

speaker: Ryder
en: They'll be hunted down eventually. Every last one of them.

speaker: Guard
en: Who's that there?

speaker: Ryder
en: Two old 'gators come for their supper.

speaker: Guard
en: Ryder, me old mucker. Bit warm tonight, ain't it?

speaker: Ryder
en: We'll talk about the weather another time, mate. Bit of a hurry. This blockade best end soon. I'm going land-crazy, and this dirty puddle won't do.

speaker: Soldier
en: One would suppose all this was for gold. Or rum at least.

speaker: Ryder
en: Nothing but medicines to cure whatever ailments fester aboard their vessels.

speaker: Soldier
en: Syphilis and scurvy, no doubt. What noxious coffins these pirate ships must be. What was that?! It was a crocodile, wasn't it? It's coming straight for us, I can feel it.

speaker: Soldier
en: You seen any crocodiles tonight? I could've sworn I saw something pass the boat.

speaker: Guard
en: Nope, quiet night.

speaker: Soldier
en: Are you sure? I heard something in the water.

speaker: Guard
en: Quiet 'till you showed up. Go on then. Captain's waiting.

speaker: Soldier
en: Almost there.

speaker: Ryder
en: Good. Captain Wyatt is not a patient man.

speaker: Simon
en: Hullo! Is that Ryder yonder?

speaker: Ryder
en: The very same.

speaker: Simon
en: Then speed along. You're expected. And you know how

speaker: Ryder
en: Oh Christ!

speaker: Soldier
en: It took him! It took him! I told you!

speaker: Ryder
en: Just row, for godsakes! Row!

speaker: Soldier
en: I told you there was something! Didn't I tell you? Oh god...

speaker: Ryder
en: Let's just get out of here.

speaker: Soldier
en: Thank Christ! I thought we'd never make it.

speaker: Ryder
en: I apologize, sir. There was an accident. Private Simon-- this crocodile

speaker: Wyatt
en: I don't care about your accidents. What's the word from the harbor, soldier? Speak!

speaker: Ryder
en: No change, sir. They're holding fast but are yet to kill or maim any of the captives, near as we can tell. Perhaps it's time to

speaker: Wyatt
en: To surrender? I've been entrusted with the affairs of the town, and I do not intend to bow to the demands of a pirate, no matter how fierce his reputation.

speaker: Ryder
en: Yes, sir.

speaker: Wyatt
en: As long as the supply key is with me, no man shall touch that medicine. May plague and calamity strike them all.

speaker: Ryder
en: Bloody idiot.

speaker: Wyatt
en: What?

speaker: Guard
en: Pirates! Their ship's here! Pirates!

speaker: Wyatt
en: Fall back! To the mansion!

speaker: Wyatt
en: Intruder! Help! Help! Kill him! Kill him! Stop him! Somebody shoot him! Do something, you fools!

speaker: Soldiers
en: What's going on?! Someone's after the captain! Hey! Stop! He's going for the captain! There's an intruder! Get 'im! Do something! Careful with the gunpowder barrels! Don't hit the gunpowder!

speaker: Wyatt
en: Close the gate!

speaker: Wyatt
en: Oh God! Oh God, save me! And flay all you devils! Ah!

speaker: Edward
en: Blackbeard made you as good an offer as ever a man got from any pirate. You might curse his methods, but medicine was all he wanted. And now he'll get it.

speaker: Edward
en: You should have bartered, mate.

speaker: Crew
en: He's returned, Captain!

speaker: Hostage
en: Mmph!

speaker: Thatch
en: What's the take?

speaker: Edward
en: Two crates, and the means for mixing additional doses.

speaker: Thatch
en: Ah... That's right thinking. Precious little of that these days. You hear that, Mister Wraggs? My young friend returns with offerings, and so saves your scrawny neck! Will you not thank him?

speaker: Hostage
en: Mm hm!

speaker: Edward
en: We should quit these waters, Thatch. The governor is bound to muster more soldiers.

speaker: Thatch
en: Nah, you go on ahead. I got some business in the north.

speaker: Edward
en: You're done, aren't you? Giving up on us? On Nassau?

speaker: Thatch
en: Look, lad. I'm late into my fourth decade on this Earth. And if I don't find some means to make the fifth a quiet and cozy voyage, I'd rather sink to the devil's doorstep than call myself captain another year. We'll meet again, lad. In this world or the one below.

speaker: Silk on the Waves
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Edward
en: Gentlemen!

speaker: Edward
en: As is among our kind, we do not plunge headlong into folly on the orders of a single madman, but act according to our own collective madness! The object of our attention is a square-rigged galleon, and we want her for the advantage she'll bring Nassau. So I'll put it to the vote... All those in favor of storming this cove and taking this ship, stomp and shout "Aye!"

speaker: Crew
en: Aye!

speaker: Edward
en: Those who oppose... whimper "Nay."

speaker: Edward
en: Never was the King's so unified.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: ¿Le has dado a algo? ¿Ves algo? (Did you hit something? Can you see?)

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Si sientes curiosidad, ¿por qué no miras tú? (If you're so curious, why don't you have a look?)

speaker: Edward
en: Swing the Jackdaw 'round to the cove's entrance and make as big a show as you can.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye, captain!

speaker: Edward
en: Damn this wall.

speaker: Edward
en: That was too bloody close.

speaker: African civilian 1
en: They shot him! Right in the head!

speaker: Edward
en: Du Casse hasn't lost any of his charm.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: He's not there. Come on. When we find that rat, I'll gut him.)

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Shall I bring you to the manor then? Mister du Casse is in a foul mood.

speaker: African civilian 2
en: No, please. I have told you all I know.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: If the runaway doesn't show, we'll be back

speaker: Soldier 5
en: (Du Casse's rare pistols have gone missing and they're saying it's my doing.)

speaker: Edward
en: Du Casse is a bit of a dandy.

speaker: African civilian 3
en: Mercy, please! I won't tell a soul.

speaker: Edward
en: Those prisoners may know something I don't.

speaker: Soldier 7
en: (Don't you dare look at me like that. We had an agreement. Your people broke it.)

speaker: *African civilian 3
en: Thank you. Du Casse is a hard master.

speaker: Edward
en: Not for much longer. Where can I find him?

speaker: African civilian 3
en: By the docks. We can take him together.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, I'll catch you up.

speaker: Julien
en: Lively, lads!

speaker: Edward
en: Du Casse may be a snob, but he's got taste.

speaker: Julien
en: Speed along, muchachos (men)! Double time! ¡Vamos, deprisa! (Hurry now)! We've four harbours to hit this week! Eh, oh! Look alive! We'll weigh anchor before dawn! ¡Comed hasta hartaros! (Eat your fill, men)! This is the last time you will see land for a month! Lively, lads! What's happening there? See that the cargo is secure! Move your ass and do your job, (son of a bitch!)

speaker: Julien
en: Filthy thief. I'll drag you straight to the gallows.

speaker: Edward
en: You remember the gift you gave me? Well it answers just fine.

speaker: Julien
en: Fils du putain! (You son of a whore!) As bold as a musket ball, and still half as sharp.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm sorry about this, mate. But I can't risk you telling your Templar friends about me still kicking around.

speaker: Julien
en: I pity you, boucanier (buccaneer). After all you have seen, after all we showed you of our Order, still you embrace the life of an ignorant and aimless rogue.

speaker: Edward
en: What's this...?

speaker: Julien
en: Is petty larceny the extent of your ambition? Have you no mind to comprehend the scope of ours? All the empires on Earth, abolished! A free and opened world, without parasites like you! Que l'enfer que tu trouveras soit le fruit de ton insouciance. (May the hell you find be of your own making.)

speaker: Edward
en: The cove is ours!'

speaker: The Slave Master
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Templar
en: Habitual delays. Shoddy craftsmanship. Penurious sums. I don't know why I bother bartering with you lot.

speaker: Slave trader
en: 'Cause we're the only outfit stupid enough to treat with you Templars.

speaker: Templar
en: Time is of the essence! What is taking so long? Something's wrong here. I can feel it. We're not safe.

speaker: Slave trader
en: Pipe down, you. We'll be done soon.

speaker: Templar
en: Every minute we tarry is a waste of time and breath. Do hurry, won't you!

speaker: Slave trader
en: Quiet.

speaker: Guard
en: How long 'til that bloody ship arrives? I've been here well-nigh two weeks waiting on the Royal African Company to anchor. But all I see are fisherman and drunkards!

speaker: Trevor
en: So much coin to spend, and yet so little cargo!

speaker: The Spanish Commander
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: A Spanish Plague
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Edward
en: Why look! It's the bastard son of the late William Kidd! Still a mere boy, and yet... ten times the demon his father was.

speaker: Kidd
en: Fancy seeing you here, Kenway, still looking sleek and mean. Did you steal that costume from a dandy in Havana?

speaker: Edward
en: No, sir. I found this on a corpse... one that was walking about and talking shite to my face only moments before.

speaker: Kidd
en: Ah...

speaker: Edward
en: So... what's this I hear about a planned raid on a plantation? Not keeping secrets from me, are you?

speaker: Kidd
en: Not very well. Every day schooners packed with sugar sail past, coming from plantations nearby. Most times they stop here to sell off a few crates. There's one man visiting today that'd earn you a fine profit. So if you'd like to rob his plantation, I'll point him out...

speaker: Edward
en: I would. Is it a Mister that owns this plantation?

speaker: Kidd
en: That's the man. Owns dozens 'round these islands. And he's bloody rich.

speaker: Edward
en: Just the sort I like to see robbed.

speaker: Kidd
en: His agent is around here somewhere. Find and follow him, and he'll lead you straight to your prize.

speaker: Agent
en: Yes, yes... We trade at prices Mister Beckford knows are fair. And with a quality he knows is sound.

speaker: Merchant
en: Aye. 'Tis hearty molasses and raw cane. That's a given.

speaker: Agent
en: It gladdens me to hear your saying so. Despite the waywardness of your enterprise here, I understand that you are men of discernment.

speaker: Agent
en: Beauford. Manning. To me. We've done with this place.

speaker: Soldier
en: Aye, sir. What's our course?

speaker: Agent
en: We'll return to the plantation and there take stock of our inventory. It was a good harvest this year.

speaker: Soldier
en: You might not talk so loud sir. This ain't anything like a friendly port, ken?

speaker: Agent
en: Nonsense, man. I had a delightful conversation with a chap just now. We came to quite an understanding.

speaker: Soldier
en: As you say, sir.

speaker: Agent
en: Haul up and unfold, boys. We're going home!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Captain. You have the look of a man crafting a bold idea. A look I've seen before.

speaker: Edward
en: You mark well, Adé. I've just overheard one of the Beckford men talking grandly about his plantation, and all the cargo he's keeping there. And it gave me the idea that I might take these goods off him, and sell them off for a better price than he'd ever ask.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Ah! A man of vision. I like this idea.

speaker: Edward
en: Hold, Adé. There's trouble afore.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I see them!

speaker: Edward
en: This man's working for Peter Beckford's people. Do you know them? The Beckfords and their sugar empire?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye. The Beckfords and the . I never worked their plantations, but I knew their names from hearing other men curse them.

speaker: Edward
en: But you worked a plantation, no?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: A modest one, aye. As a striker in the boiling house.

speaker: Edward
en: Boiling house? Was it water they boiled? Or something else?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Cane juices. It's a hard process making sugar. Dangerous too. Must be why it fetches such a dear price.

speaker: Edward
en: What's it like toiling on a plantation day and night?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Well, with the cane sugar cut and harvested, it's run between two metal rollers that crush the juice from the plant. After collecting the juice, it was time to boil away the waters from the sugar. This we did in taches made of copper. And let me tell you, breddah. Boiling sugar is near the hottest thing on Earth. Just a touch on the skin will stick like and burn on, leaving a terrible scar.

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus.

speaker: Edward
en: It's a risk to anchor too close. The soldiers roving the plantation would catch us for sure.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Drop here, then, and sneak ashore. We'll look after the Jackdaw.

speaker: Agent
en: What's happened here! Why such disarray?

speaker: Guard
en: Bit of a do, sir. That's all. It's Wilmington's birthday.

speaker: Agent
en: And you saw fit to get pickled on duty!

speaker: Guard
en: It's no bother, sir. We've everything sorted.

speaker: Agent
en: We'll soon see, won't we? For you must double the watch this evening.

speaker: Guard
en: Double, sir? Whatever for?

speaker: Agent
en: I believe I was followed here, young man. By pirates if my eyes honour me, though the ship was uncommonly large for such rascals. Certainly wasn't slavers, though. Not a ship that size. In any case, double the watch! And keep your damned eyes wide for anything suspicious. You up there! Look alive, man! You've a job to do!

speaker: Guard
en: Apologies, sir. I'll keep my eyes peeled.

speaker: Agent
en: For God's sake, what the hell is going on here today? How do you suppose you'll be able to ring that alarm if you're piss drunk and barely able to stand?

speaker: Guard
en: Forgive me, sir. I am fit and able. And if I see any strangeness about, you'll hear the bell ringing straight away, I promise.

speaker: Agent
en: I'd like to speak to the man in charge here. I require entrance to the warehouse! Which of you dogs has the key to the warehouse? Hm? Is there no one sober here? Fetch me the warehouse key if you please! The key, Goddammit! Someone find me the key!

speaker: Edward
en: Opía? Oh... Easy, Milady. Just thought you might like some help.

speaker: Opía
en: Why? What is your real motive?

speaker: Edward
en: Your name was on a map. I may have sold it to a nest of Templars. In error. We all make mistakes.

speaker: Opía
en: Typical. Twist a Templar blade to our back to play savior to our face.

speaker: Edward
en: Look, I'll level with you, lass. I'm also looking for a key. I figure I help you, you let me keep the key if it turns up... Right. You're offended. I'll go.

speaker: Opía
en: We will challenge you to a hunting contest. Gather more skins than us, and you win.

speaker: Edward
en: Easy. Let's go.

speaker: Opía
en: That was just luck.

speaker: Edward
en: That's not fair.

speaker: Opía
en: Consider it motivating.

speaker: Opía
en: It's obvious hunting is not in your blood. What makes you believe you can beat us? You will never win. One more for you. But I am not worried.

speaker: Opía
en: The white jaguar! A fine catch. You have more than proven yourself. We accept your help.

speaker: Edward
en: With what?

speaker: Opía
en: Look!

speaker: Edward
en: Frigates. Why? Is there anything out there but fish?

speaker: Opía
en: No... Those are your Templars. You have a ship and a pale face. Vessel and passport. Meet us at Grand Cayman to help us investigate.

speaker: Rhona
en: Ah... Captain Kenway. I'm assuming this is the friendliest face you've seen since dropping anchor?

speaker: Edward
en: Is Havana under curfew on my account?

speaker: Rhona
en: Hm, aye. Torres seems to think someone's coming after him.

speaker: Edward
en: He's not wrong...

speaker: Rhona
en: A manky looking thing. Is that what I think it is?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Watch. Through the blood of the governor, we can see through his eyes.

speaker: Rhona
en: That's... that's by the church.

speaker: Edward
en: Keep this safe. Just in case.

speaker: Rhona
en: I'll be at the bureau. Good luck.

speaker: Captain
en: (We have business with El Tiburón in the castillo. Mister Torres would like to speak with us personally.)

speaker: Captain
en: (Hush! Rumours will break confidence faster than any bullet. Now shut up about Assassins!)

speaker: Captain
en: (You two back there... shut your mouths before I shut them for you!)

speaker: Sailor 1
en: Yeah, right! So you can shoot us like you did the rest of our crew?

speaker: Sailor 2
en: Piss off!

speaker: Sailor 1
en: Marcus! Oh Jaysus... you bleeding animal!

speaker: Captain
en: (Shut up! Ok... let's continue... you, follow us. And don't screw up this time. Make way!)

speaker: Captain
en: (Take your positions! Call if you see anything unusual. Good evening, soldier. Stay alert.)

speaker: Edward
en: You're done, Torres. Christ!

speaker: Edward
en: This again, eh? You're too skilled for swordplay. How about a little gunplay? No man's immune to pistol shot, I reckon. I can't score a hit like this. You're a canny one up close. Are you weak against bullets?

speaker: Edward
en: If you could speak, mate, it would gladden me to hear your side.

speaker: Edward
en: You humbled me once, and I took that hard lesson, and I bettered myself. Die knowing that for all of our conflict, you helped make a soldier out of a scoundrel.

speaker: Edward
en: Leave this life for a lasting peace, down among the dead.

speaker: Rhona
en: We got word Torres left the city. Who were you chasing?

speaker: Edward
en: That vial was labeled Torres, but held the blood of his second. Where's he gone?

speaker: Rhona
en: Left port this morning, heading west along the coast.

speaker: Edward
en: The Observatory.

speaker: Anne
en: Will we follow?

speaker: Edward
en: Send word to Ah Tabai. We've cornered our man.

speaker: Edward
en: Opía! And how are "we" today?

speaker: Opía
en: Surprised. We did not think you would keep your word. Tell us... why do you expect to find your magic key here?

speaker: Edward
en: It holds an irresistible attraction to Templars, if that is who brought these ships.

speaker: Opía
en: We don't know what the Templars could want here. These people lead simple fishing lives.

speaker: Edward
en: Or perhaps not so simple. I'll go and have a mingle, see what "we" can find out.

speaker: Man
en: Your whole catch? You must have made a fortune.

speaker: Alvin
en: I did. But you know, this is exactly why they call me the King of Fishermen!

speaker: Man
en: Who calls you that?

speaker: Woman
en: Oh don't be jealous!

speaker: Man
en: Jealous? I'm not jealous!

speaker: Alvin
en: I'll show you the bill of sale if you like. Señorita Márquez's right-hand man Vargas signed it himself. She is using his home as her headquarters. I even met her there when I delivered the fish.

speaker: Woman
en: You see! Alvin is practivally nobility now!

speaker: Man
en: Ah! A noble fisherman. Indeed.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Quiet beach. Top Grog. A bleedin' House on a Hill. We'll be made soft and the Job's not done.

speaker: Anne Bonny
en: It's treasure enough for some, Edward. You must keep that in sight.

speaker: Edward
en: There's a Lot to keep in sight these Days. Thatch had it all figured, and look what it got him.

speaker: Anne
en: That need not be your End.

speaker: Robert Maynard
en: The King of England loves Mulled wine. Do you have mulled wine at this... ...establishment? What makes it special is the addition of Nutmeg, you see. A spice our Majesty the King has delivered from the far East, for we, his Subjects, to enjoy.

speaker: Maynard
en: Let it not be said that those with Power cannot treat the Little People charitably.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah...You'll find no little People here.

speaker: Edward
en: You must be lost, Mate.

speaker: Maynard
en: Lost? On the contrary.

speaker: Maynard
en: I'm here with purpose; to offer this Boon from the King's Table as a gesture of his good Will. And with it a Chance for you, Edward Kenway, along with these other Pirates, to leave this place with your Lives. It's what Our Majesty the King, God save him, would prefer.

speaker: Maynard
en: Myself, I'm inclined to a more... Permanent Solution.

speaker: Maynard
en: I await your unconditional Surrender at Kingston.

speaker: Anne
en: Who was that Bastard?

speaker: Edward
en: That was the bastard that killed Thatch.

speaker: Anne
en: Edward. A word... best in Private.

speaker: Edward
en: My Quarters, then.

speaker: Edward
en: That bastard Pirate Hunter... his name's Lieutenant Robert Maynard, though I call him a few other things besides.

speaker: Anne
en: Maynard's going to be a problem for us.

speaker: Edward
en: That's his intention.

speaker: Anne
en: There's been Redcoats everywhere since Thatch. Now that cocky Bastard walks in, bold as you please, and threatens us to our faces. Blackbeard would be turning in his Grave.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. I've been thinking on that.

speaker: Anne
en: What's your Plan for Maynard, then?

speaker: Edward
en: I mean to go to Kingston, pay him a quiet visit.

speaker: Anne
en: Getting there may not be easy. They say he's got a Warship tearing up Freebooters anywhere near the Place.

speaker: Edward
en: The Jackdaw's Crew can hold their own in a Fight well enough.

speaker: Anne
en: This is no ordinary Fight. Maynard's got the King's Navy behind him. And he hates us, you saw it. I think he hates you most of all.

speaker: Edward
en: Even more Reason for me to go in quiet.

speaker: Anne
en: Kingston then, just... be careful, Edward. We've lost Nassau. We can't lose Inagua too.

scene: The Boarding of the Black Ivory
speaker: The Boarding of the Black Ivory
en: was a genetic memory.

speaker: Known Owners
en: Unknown pirate, Captain "Keelhauling" Jeff Current Status: Unknown Crafted by Idun, an esteemed member of the Æsir lineage of the Isu, the Rings of Eden were a revolutionary invention that harnessed the power of electromagnetic fields. These remarkable rings possessed the ability to deflect projectiles with precision while also effectively neutralizing energy-based weapon discharges. However, wearing the Rings did not provide absolute immunity, and the Isu often employed them alongside shielding devices for enhanced protection and defense.While wearing this ring, you gain the ability to protect yourself with an energy shield.

speaker: Judge
en: Luisa, act a lady and open this bloody door now! You've taken this all wrong! Do you hear me? You're overreacting to... a filthy canard! Lies and slander meant to discredit me! The simple fact is, that woman is my secretary, nothing more! Luisa, do as I say or I will have the soldiery dismantle this door!

speaker: Judge
en: Ah! Who's this! A killer?

speaker: Judge
en: Help! Somebody help me!

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: Captain! A Word.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: What's on your mind, Shipwright? Are you ready for that Drink?

speaker: Lucy
en: Easy. I'm not your Shipwright yet. I was thinking to put Ashore when we're next near Land.

speaker: Edward
en: You're not leaving? I thought the Jackdaw and her Crew would secure your good Opinion.

speaker: Lucy
en: Not yet, at any Rate. I'm just in need of some good Rum, and Distraction.

speaker: Edward
en: Spoke like a Pirate. I know a place with an Abundance of both.

speaker: Lucy
en: I've yet to finish here. You weren't jesting when you said the Ship needs work. I'll find you at the Tavern when I'm done.

speaker: Edward
en: You're murdering the wrong people if you've gained the King's Enthusiasm.

speaker: Lucy
en: Accused of murdering. It's a fucking stitch-up, I told you.

speaker: Edward
en: What will you do now, then? You could join us. You won't find a better Ship than the Jackdaw, nor a fairer Crew.

speaker: Lucy
en: Christ, you're relentless.

speaker: Edward
en: I need you.

speaker: Lucy
en: So you said. You did keep me from hanging.

speaker: Edward
en: True.

speaker: Lucy
en: But that doesn't mean you own me.

speaker: Edward
en: Also True.

speaker: Lucy
en: The Jackdaw's not a bad Tub. And the Crew know their Work well enough. What else have you got for me?

speaker: Edward
en: I'll show you.

speaker: Edward
en: It might not look like much yet, but it will in Time.

speaker: Lucy
en: I've puked in every Town from here to Havana. What's different about this one?

speaker: Edward
en: This is ours, a Place where Men and Women can live easy and free, as God made them. Nothing but Sun, Rum, and Leisure.

speaker: Lucy
en: You've rehearsed that little Speech. Are the Words all yours?

speaker: Edward
en: Mine... and those of Friends. They're not any less true for that.

speaker: Lucy
en: I was just asking.

speaker: British civilian
en: Edward! Trust you to come at the right time. I've got a Pot of Plantain fresh off the Fire.

speaker: Lucy
en: Plantain! That's what you should have led with.

speaker: Edward
en: Let's eat up at the Villa. I want you to see it, anyway.

speaker: Lucy
en: Villa? Lardy-dardy! Next you'll tell me you're not Pirates but Noblemen.

speaker: Edward
en: I always hoped one would lead to the Other.

speaker: Pirate 1
en: It's a good Day for it, Edward!

speaker: Edward
en: Aye! And better for being Free to do it.

speaker: Pirate 2
en: That's a pretty Morsel you've found there, Kenway.

speaker: Lucy
en: Back off Swab, or I'll unman you where you stand!

speaker: Pirate 2
en: All right, all right! I meant no Offense.

speaker: Edward
en: Some have yet to grasp the true Purpose of this Place.

speaker: Lucy
en: Pff! Look at you, playing the Politician. Your Crew respects you. I see that.

speaker: Edward
en: It's mutual. Are you surprised?

speaker: Lucy
en: My experience with Authority is... uneven.

speaker: Lucy
en: Moggy!

speaker: Lucy
en: Hey there Moggy. What are you doing? Look at your fetching little Face.

speaker: Edward
en: Careful with that one. He's as much a Scoundrel as any of us.

speaker: Lucy
en: My Grandfather owned a place like this on Black Island. Had the best Plantain in the West Indies.

speaker: Edward
en: That's quite a Boast.

speaker: Lucy
en: It's True nonetheless. When my Mother died, it was Grandad who raised me. We ate Plantain every day. I'm pretty much made of Plantain.

speaker: Edward
en: Where's this Grandfather now?

speaker: Lucy
en: Murdered. I'm going to find the one who did it and vent his Skull. It's like this... I'm heir to Grandad's Fortune. If you help me recover it, I'll cut you in. Then we'll talk about joining your Crew.

speaker: Edward
en: I see you're going to make me work for this.

speaker: Lucy
en: I'm worth it.

speaker: Edward
en: Where is this Inheritance?

speaker: Lucy
en: Grandad's Plantation. And we have to be quick. My Father and his blood-sucking Barrister are after it, no Doubt.

speaker: Edward
en: You had better be a very good Shipwright.

speaker: Lucy
en: As to that, I'll be back on the Jackdaw patching your sorry Sails...

speaker: Lucy
en: ...Captain.

speaker: Lucy
en: We've improved the Jackdaw's Hull, but it needs more than just Joinery. The Crew have a Part to play as well. They should brace the Ship just before we're hit. If we time it right, we'll take less Damage. That means less Work for me.

speaker: Edward
en: Another String to our Bow, then.

speaker: Lucy
en: My Papa was not a good Father. He couldn't make it as a Businessman like Grandad. He turned his hand to Piracy but lacked the stomach for it. So he drank, and took it out on me.

speaker: Edward
en: And now he wants your Inheritance.

speaker: Lucy
en: He'll come looking for me, and that means Trouble. Sorry.

speaker: Edward
en: You'll make it up to me.

speaker: Lucy
en: Hello, Papa.

speaker: Edward
en: Your Father?

speaker: Lucy
en: His Lackies. Right on time.

speaker: Edward
en: Whatever your Father paid them, it wasn't enough.

speaker: Edward
en: Bon Voyage, Shitbirds.

speaker: Lucy
en: The Harbor's too dangerous, my Father will have it watched. There's a place on the far side of the Island where we can dock.

speaker: Lucy
en: Right. We should be careful. My Father's a Drunk but he's not stupid, and he's mean as a cut Snake when Money's involved.

speaker: Edward
en: Quiet as Church Mice, then. Lead on.

speaker: Lucy
en: Grandad taught me to shoot out here. He had a pair of gold Pistols he loved even more than me.

speaker: Lucy
en: There's a Hut near the Beach where Grandad used to hide things. I want to check there first.

speaker: Lucy
en: I spent a lot of time in that Hut as a kid.

speaker: Edward
en: I had a place like it on my Father's Farm. I'd hide there to escape my Chores.

speaker: Lucy
en: It wasn't that, I... My Father would lock me in it when he was drinking. Once I was stuck there for Days. He forgot about me.

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus.

speaker: Lucy
en: I'll search the Hut. I know Grandad's hiding spots. You should check the Manor. The Will could be somewhere in his Office. We need to find it before my Father does. I'll meet you back there.

speaker: Edward
en: Shit! The Father and this Barrister changed the Will, and murdered Lucy's Grandfather. Lucy will kill him before we find the Gold.

speaker: Edward
en: Lucy's Father and this Barrister rewrote the Grandfather's Will. He gave himself everything.

speaker: Lucy
en: Get inside!

speaker: Edward
en: That's not good.

speaker: Lucy
en: You remember this Place, Papa? I remember every fucking Inch.

speaker: John Baldwin
en: I remember your Mother letting you out. She was always too soft on you.

speaker: Lucy
en: Shut up! I know you killed Grandad, and then stitched me up for it.

speaker: John
en: You know Nothing, Girl.

speaker: Lucy
en: But you're only his Son-in-law, aren't you? You won't get Anything in the Will.

speaker: John
en: Is that what you think you little Harpy? I get all of it. The Will's changed. And he can't change it back now, can he?

speaker: Lucy
en: It was you! Admit it. You killed Him. Say it!

speaker: Lucy
en: Say it.

speaker: John
en: Who do you think you are...

speaker: Lucy
en: I'm the one with the gun, Papa.

speaker: Lucy
en: Captain Kenway, I don't believe you've met my Father...

speaker: Edward
en: You've avenged your Grandfather at the least.

speaker: Lucy
en: But no Gold. There was nothing in the Hut but his Pistols.

speaker: Edward
en: Nothing at the Manor either. I only found a fake Will drafted by your Father's Barrister.

speaker: Lucy
