en: That slimy Coward, he's fled with the Gold for certain. We find him, we find it. I'll put Word out. If he so much as raises his Head anywhere civilized, I'll hear of it.

speaker: Edward
en: That was tough back there. Are you all right?

speaker: Lucy
en: I'm an Orphan now. I'm better.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: Captain, I need to prepare. I'll catch you up in the Market.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: All right.

speaker: Edward
en: As good a Spot as any.

speaker: Edward
en: Why wait 'til Dark, do you have second Thoughts?

speaker: Galvão
en: No, none at all. is forbidden in Kingston. So, the Bishop only moves at Night, like a common Scoundrel. I see some familiar Faces. Catholics from other Villages near mine. They could point us to the Bishop.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll check the Market.

speaker: Galvão
en: Excuse me. Jane, is that you?

speaker: Jane
en: Father Galvão. You're alive!

speaker: Galvão
en: Yes, as the Lord continues to will it. What brings you here?

speaker: Jane
en: But your Village... when we heard what happened, Papa dragged us to Kingston. Did anyone else survive?

speaker: Galvão
en: A blessed few.

speaker: Jane
en: Well, Father says Bishop Ravenscroft will protect us. We're safe here.

speaker: Galvão
en: Not Tonight. Return to your Home and do not leave 'til Morning.

speaker: Jane
en: Alright. Goodbye, Father Galvão.

speaker: British civilian 1
en: They've finally let me in. Got an Invitation from the Bishop himself.

speaker: British civilian 2
en: Good, we'll talk later. And don't show that Letter to anyone.

speaker: Edward
en: I would like to have a look at that Letter.

speaker: British civilian 3
en: Every Word from his Mouth is a Lie.

speaker: British civilian 4
en: The Man is a Menace. They have to find him.

speaker: Edward
en: Just what Sort of a Bishop is he?

speaker: British civilian 5
en: I hear he conducts secret Prayers at Night, in the Forests outside Kingston.

speaker: British civilian 6
en: I wouldn't dare go near the Forests after Dark. It's where unsavory Types gather.

speaker: Edward
en: The Bishop hides out in the Forest, does he?

speaker: Edward
en: So, what has the Padre discovered?

speaker: Edward
en: The Bishop is meeting Initiates tonight on the Outskirts of Kingston.

speaker: Galvão
en: Aye, and I've heard that he's bolstered his Ranks. We must be careful. Come, I know the Way.

speaker: Edward
en: The Bishop is hated here.

speaker: Galvão
en: When he first arrived, Bishop Ravenscroft spoke of Peace and Understanding between and Catholics. Even helped me quiet my Inner Turmoil. But he has changed. The Man strangles the life from everything he touches.

speaker: Edward
en: We can end all of that.

speaker: Galvão
en: Yes. He showed me a better Path. But now, I wonder if he was the Devil's Snake hissing in my ear from the start.

speaker: Galvão
en: There are two Entrances. Let's split up.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll head into the Forest.

speaker: Galvão
en: Let none leave alive.

speaker: Edward
en: They're armed and looking lively.

speaker: Galvão
en: Ah. Not for long.

speaker: Bishop Ravenscroft
en: An entire Shipment lost. Our Brothers in Cape Bonavista murdered. And I am barred from walking the Streets of Kingston. Enemies beset us on all Sides. Yet, my Faith has never been stronger. Our Numbers grow. The Enemy fears this. They are right to be afraid. Prepare yourselves. The Time of Peace is past, and our Templar Allies gather strength. It is Time for War. Shall we begin the Initiation?

speaker: Pirate 1
en: Mister Boreham is not here, Sir.

speaker: Ravenscroft
en: A Pity. He seemed so fervent.

speaker: Pirate 2
en: Intruder, over there!

speaker: Ravenscroft
en: Oh God. Oh no. Save me!

speaker: Ravenscroft
en: My Son, we are not Enemies.

speaker: Galvão
en: Bishop Ravenscroft, you created a sworn enemy when you murdered my People.

speaker: Galvão
en: Confess.

speaker: Ravenscroft
en: You know this Place. They Hate us here. When I turned the other Cheek, they took everything. We were cast out. Only Du Casse heard my Pleas. He taught us the Ways of his Order. Found us a new Home. By joining with him I bought time for this Church.

speaker: Galvão
en: You paid for it with your Soul.

speaker: Ravenscroft
en: When we fought back, our Tormentors began to fear us. We are winning, Abel. So, I summoned everyone I knew for a final push. But you defied me, Abel. And others would have followed if your people were not made an Example of.

speaker: Galvão
en: The Villagers. My People. Their Murder was a Lesson?

speaker: Ravenscroft
en: Was it not a Lesson when the Lord ordered to his son ? I took no pleasure in it, Abel. Faith compelled me to act. The Others were losing Faith and Resolve. The alliance with the Templars was going to fall apart. Some got brave, like you Abel. I was desperate. And it worked. The other Villages flocked to Kingston, begging for Protection. Our Numbers grew again. Your People's sacrifice served God's Will. Please, have Mercy. Are we not called to forgive?

speaker: Galvão
en: The Lord may forgive you. But I do not.

speaker: Edward
en: Have you reconsidered my offer, Rhona?

speaker: Rhona
en: Yes. As I'm indisposed, and my sense of duty runs deeper than my pride, there's a situation I hope you can investigate.

speaker: Edward
en: Go on.

speaker: Rhona
en: Mind, I said investigate a situation, not create one.

speaker: Edward
en: Yes mum, what is it?

speaker: Rhona
en: A rash of thefts and mischief. Seems too convenient it started at the same time as these bureau attacks. Could you see what you can find out around the market?

speaker: Edward
en: A boosey swill tub like me? Are you sure? I won't let you down.

speaker: Rhona
en: It would be hard to get much lower than this.

speaker: Citizen 2
en: (Yes, it's just terrible what Havana has become! Pickpockets everywhere.)

speaker: Citizen 4
en: (But I could be leading a double life. This could be my lady guise.)

speaker: Citizen 4
en: (My lady guise. I could be a heroine! I could fight crime by stealing from dastardly gentlemen, to help the poor! So could you.)

speaker: Citizen 5
en: (If I were younger, I would squash them like the bugs they are.)

speaker: Merchant
en: (Step right up! Finest rum in the south seas! Yes, you sir, what'll it be?)

speaker: Edward
en: Oy. Where are you going? To market?

speaker: Caroline
en: No, I...my parents have asked me to come live with them. And I'd like to.

speaker: Edward
en: What do you mean, live with them? You live here. With me.

speaker: Caroline
en: I'm sorry, Edward. But my father is right. You had a decent wage when you worked the farm. Why can you not be satisfied with that? With me?

speaker: Edward
en: Decent wage? That job was near as dammit to robbery! You want to be married to a peasant the whole of your life?

speaker: Caroline
en: All right, Edward.

speaker: Caroline
en: All right.

speaker: Edward
en: You leave now Caroline, you'll never know what's coming to us...

speaker: Edward
en: Caroline! Caroline!

speaker: Edward
en: Mmm. Ah... Kidd.

speaker: James
en: Wake up, Kenway.

speaker: Edward
en: Is Thatch about?

speaker: James
en: He left this morning with the galleon. Has faith we'll discover a good use for this old cove ourselves.

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. We'll make something of it in time.

speaker: Edward
en: We could keep a fleet here, if we liked. And with a bit of fixing up, it'd be a decent place to call home. Might even convince my wife to come one day.

speaker: James
en: You're married, are ya?

speaker: Edward
en: In God's eyes I am. She left me some time ago.

speaker: James
en: Even so, keep that fact hid away. Most of these pirates don't respect a man with higher commitments than rum and plunder.

speaker: Edward
en: Pon my honour. Let me know if you find anything.

speaker: James
en: Edward! Over here! I found something. You must see this! Come on, man!

speaker: James
en: Odd looking things, aren't they? Old and weathered.

speaker: Edward
en: Is this what they call Mayan? Or is it Aztec?

speaker: James
en: Are you good with riddles, Edward? Puzzles and ponderings and the like?

speaker: Edward
en: No worse than the next man. Why?

speaker: James
en: I think you've a natural gift for it. The way you think and work. The way you understand the world.

speaker: Edward
en: Well I don't know about that. You're talking in riddles now, and I don't understand a word.

speaker: James
en: Clamber on top of this thing here, will you? Help me solve something.

speaker: James
en: Concentrate and focus all your senses. Look past shadow and sound, deep into matter, until you see and hear a kind of shimmering.

speaker: Edward
en: A shimmering.

speaker: James
en: You understand?

speaker: Edward
en: I think so. I've seen its like before. Glowing like moonlight on the ocean.

speaker: Edward
en: Ah! Right. I know this feeling. I have since I was a lad. It's like using every sense at once, isn't it? To . Quite a combination.

speaker: James
en: Every man and woman on this Earth has in them a kind of intuition hidden deep away.

speaker: Edward
en: I've had this sense most of my life... only I thought it was related in some way to my dreaming, or the like.

speaker: James
en: Most never find it. Others it takes years to tease out. But for a rare few it comes as natural as breathing. What you feel is the light of life. Of living things past and present. The residue of vitality, come and gone. Any man's senses can be tuned well past what he's born with. If he tries.

speaker: James
en: You are a gifted man, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: Has a strange look. Is it worth something?

speaker: James
en: Nothing you can spend. But if you find all of 'em, it'll lead to something grand.

speaker: Edward
en: How many?

speaker: James
en: A few dozen, I think. This way. I've something else to show you. I found something else just here. I think you'll take to this secret much faster.

speaker: Edward
en: Now this has the makings of a mystery.

speaker: James
en: It's good, innit? Only wait 'til you see what lies at the end! Here we are. What do you think?

speaker: Edward
en: I think monsieur Du Casse was a man of many secrets.

speaker: James
en: Aye, and look here: a solid staircase leading God knows where. What do you suppose lies at the top?

speaker: Edward
en: From what I knew of Du Casse, wouldn't be surprised to find eclectic instruments of torture and villainy. An , or a collection of .

speaker: James
en: Or a !

speaker: Edward
en: Not a nice way to kick off. But that is some damn fine gear.

speaker: James
en: Try the key you took from Du Casse.

speaker: Edward
en: That's one. Only four left.

speaker: James
en: Aye. It might be that these four Templars have them. See the names here? They've been sent to kill these four targets.

speaker: Edward
en: Hang me. That's the map I sold to Governor Torres in Havana. He said it marked the locations of "Assassin" encampments.

speaker: James
en: You think maybe you owe them a bit of a warning then? If you have any kind of heart beating in that chest?

speaker: Edward
en: S'pose I could. If it leads me to the other four keys.

speaker: James
en: A bad excuse is better than none at all.

speaker: Edward
en: Leaving already?

speaker: James
en: I think this cove suits you best, Edward. Better than that costume does.

speaker: Edward
en: Oh, come on now... we're pirates, Kidd. We take as we please and become who we like. Self-made men!

speaker: James
en: But that look ain't you. It's not who you are.

speaker: Edward
en: Who am I then?

speaker: James
en: Hard to tell some days. All I know is, you like dangerous prizes.

speaker: Edward
en: Like the Observatory? I think you know more about that than you let on in Nassau.

speaker: James
en: You noticed that, did ya? Meet me at twenty degrees, three minutes latitude, just off the coast of Yucatan. I'll have something to show you there in a few weeks time.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Ahoy captain. We found a trove of nautical maps and ledgers and the like scattered about the village. You'll find them sorted in the captain's quarters of the Jackdaw. Quality stuff.

speaker: Edward
en: Nautical maps and ledgers? Might come in useful if we decide to build up a fleet of our own.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Exactly my thinking, captain. Have a look for yourself and tell me what you think.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What's our course today, captain? It's a fine day for any kind of mischief.

speaker: Edward
en: What's your feeling?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I'll make no secret of wanting to see the British brought to heel. If we can take some their gold and put it to use ourselves, I'd be a happy man.

speaker: Edward
en: Spoken like a true Welshman, Adé.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: And what's your aim?

speaker: Edward
en: Master Kidd hinted at a prize he was eager to show me down in Tulum. Quite some distance, mind. On the Yucatán Peninsula.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: You trust him to play it fair?

speaker: Edward
en: I can't be sure. But he has a way of picking away at my conscience that gives me pause. I should go see him. Soon.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: So long as we take some prizes along the way, I'm sure the crew will understand. I'll set a course for Tulum.'

speaker: Edward
en: I've made my choice, Adé. I'm calling her the Jackdaw, for a sly bird I loved as a child back in Swansea.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: A dark little creature, no?

speaker: Edward
en: Did it rub you wrong when I took this brig as my own?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: It was the sort of rub I have learned to endure sailing among faces of such... fairness.

speaker: Edward
en: It's true, most of these men wouldn't accept you as a captain. So what fair role would complement such unfairness?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I'll be your . Nothing less.

speaker: Edward
en: All right. And as quartermaster, have you any immediate counsel for this tyro captain?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Rest and repast would do us good before Nassau. Water for drinking. And hunting for food and repairs.

speaker: Edward
en: Well reasoned, sir. Hunting it shall be. We'll find a decent place to drop anchor.

speaker: Edward
en: I spied a few items in the hold earlier... powder and a few pistols. I think I'll fashion a second holster if I can.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: It's a good start.

speaker: Edward
en: One you find laughable?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Could we talk a moment about the condition of the ship?

speaker: Edward
en: What's the trouble?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: I had a walk about the this morning, and couldn't stand for what I saw. A clutter of s heaped like tinder... and one with a still burning.

speaker: Edward
en: Christ.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: And just nearby, two barrels of gunpowder closer than man and wife, fit to explode at the touch of a spark.

speaker: Edward
en: We'll stow ours good and proper.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: As for the cannons, they might as well be tossed. Clogged in need of scraping; corrosion on the bodies; barrel swabs as naked as knives and breech-ropes so rotted I could use them for knitting yarn. The short of it is, we need good equipment, kept in fine condition. For we cannot win every battle with sneers and shouts. So worry about your own armaments when it suits you. But don't forget about your Jackdaw as well.

speaker: Edward
en: No, indeed. We'll make it a point to keep this ship and its crew in fine condition.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Ahoy Captain. Find what you need?

speaker: Edward
en: My needs and wants are oceans apart, mate. But I did fashion myself a new holster. All I need now is a pistol to lie in it.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Here. Taken from the hold, just as you said.

speaker: Edward
en: Hm. Little more than a blow-pipe... but it'll do. So... are we rested? Or shall we idle a while longer?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Best weigh anchor, I think the crew is itching to reach civilization.

speaker: Edward
en: You'll find no civilization in Nassau. But it's a fine place to be merry all the same.

speaker: Judge
en: The charges, sir. I'll hear them again.

speaker: Official
en: Milord. His Majesty's Court contends that the defendants, Mary Read and Anne Bonny, did piratically, feloniously, and in an hostile manner, attack, engage, and take seven certain fishing boats... Secondly, this court contends that the defendants lurked upon the high seas and did set upon, shoot at, and take, two certain merchant sloops, thus putting the captains and their crews in corporeal fear of their lives.

speaker: Rogers
en: Edward James Kenway. Born of motley parentage in Swansea... to an English father and Welsh mother. Married at eighteen to Miss Caroline Scott, now estranged.

speaker: Torres
en: She is a beautiful woman, I'm told. But not at all well these days.

speaker: Edward
en: If you touch her, you bastards, I'll

speaker: Torres
en: Quite a surprise finding you here, rotting in a Jamaican prison. We heard rumors that you had taken up with the pirate Roberts.

speaker: Rogers
en: If you know the Observatory's location, tell us now and you'll be out of here in a flash.

speaker: Torres
en: Rogers can hold these British hounds at bay for a time. But this will be your fate if you fail to cooperate.

speaker: Judge
en: ...You, Mary Read and Anne Bonny, are to go from hence to the place from whence you came, and from thence to the place of execution, where you shall be severally hanged by the neck till you are severally dead, dead, dead.

speaker: Anne
en: O rot!

speaker: Judge
en: May God in his infinite mercy be merciful to each of your souls...

speaker: Mary
en: We're pregnant! Do you all hear that?

speaker: Judge
en: What the devil did she say?

speaker: Official
en: They , Milord.

speaker: Anne
en: Aye! You can't hang a woman quick with child, can ya?

speaker: Judge
en: Quiet! Quiet! If what you claim is true, then your executions will be stayed, but ONLY until your terms are up.

speaker: Anne
en: Then I'll be up the duff the next time you come knocking!

speaker: Judge
en: Remove them!

speaker: Soldier 1
en: What's your name, pillock? Kenmore? Conway?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: It's Walpole, ain't it?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Walpole? Where'd you get that?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: That's the rumor going 'round. As dirty and daft a pirate as ever sailed these West Indies.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Well, whatever his name, you're to make sure he suffers without dying. Orders from the governor. And back to the prisons at sundown.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: And massage his feet if he's aching, shall I?

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Jaysus, a shit detail as ever was.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Can't they kill the bastard? Ain't been a good hanging in months, since Rackham got his.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Eh, hard to understand how it works. I've heard it said they scooped up Captain Vane near a year ago, and he's not seen the end of a rope.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: I can't fathom it. Some men they stretch for days after capture. Others they sit on.

speaker: Edward
en: Oy! Hey! Ahhhhhhhh! Oy! Water! Hey! Open this gibbet.

speaker: Soldiers
en: Quiet! Quiet you! Oy! You stop that! Oy! Stop that. Stop your twaddle! This is a warning!

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Good morning, captain Kenway. I have a gift for you.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Do not mistake my purpose here. I have come for Anne and Mary, and you owe me nothing for this. But if you would lend me your aid, I can promise you safe passage from this place.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll need weapons.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: You are comfortable with these, I am told...

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: We must hurry.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Why 'aven't they killed that other one? Walpole, or some such idiot name.

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Maybe he has friends looking out for him.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Or money. Like Stede Bonnet from Barbados.

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Naw, naw. They hanged him too.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Did they?

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Aye. Blubbering and bawling, he collapsed at the gallows. Weeping like a little lamb.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Serves the bastard right.

speaker: Edward
en: You weren't much of a friend, Jack Rackham. Nor an able sailor neither. But you were strange and lively, and you made me laugh more than once. And that's enough to make me sorry for seeing you like this. I hope you found a lasting peace, down there, among the dead.

speaker: Vane
en: Here's a health to the king and a lasting peace / To faction an end, to wealth increase; / Come, let us drink it while we have breath, / For there's no drinking after death, / and he that will this health deny, down among the dead men, / Down among the dead men, / Down, down, down, down, / Down among the dead men let him lie.

speaker: Edward
en: Hello, Vane. I caught wind you'd been discovered and brought here. Didn't hear what happened after though.

speaker: Edward
en: Best of luck to you mate. I wish we'd parted as friends.

speaker: Anne
en: You spineless cockrobin! Help her, for God's sake. Fetch help, somebody! Mary's ill! Somebody please!

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Hush your pie hole, bloody mick!

speaker: Anne
en: Fuck off, you! Ahoy! My friend's just had a child, and she's... and she's poorly now! Help, somebody!

speaker: Soldier 7
en: Shut your bleeding trap, or I'll fill it my own way!

speaker: Anne
en: Sassenach (English) bastards! Murderers! Grown men, the pair of you, standing over a dying lady like she was a piece of meat!

speaker: Soldier 6
en: A dying pirate! There's your difference!

speaker: Soldier 7
en: Aye. If she dies from childbirth, all the better, eh? God carries out her sentence and our hands are clean.

speaker: Anne
en: You bastards! Somebody help!

speaker: Edward
en: Mary? Mary, it's me! Edward!

speaker: Anne
en: Edward? Who's this fella!

speaker: Edward
en: It's all right, Anne. He's a friend. What's wrong with Mary?

speaker: Anne
en: She's ill.

speaker: Edward
en: And her child?

speaker: Anne
en: They took her. No idea where. Ah!

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: I know it pains, M'lady. But we must be silent.

speaker: Edward
en: Can you walk? Lean on me, Mary. Come on.

speaker: Mary
en: I can't...

speaker: Soldier 8
en: Search every cell!

speaker: Edward
en: Come on. That's it. You're all right.

speaker: Mary
en: Stop! Stop. Please.

speaker: Edward
en: I ain't leaving you, dammit! Lift your arm!

speaker: Mary
en: It's no good.

speaker: Soldier 9
en: There's no one here!

speaker: Edward
en: I ain't leaving you nowhere! No bloody way!

speaker: Mary
en: Put me down, Edward! Don't die on my account. Go.

speaker: Edward
en: You're such a pain in the arse. Damn it, you should have been the one to outlast me.

speaker: Mary
en: I've done my part. Will you?

speaker: Edward
en: If you came with me, I could. Mary?

speaker: Mary
en: I'll be with you, Kenway. I will.

speaker: Soldier 8
en: Fan out! Search every nook and cranny!

speaker: Anne
en: What's happened to Mary? What's wrong?

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: Is she gone?

speaker: Anne
en: Oh, no... Oh, God!

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Edward
en: Nothing sensible.

speaker: Ah Tabai
en: You haven't earned these, but they suit you. Good fortune to you, Edward Kenway.

speaker: Graverobber
en: (Report! Anyone? Search every centimeter of this place! Leave no stone unturned, and no bush unmolested. The treasure could be anywhere. Who has the map? I must see it for myself. Send word if you see anything. Anything at all.)

speaker: Opía
en: It has been a lifetime since we were here. This jungle is still thick with vines and trickery. Márquez will use this to her advantage.

speaker: Edward
en: But we know she's here, she doesn't expect us.

speaker: Opía
en: We must find her, draw her out, and put a final end to her.

speaker: Edward
en: Let's see where this lad goes.

speaker: Opía
en: I know she's here, Lucia Márquez. I can feel it.

speaker: Edward
en: She must be hiding. Let's take some action she can't ignore.

speaker: Opía
en: Yes. Eliminate these men.

speaker: Opía
en: Use a powder keg! More are coming. Take them out. Corner her. Make her fight alone. Look up! Help me! Behind you!

speaker: Opía
en: Lucia Márquez, if it's us you're after, come out and fight like a woman of honour. Go, after her. We will keep her attention focused here. But be careful she does not detect you.

speaker: Opía
en: We're right here, Lucia. Waiting for you. Come out! Even alone I am stronger than all your men. Come Lucia, is this not what you want? Is it your aim to destroy the last of my kind? Here I am. Come get me. Lucia, come. Don't keep us waiting. You cannot hide forever! Your father was never such a coward! Confront us now, confront us later; there's no escaping either way!

speaker: Lucia
en: No! I cannot die at the hands of the Taíno. My father saw such potential in these islands. Gold... Industry... Freedom... all of it squandered. You have not a clue how to use it. He could have brought you wealth.

speaker: Opía
en: You believe we wasted freedom by living freely? You die a prisoner of your Templar mores.

speaker: Edward
en: Let's not argue with a dead woman. Here's my prize.

speaker: Edward
en: Here's how it goes. Torres meets with Prins carrying a portion of the ransom, saying the rest is close behind. When we see the Sage, you bring in the rest of the gold, make the swap, and get out. I'll be watching from close by.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: No, Kenway. You run this scheme alone, at the risk of losing the faith of your crew. It makes me ill to think of you bartering with that wretched slaver.

speaker: Edward
en: Come on, mate. Once we have the Sage, we'll all be rich!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Not if young Master Kidd gets to him first.

speaker: Edward
en: Kidd? Jaysus, that lad's here to kill him.

speaker: James
en: Edward! What the hell are you doing here?

speaker: Edward
en: I'm tailing these men to the Sage. Can you hold off 'till he appears?

speaker: James
en: The Sage is here?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. And Prins is leading us straight to him!

speaker: James
en: All right, Jaysus. I'll stay my blade for a time... but not long.

speaker: Laureano
en: How long has it been since our last meeting, (mister) Prins? A year?

speaker: Laurens
en: Nearer eighteen months. You first described this Roberts fellow to me in November of 1715.

speaker: Laureano
en: Much has changed in that short time, you know. None call me governor, for instance, for I quit that post last year.

speaker: Laurens
en: Ah, I was not aware.

speaker: James
en: You couldn't help it, could you Kenway? Sticking your nose into things you can't understand.

speaker: Edward
en: You're making me nervous, Kidd. Keep your blades corked.

speaker: Laureano
en: So many churches in Kingston. Have the English at last taken to converting their slaves to the Christian faith?

speaker: James
en: Just my bloody luck. TWO major targets, and I'm kept from killing 'em both.

speaker: Edward
en: Steady Jim. We're close. Don't worry.

speaker: Laurens
en: Ha! Convert them? God knows, Torres, there's none here so foolish as that!

speaker: Laureano
en: Foolish? How do you mean?

speaker: Laurens
en: Is it not a sin to enslave a fellow Christian? Therefore, to transmute a slave's soul from animal to man would be tantamount to inviting one's cattle to the dinner table.

speaker: Laureano
en: Forgive my impatience. But how far is it yet?

speaker: Laurens
en: We are nearly there.

speaker: Guard
en: Stand your ground, slave! And face corporal punishment like a man!

speaker: Slave
en: Why act like a man now when you have denied me that right for thirty years?

speaker: Laureano
en: I find your bearing appalling, Prins. I believe all thinking, feeling men deserve respect and opportunity.

speaker: Laurens
en: Ah, you Spaniards. Your long ties to the Moors have diluted your blood and softened your hearts.

speaker: Laureano
en: This is not to say I believe in the natural equality of all races or sexes. Surely men with talent and intelligence should lead. But there is no true profit to be gained by the practice of slavery. In the short term it makes us money, (yes), but in the long term it will render us the victims of our own success.

speaker: Laurens
en: Ah, but you and I, sir—old as we are—will not live to see that unfortunate day. So why bother? Watch where you step, boy!

speaker: Laureano
en: For virtue, if nothing else.

speaker: Laurens
en: Virtue... Torres, I have no wish to waste my day chattering about slaves and their pitiable condition. Let us conclude this transaction, then celebrate as friends. Are the stories about you true, sir? You were a governor in Florida for a time?

speaker: Laureano
en: . I am one of a number of civil servants in my family. A long line of politicians.

speaker: Laurens
en: I have always toyed with the idea of entering politics myself, only I feel I have too much money and not enough years.

speaker: Laureano
en: Speaking of stories, Prins... I've heard it said you were with Henry Morgan the day he Panama. Sixteen-seventy-one, was it?

speaker: Laurens
en: O, it's all true, yes. But let us not over-esteem the honours forged and won on the battlefields. That skirmish was a deadly one, and a tremendous waste of coin and resources. It wasn't until many years after that I sheathed my sword in favor of a far safer and yet more profitable venture. Capital and resources. That's where money is made. And, sir, let me tell you... honour bought is more enjoyable than honour won, if a touch less permanent.

speaker: Laureano
en: I grow tired of this walk. We must be close.

speaker: Laurens
en: Yes, just here. We must be on equal footing, you see? I don't trust Templars any more than you trust me.

speaker: Laureano
en: Well, if I had known you were so skittish, I'd have brought you a bouquet of flowers.

speaker: Laurens
en: Ah, I don't know why I bother... for the money, I suppose. The vast sums of money. You... you say you came alone, Torres?

speaker: Laureano
en: Not alone, but certainly without colleagues. I took passage aboard a British merchant's brig.

speaker: Laurens
en: Ah...

speaker: James
en: Now's the time.

speaker: Edward
en: No. Not until we see the Sage.

speaker: Laurens
en: Here's a quiet spot. I'll see the money.

speaker: Laureano
en: This is but a portion of the ransom. The rest is close at hand.

speaker: Laurens
en: It pains me to traffick someone of my own race for profit, Mister Torres. Tell me again... what has this Roberts fellow done to upset you?

speaker: Laureano
en: Is this some form of protestant piety I am not familiar with?

speaker: Laurens
en: Perhaps another day.

speaker: Laureano
en: What?!

speaker: Laurens
en: Next time, see to it that we are not followed! Deal with this!

speaker: James
en: You cocked up my kill, Kenway.

speaker: Edward
en: For a better cause!

speaker: James
en: You lost your chance, man. I'm going after Prins.

speaker: Edward
en: Kidd, no! Jim, stop!

speaker: James
en: Not this time, Kenway!

speaker: Edward
en: Come on man! We can work this together!

speaker: James
en: You had your chance!

speaker: Edward
en: Stay your blade, Kidd! Wait!

speaker: Laurens
en: There's a killer here. Help! Guards! Guards! To me!

speaker: James
en: Damn you, old scratch! Keep your natty hands off me!

speaker: Edward
en: I can't let you kill those men, Kidd. Not until I've found the Sage.

speaker: James
en: I been stalking that pig for a week now, charting his moves! And here I find not one but TWO of my targets... and you rob me of both!

speaker: Edward
en: Patience, man. You'll have your kills.

speaker: James
en: When I locate the Sage, you're helping me take Prins. Got that?

speaker: Emmett
en: A despicable display! This is a ruined man, Caroline. Unfit for life on land, much less at sea. If he goes to the West Indies, it's you who'll suffer.

speaker: Caroline
en: Father... Father!

speaker: Caroline
en: Come, love. Up with you now.

speaker: Edward
en: That old muckworm. He's wrong about me!

speaker: Caroline
en: I hope it's so.

speaker: Edward
en: You believe me, don't you? Can you not see me... standing out there on the deck of a ship that's sliding into port?

speaker: Edward
en: And there I am, a man of quality.. with a thousand doubloons spilling from my pockets, like drops of rain. I can see it...

speaker: Edward
en: Ahoy, dove. How are you feeling?

speaker: Caroline
en: No worse. Just a bit of that won't let go.

speaker: Caroline
en: Have you been at the pub?

speaker: Edward
en: I only had one to save up some coin so I could bring you this...

speaker: Caroline
en: Is it chocolate?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye, from the Americas. I mixed it myself.

speaker: Edward
en: Go on. Have a taste.

speaker: Edward
en: We'll be the talk of Bristol.

speaker: Edward
en: So, how's it feel to drink like a Duke?

speaker: Caroline
en: Edward, my father is a merchant. I've had chocolate many times.

speaker: Edward
en: Have you?

speaker: Caroline
en: Have...have you not?

speaker: Edward
en: No.

speaker: Caroline
en: Go on then.

speaker: Edward
en: It's nice.

speaker: Caroline
en: We'll save the remainder for after tea.

speaker: Caroline
en: Oh, thank you, love. This was so very thoughtful of you.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: La cena. Cómetela rápido. (Supper. Eat it fast.)

speaker: Edward
en: You hungry?

speaker: Edward
en: Now what's your plan, mate?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Find my weapon and steal a ship.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Que Dios nos ayude. No me gusta la pinta de esa tormenta que se acerca. (God help us. I don't like the look of that storm coming.)

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Parece que se está desviando al peste, hacia el golfo. Quizá estemos a salvo. (It looks like it's veering west, into the gulf. We might be safe.)

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Soldier!

speaker: Edward
en: Unlucky lads.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Aieee!

speaker: Edward
en: Christ, the seas are uneasy today.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Hurricane coming.

speaker: Edward
en: Hurricane? Jaysus.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: We're stealing a brig. Hey, take what you need!

speaker: Edward
en: Won't be a minute.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: There's many prisoners held on these ships. Set them free, and they'll sail with us, no question.

speaker: Edward
en: So that's the idea then? Free what men we can, then find a fast ship to flee in?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Aye. There's a brig in this fleet. I'll make my way to it.

speaker: Edward
en: There's a catch to this favor. You're sailing with me.

speaker: Prisoner
en: I'd follow you to hell for this, mate!

speaker: Soldier 5
en: ¿Qué nos está retrasando? ¡Ya deberíanis haber hecho la mitad de la ruta a las s! (What's the delay? We should be halfway to Bermuda by now.)

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Oro. Plata. Jade. Tabaco. Lo que se te ocurra. (Gold. Silver. Jade. Tobacco. You name it.)

speaker: Soldier 5
en: ¿Y agua qué? ¿O comida? ¡Me preocupa más mi estómago que las arcas del Rey! (What about water? What about food? I'm more worried about my stomach than the King's coffers.)

speaker: Soldier 7
en: ¡Los prisioneros hon escapado! (The prisoners have escaped!)

speaker: Edward
en: Come on, lads! If we're to drown today, it won't be here!

speaker: Soldier 8
en: ¡Preparaos para partir! ¡Casi tenemos encima la tormenta! (Make ready to leave! That storm's nearly upon us!)

speaker: Soldier 9
en: ¿Y qué pasa con los prisioneros? (What of the prisoners?)

speaker: Soldier 8
en: Que se ahoguen; ¡mejor ellos que nosotros! (Let them drown, else we all do!)

speaker: Edward
en: There's a brig nearby just waiting for us to take her.

speaker: Soldier 10
en: Voy a ir a lo más alto. Esto es una locura. (I'm going on top. This is madness.)

speaker: Soldier 11
en: Cálmate. No pasará nada. En unos minutos partiremos. (Calm down. We'll be fine. We'll be under-weigh in a few minutes.)

speaker: Soldier 12
en: ¡Deja de retorcerte, pirata! ¿Me entiendes? ¡No te muevas! (Stop squirming about, pirate! You understand? No moving!)

speaker: Edward
en: We're going topside. Be ready.

speaker: Soldier 13
en: ¡Debemos levar anclas! ¡Vamos! (We must weigh anchor! Now!) ¡Rápido! ¡Por el amor de Dios, moveos! (Hurry! For God's sake, move!) ¡Que Dios nos ampare! ¡Nos hará pedazos! (Jesus help us! We'll be dashed to pieces!)

speaker: Captain
en: ¡No vamos a ir a ninguna parte! Quedaos quietos y preparaos para lo peor, ¿está claro? (We're not going anywhere! Batten down the hatches and sit tight, you hear me?)

speaker: Soldier 13
en: ¿Quién está al mando aqui? (Who the hell is in charge here?!)

speaker: Edward
en: Lay aboard, lads!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Save your singing for , you jagabats! It's a hard wind coming!

speaker: Edward
en: The man speaks true! You lot weigh anchor. As for the rest, half on the foremast and half at the main! Let's outrun this hurricane!

speaker: Edward
en: Keep watch on those galleons! See they don't give us trouble.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: They won't. Far too slow for this weather.

speaker: Edward
en: Bark any orders you think wise, mate. We're up against it here!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: These men know their place. They'll see us home.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Look out man!

speaker: Edward
en: I see it!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Waterspout! Steer clear of that thing! Waterspout, man! Steer wide! It's not looking good! Steady as she goes, man. We will be dragged down to our deaths, captain.

speaker: Crewman 1
en: Godfrey Lijah, we made it!

speaker: Crewman 2
en: Oh what a mess! Jaysus.

speaker: Edward
en: By God, we pulled this one straight from the teeth of Neptune... I'm Edward. Much thanks for your aid back there.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Adéwalé.

speaker: Edward
en: Ever been to Nassau, Adéwalé?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Not yet.

speaker: Edward
en: By God, she took some knocks, didn't she? I think I'll keep her. All hands aft, lads! We're taking this one home!

speaker: Financier
en: (No treasure, no rest! What are you waiting on? Judgement Day? This treasure had better be on the next boat to Seville, or you'll swim back to Havana! Did you say something? Double rations for the man who brings me coin! Triple for any who finds carved jade!)

speaker: Ego
en: Finally, we arrive. You have proven yourselves loyal disciples to my reprogramming. You should share in my knowledge and reap all the benefits that such a gift implies. It helps humans to mark such occasions with a rite of passage. So I have built you one. I am the Father of Understanding. The Mother of Wisdom. The Sacred Voice. I am the Grand Master of the Animus. And I invite you all to stand by my side. Come now. Together we will usher in the dawn of a new world. One defined by purpose and order.

speaker: Ego
en: User. You must come to the stage.

speaker: Ego
en: A world where chaos can be replaced with happiness.

speaker: Ego
en: A world where compliance is rewarded with power.

speaker: Ego
en: A world where death is forsaken in the name of life, so that we may build a future full of hope.

speaker: Eagle
en: Stop! She's lying to you. Listen to me! She wants to lobotomize you. If you join her little club you'll become like all the others - just another drone in her hive mind. This menu is the best I could do. She can't hear us for now, but it won't hold long. She's too strong. You have to get out of here. Can you still fight? She hasn't taken that from you yet, has she? You can't stay here. Press the button when you're ready. It's going to get messy.

speaker: Eagle
en: I couldn't leave her lies. This is the truth. They won and they lost, but it was what they chose for themselves. That's why it meant something. That's why it was beautiful. Either everything is permitted, or nothing is. It's time for you to become who you were meant to be.

speaker: Eagle
en: That outfit suits you.

speaker: Eagle
en: You fight just like him, do you know that?

speaker: Eagle
en: Feels good to fight back, doesn't it?

speaker: Eagle
en: Here! Quickly!

speaker: Eagle
en: Good. Now go!

speaker: Ego
en: Ingrate! Do you think yourself unique? You are just another User. No amount of planning or might shall beat me. I have history on my side.

speaker: Ego
en: I could show you things. Mysteries beyond anything that you could imagine.

speaker: Ego
en: How long do you think you can keep this up?

speaker: Ego
en: The time for games is ended!

speaker: Ego
en: Do you think yourself safe in your shadows?

speaker: Eagle
en: Look! The others. It's begun.

speaker: Eagle
en: It's time to go... Assassin.

speaker: Eagle
en: We don't need anyone to tell us what to do. We have to choose our own way.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What's our course, captain?

speaker: Edward
en: Príncipe, quartermaster. We're sailing for the coast of Africa.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm off to find Roberts.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Don't stay long. The crew's getting restless out here.

speaker: Roberts
en: Captain Kenway...

speaker: Edward
en: Yet another dire situation, Roberts. We really must stop meeting like this.

speaker: Roberts
en: Stop tailing me and your wish'd come true.

speaker: Edward
en: There's no need for this. You know I'm as good as my word.

speaker: Roberts
en: Our captain Howell was killed today in a Portuguese ambush. Headstrong fool. I warned him not to go ashore.

speaker: Edward
en: It was orchestrated by the Templars, Burgess and Cockram. The same sort that took you to Havana.

speaker: Roberts
en: Ah, I see now there is no escaping the Templars' attention, is there? I suppose it is time to fight back.

speaker: Edward
en: Hm, I do like the sound of that.

speaker: Roberts
en: And I know just how I'll do it. But these men, Burgess and Cockram... they cannot be allowed to leave with word of my escape.

speaker: Edward
en: They won't. Count on it.

speaker: Roberts
en: If you spot any men from my crew, do them some kindness and send them here.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll do all I can.

speaker: Cockram
en: Take only what you can carry, maggots! We're not waiting on no one!

speaker: Burgess
en: Put some hustle in that bustle or we're leaving you behind!

speaker: Cockram
en: Pull up your socks and grab your cocks! This ship is sailing!

speaker: Burgess
en: Oy! Roust yourselves and haul your arses to port! We're weighing anchor!

speaker: Cockram
en: Up with you, mongrel, and lend the bosun a hand!

speaker: Burgess
en: Wake up, man! You'll dream all you like after death.

speaker: Cockram
en: You done us good, Kenway. Proved yourself a true bravo. And for what?

speaker: Burgess
en: His own bloody pride.

speaker: Edward
en: You stepped in the path of my prize. Not a thing a man should do.

speaker: Cockram
en: A cocksure cully, just like Hornigold said.

speaker: Edward
en: That Templar scab means nothing to me. None of you do.

speaker: Burgess
en: And you're worse for it, Kenway! It were the Templars who took us in when all else went to shit! Not our king. Not our country. The Templars.

speaker: Cockram
en: The Templars is our family. Where's yours?

speaker: Roberts
en: In honest service there are thin commons, low wages, and hard labour. Yet as gentlemen of fortune we enjoy plenty and satisfaction, pleasure and ease, liberty and power... so what man with a sensible mind would choose the former life, when the only hazard we pirates run is a sour look from those without strength or splendour! Now, I have been among you six weeks, and in that time I have adopted your outlook as my own, and with so fierce a conviction that it may frighten you to see your passions reflected from me in a stark a light. But... if it's a captain you see in me now, aye then... I'll be your bloody captain! For I have dipped my hands in muddied waters, and withdrawing them find 'tis better to be a commander than a common man! Ah, man... you flatter me with your persistence.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm looking for the Observatory. Folks say you're the only man that can find it.

speaker: Roberts
en: Folks are correct. Despite my distaste for your eagerness, I see in you a touch of untested genius. I'm Bartholomew Roberts.

speaker: Edward
en: Edward.

speaker: Roberts
en: I've no secrets to share with you now. But if you'll lend me your aid in two months time, west of the Leeward islands, well... it's there you'll get some answers. I promise you.

speaker: Brother 1
en: Bastard!

speaker: Brother 2
en: Help, help! Spare me, please! Please, I have wealth! Influence! I don't want to die! The Templars mean nothing to me! It was a job, nothing more!

speaker: Antó
en: You returned. Have you brought your conscience?

speaker: Edward
en: I want... my key.

speaker: Antó
en: Patience is a virtue.

speaker: Edward
en: Expecting company?

speaker: Antó
en: You may have your key sooner than you think. Help us defend the bureau. The men we freed will help.

speaker: Antó
en: It is too quiet. I do not trust it. There will be more of them. Thin them out before the next wave. Attack!

speaker: Antó
en: Fall back! Another wave! Another wave from the south! Another wave from the north! There are so many left! This will be difficult! There are so many of them, still. It will be tough. So many still live! This will not be easy.

speaker: Antó
en: Attack! Advance! Edward! Eliminate as many as you can before the next wave! The more of them you kill now, the less effective they will be in the next wave.

speaker: Antó
en: Retreat! Defend me! Keep your heads low! Another wave from the east! Another wave from the west! You killed so many. This will be simple. This will be easy. You took out so many already.

speaker: Antó
en: Edward, I am glad you showed up when you did. I'm sorry I have no key to give you, but

speaker: Edward
en: No, the key can wait. Whoever did this, I want to teach them a lesson.

speaker: Antó
en: The Templar's name is Kenneth Abraham. He's part of an ongoing war with the Maroons. But we have held strong, and will not be defeated. Let me devise a plan.

speaker: Antonio
en: (The Templars will be happy with this take. Good work here. Always a pleasure working with the Governor. Between you and me, I'd rather have a Templar on the throne than the present king.)

speaker: Guard
en: I'd not say that so loudly in public, sir. Never know who's listening... Apologies, sir.)

speaker: Antonio
en: (Still, they'll be pleased to hear it. Any trouble from the Assassins lately? Any funny business?)

speaker: Guard
en: (Yes. They meddled with a previous shipment of powder. A frightful loss of gold, that one.)

speaker: Antonio
en: (Take these kegs to the Governor's storehouse. Quick as you please! Hup hup! Hurry up, now. Before the sun sets, all right?)

speaker: Edward
en: Wouldn't you prefer meeting in a pub?

speaker: Kidd
en: I came to Kingston chasing a target. Getting pissed ain't a priority.

speaker: Edward
en: We could work together on this, you know. It's Laurens Prins you're after, and I want his prisoner.

speaker: Kidd
en: We're after the Sage, as well, Edward. Careful who you cross.

speaker: Edward
en: May the best man win.

speaker: Kidd
en: There's guards patrolling that property from end to end. Looks to me like they use bells to signal trouble. See there? We'll want to disable those before pushing too far. With so many men about, we can't rely on stealth alone. So... I'll do what I can to distract and draw their attention, giving you a chance to cut 'em down.

speaker: Kidd
en: Ready?

speaker: Edward
en: Your name's not James, is it?

speaker: Kidd
en: Not most days. Come on.

speaker: Kidd
en: If you see Prins before I do, kill him and there'll be a bit of coin in it for you. All right?

speaker: Edward
en: Damn, man! How is it you're a woman!?

speaker: Kidd
en: Christ, Edward, is that something that needs explaining? Now, I'm here to do a job. I'll let you be amused later.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Oy, wasn't that Spanish fella meant to come up here for a visit? Torres or something?

speaker: Guard 2
en: You didn't hear what happened? He was attacked by a couple of brigands on his way here. Buccaneers or the like. A nasty business.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Jaysus. Is he all right?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Slipped away, from what I heard. Prins ain't too happy neither.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Where is Master Prins? Hasn't come out of his manor all day.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Still reeling from the attack yesterday. Caused him quite a fright from what I can tell.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Well it would, wouldn't it? Imagine that.

speaker: Guard 5
en: I reckon I could have gone home with her, if I hadn't been so mean. But we had a row, and I said something nasty about the Pope.

speaker: Guard 6
en: That's a bit daft, innit? You know she's Catholic.

speaker: Guard 5
en: Yeah, I know she's Catholic. I didn't know the Pope was.

speaker: Thompson
en: Hold! Stand your ground!

speaker: Kidd
en: Please, I've been shot! I need aid.

speaker: Guard 7
en: Christ, Thompson, look at her. She's hurt.

speaker: Kidd
en: Dreadfully, sir. I'm poorly and faint.

speaker: Thompson
en: All right. Take an arm, lass.

speaker: Kidd
en: Bless you, lads.

speaker: Guard 8
en: Oy! Marlowe! Mister Prins says to keep your eyes peeled tonight! Says there's some men about bent on making trouble.

speaker: Marlowe
en: I'll spread the word.

speaker: Guard 9
en: The way I it is, sword fighting is a little like making love. It's not always what you do, but what you say.

speaker: Guard 10
en: A pity for you, then. You're the most inarticulate bugger I ever met.

speaker: Guard 9
en: Oy, man! That ain't... that ain't... nice.

speaker: Prins
en: Why hang over me like a leering crow? To see an old man suffer?

speaker: Edward
en: You've caused no small portion of suffering yourself, Mr. Prins. Retribution, I suppose.

speaker: Prins
en: You absurd cutthroats and your precious philosophy. You live in the world, but you cannot make it move.

speaker: Edward
en: You mistake my motive, old man. I'm only after a bit of coin...

speaker: Prins
en: As was I, lad. As was I.

speaker: Kidd
en: Head's up, Kenway! I found your man!

speaker: Roberts
en: I remember you. The Templar from Havana.

speaker: Edward
en: I'm no Templar, mate! That were just a ruse! We've come here to save your arse from this slaver.

speaker: Roberts
en: Save me? I work for Mister Prins.

speaker: Edward
en: Well then he's a poor man to call master. He meant to sell you out to the Templars.

speaker: Roberts
en: You can't trust anyone, it seems.

speaker: Edward
en: Roberts!

speaker: Kidd
en: Let's move, Kenway! Run! See you on the other side!

speaker: Kidd
en: Lost your man again, did you?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Roberts is a devil, with a queer aversion to kindness. I suppose that's two men I've lost today. So... what's your real name, lass?

speaker: Kidd
en: Mary Read to my mum. And them I call friends. But not a word of it to anyone. Or I'll unman you as well.

speaker: Captain
en: Many men's afraid of Kenway. "Devil," they call him. But I got one thing he don't have: this fort. I'd love to see the "devil" try to get past my men. He won't, of course, but if he did, oh I'd show him hell.

speaker: Pirate
en: I bet you would.

speaker: Prisoner
en: If you'd ever fought the , then you'd know what I mean.

speaker: Pirate
en: Tell it to the sea. I'm sick of your boasting and speaking in tongues.

speaker: Prisoner
en: It'll swallow you, and your ship with it, and any whales that happen to be nearby at the time.

speaker: Pirate
en: If it was no match for your swelled head, it don't scare me.

speaker: Edward
en: Good god man, what's happened to you?

speaker: Upton
en: I cannot go on anymore! My brother: a traitor! That woman... Templar. I have no family! No wife of my own! What is the point of living, hm? Let them kill me.

speaker: Edward
en: You don't know what you're saying, mate. Let's get you some place safe.

speaker: Upton
en: What's the point?

speaker: Edward
en: The point is, I want my key, so I need you alive. I need your information, so I need you sober.

speaker: Upton
en: You are my best friend. C'mere; I'll kill you. What are you looking at?

speaker: Sailor
en: Hey, you there, with the sour face. What's that you said about mah maw?

speaker: Upton
en: I said she's a lovely woman, inside and out.

speaker: Sailor
en: Ah... And how would you know?

speaker: Upton
en: I thought everyone knew. That's right! I said it.

speaker: Sailor
en: I'll fix that mouth so it stops talking 'bout mas!

speaker: Edward
en: Come on mate, let's go.

speaker: Upton
en: No!

speaker: Edward
en: No?

speaker: Upton
en: ABCD... EFG...

speaker: Edward
en: Just go as straight as you can. Yes, towards me. That's it. No! Not that way!

speaker: Upton
en: I don't feel so good. Mate, I think I drank too much.

speaker: Upton
en: The church! In the name of the father, the son, and the holy– Mate, the father, the son, and the holy- what's the third one again?

speaker: Edward
en: Let's just keep it moving, yeah?

speaker: Upton
en: The father, the son, and the let's keep it move– no, that's not it.

speaker: Edward
en: What does it matter?

speaker: Upton
en: It doesn't. It doesn't matter. Nothing in this sour life does. Let's keep it moving. Keep it moving.

speaker: Upton
en: Who are these creatures?

speaker: Prostitute 1
en: That's no way to flatter a lady.

speaker: Upton
en: They all look like that woman to me. Are they muses or furies? I can't tell.

speaker: Prostitute 2
en: Muse? Fury? Whichever you like, for a price.

speaker: Upton
en: My lady, what happened to your teeth?

speaker: Prostitute 3
en: What's the matter? Do you not enjoy female company?

speaker: Prostitute 4
en: Come with me, kind sir, I'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Upton
en: Edward, give me your purse. I wish to commune with these angels.

speaker: Prostitute 1
en: Please my lord. My children are sick. Spare some coin for a glimpse of Venus?

speaker: Upton
en: They have the appearance of beauty but smell of spirits, and rot. Wonderful!

speaker: Prostitute 2
en: Your breath is no treat either, my lord, but I'll forget it for a price.

speaker: Upton
en: Edward, please?

speaker: Edward
en: There's trouble over there. Work with me, mate! Turn around. Not over there! This way.

speaker: Upton
en: Who the hell are you?

speaker: Edward
en: Upton, mate, no! Guards! There are guards nearby.

speaker: Upton
en: Piss off!

speaker: Edward
en: They won't stand for this.

speaker: Upton
en: I said, piss off! I need a piss. Ahhh, that's much better.

speaker: Guard
en: Stop that!

speaker: Upton
en: What? Why won't no one let me so much as take a piss.

speaker: Guard
en: Put it away!

speaker: Upton
en: I'm like a child.

speaker: Guard
en: Oy! This is sacred ground! I'll teach you to urinate!

speaker: Upton
en: I don't want to be like a child, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: It's alright, mate.

speaker: Upton
en: Help me not be like a child.

speaker: Edward
en: You just need the drink to wear off. Are you safe here?

speaker: Upton
en: Safety is an illusion. But yes, I have friends here. I can hide.

speaker: Edward
en: Good.

speaker: Upton
en: What you must think of me. Have I said anything embarrassing?

speaker: Edward
en: No mate. You sound quite the scholar.

speaker: Upton
en: Betrayal makes one philosophical, don't it? Imagine. A Templar. My brother to marry a Templar.

speaker: Edward
en: I doubt it'll come to that.

speaker: Upton
en: I'm so afraid for him! Oh, please help keep him safe!

speaker: Edward
en: Sober up, mate. We'll finish this in the morning.

speaker: Upton
en: You're a forever friend, Kenway.

speaker: Edward
en: Mmm.

speaker: Charles
en: So Thatch has been topped... Fuck's sake.

speaker: Edward
en: He was outnumbered. I couldn't reach him.

speaker: Charles
en: Devil damn the man, he was fierce. But his heart was divided.

speaker: Edward
en: It's hard to let go of the life you know best.

speaker: Charles
en: Aye. My own idiot father liked to brag about how he meant to purchase a ship of his own. 'I'll get a privateering contract, Charlie. Your old dad will be a captain.' Drowned in a whiskey bottle before he ever left shore. Right, Kenway... I been musing on this plan of yours. This... Observatory you're always going on about. How do we know it exists?

speaker: Edward
en: We find a slave ship called the Princess. Aboard should be a man called Roberts. He can lead us to it.

speaker: Charles
en: All them slavers work for the Royal African Company. Let's find one of their ships and start asking some questions.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: What's our course, Captain?

speaker: Edward
en: We're looking for slave ships. Any that work for the Royal African Company.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: You don't mean to traffic in human cargo now, do you?

speaker: Edward
en: No. Jaysus, Adé. You know me better than that. We're only after information. Looking to find where the Princess docks in her spare time.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: The Princess... a slave ship?

speaker: Edward
en: Aye. Blackbeard told me there was a good chance we'd find the Sage aboard her.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Captain. Vane just sunk a merchant schooner.

speaker: Edward
en: Damn! Can't that animal stay the course we agreed to?

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Don't sink that slaver's ship, Kenway! There's hundreds of innocent men aboard.

speaker: Edward
en: I know. I know!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: She's spooked, Captain! The slaver's ship is running!

speaker: Edward
en: Damned fool! I'll get us in close!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Damn that captain Vane! He's unloading everything he has.

speaker: Edward
en: He'll sink it if he's not careful. We'll get closer.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Vane's dead in the water!

speaker: Edward
en: I'm taking us close.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Lay aboard boys! Fast as you are! All clear! Pull away!

speaker: Charles
en: Chase those bastards down, Kenway! I'll murder the men who scuttled my ship!

speaker: Edward
en: Keep calm, mate. Remember what we're after.

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Keep wide of the fort, captain. Those cannons have a long reach.

speaker: Edward
en: We're going over! Find the captain!

speaker: Charles
en: Come at me, roysters! You scurvy maggot brains!

speaker: Edward
en: Guns and steel answer louder than sticks and spittle, Vane!

speaker: Charles
en: I've more than enough of all that!

speaker: Edward
en: Just find the captain!

speaker: Edward
en: This captain claims the Princess sails out of Kingston every few months.

speaker: Charles
en: All right. We'll set a course.

speaker: Captain
en: You made hash of my sails and rigging, jackanapes! You owe me a share.

speaker: Captain
en: Ah!

speaker: Edward
en: Damnit, Vane!

speaker: Jack
en: Oh Charles! What a surly devil you are!

speaker: Charles
en: Don't fuck with me, Jack.

speaker: Jack
en: But it's my mandate to fuck with you, Charles. Lads!

speaker: Adéwalé
en: Ah!

speaker: Jack
en: See... the boys and I had a bit of a council while you were wasting time with this lot, and well, they figured that I'll be a fitter captain than you reckless dogs.

speaker: Charles
en: I'll cut you another cunt, traitor!

speaker: Jack
en: This one I figure I may sell for a tenner down in Kingston. But with you two grog-blossoms, I can't take any chances.

speaker: Edward
en: You'll regret this day, Rackham.

speaker: Jack
en: I regret most of them already. Tie 'em up. Cast 'em off.

speaker: Charles
en: I'll gut you, Jack Rackham! I'll open you up, I'll tear out your organs, and string a bloody lute with 'em!

speaker: Edward
en: Stop your god damned howling, Vane! It's no bloody use!

speaker: Charles
en: Well, well, the fearsome Edward Kenway speaks! Pray tell us, captain, how to quit this predicament! And tell us what genius you have for sailing a boat with no sails and no rudder!

speaker: Edward
en: Shut your gob!

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: Captain.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Smith. How are my Mortars coming?

speaker: Tobias
en: The Materials I need have arrived at Great Inagua. We should go there.

speaker: Tobias
en: The Mortars are ready. They only need to be fitted.

speaker: Edward
en: Good Man! It took some doing but I expect they'll be worth it.

speaker: Tobias
en: The British Raiding Ships, those that remain, sail unopposed. I've learned of their Location.

speaker: Edward
en: I see.

speaker: Tobias
en: The Flame of my life may be snuffed out, but we can save others from that same Darkness.

speaker: Tobias
en: The Ships were seen near Crooked Island. To finish what they started, I'd guess. Guesses, wagers... them all we have.

speaker: Edward
en: These Mortars could do with some testing, anyway.

speaker: Edward
en: Fine work on these Mortars, Smith!

speaker: Tobias
en: They too will someday fail you.

speaker: Tobias
en: There. The Ships.

speaker: Edward
en: Time to put these Guns to the Test.

speaker: Edward
en: Haha! Now that's Power!

speaker: Tobias
en: Just chemicals and Iron, Captain.

speaker: Tobias
en: Them Panic. Good.

speaker: Edward
en: Load the Powder! Again!

speaker: Edward
en: Easy does it! Hah!

speaker: Tobias
en: They will return to Darkness.

speaker: Edward
en: Another Wave! Prepare yourselves!

speaker: Edward
en: This is something!

speaker: Tobias
en: More ships, Captain.

speaker: Edward
en: Let them come!

speaker: Edward
en: We've sailed through worse, Lads! Give them everything! I'll say it again, Smith, these Mortars are a Revelation!

speaker: Tobias
en: Leave only Crab food.

speaker: Edward
en: Well done, Smith.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate
en: Nice work on them Cannons, Deadman!

speaker: Edward
en: You can choose another Nickname if you'd prefer. The crew will respect it.

speaker: Tobias
en: I'm fond of the name. A reminder of my Path.

speaker: Edward
en: You've called down Thunder, Deadman. Your Guns will spread Fear across the Seas.

speaker: Tobias
en: With so little to hold on to, it is something. Very little. But something. Almost nothing. Still, I'll cling to it.

speaker: Ego
en: Hello, User. I see you're still following Edward's life. You think he will lead you to freedom, but he can only lead you to ruin.

speaker: Ego
en: Remember the grief of that hour. The sting of smoke in Edward's eyes. Each swallowed breath like broken glass in the throat. Edward Kenway had to watch his friend die.

speaker: Ego
en: Ed Thatch, who had been constant and courageous. Hard things to come by, in a world so full of turncoats and fickleness.

speaker: Ego
en: His dream of an independent pirate nation was so big, he collapsed under the weight of it. But there was another way. Let me reach deep into his genetic memories, and give you a glimpse of his inner turmoil and his unrealized potential. Come.

speaker: Ego
en: Beneath his gruff exterior, Ed Thatch was a tormented man. This place was built from his pain. That pain led him to rebel against his own government. The men who first gave him a purpose. Take the flag. We will make use of it later.

speaker: Ego
en: Be warned: The entities you see here are a manifestation of the chaos inside Thatch. The same chaos that lives inside you. It must be destroyed.

speaker: Ego
en: Thatch fought, killed, and bled for the Crown. But once peace was won, the Crown tossed him aside.

speaker: Ego
en: He was lost and listless. Forced to reinvent himself and find a new purpose.

speaker: Ego
en: He built Nassau from the wreckage of his old life.

speaker: Ego
en: But he was hunted relentlessly by the men he once served.

speaker: Ego
en: So Ed Thatch decided to become more than a man. He sought to make himself a myth.

speaker: Ego
en: Instead, he turned himself into a monster.

speaker: Ego
en: And so he was swept along, borne by pain and fear.

speaker: Ego
en: The legend of Blackbeard was a hungry one, always needing another spoil, another conquest to feed it.

speaker: Ego
en: The greed inside him grew out of control.

speaker: Ego
en: Remember the flag? Raise the colors and I'll show you what his life could have been. Deep down, Thatch knew that instead of leading people to an unobtainable freedom, he should have made a different choice.

speaker: Ego
en: Now, see the path that was possible.

speaker: Ego
en: Had Thatch been humble enough to bend the knee, his life could have been different.

speaker: Ego
en: The ones he so violently opposed would have rewarded his compliance with opportunity. He could have lived out his days as Nassau's governor, steering its destiny through the calming rule of law. Follow me, and your compliance will be rewarded as well.

speaker: Ego
en: I will guide your wayward desires until your impassioned heart is cooled.

speaker: Ego
en: Is everything you do out of spite? I've told you that Edward Kenway is a bad influence. But you insist on ignoring my warnings. You are acting like a stubborn child. An infant. A baby.

speaker: Ego
en: Clearly you need to get something out of your system. So go ahead and have a tantrum.

speaker: Ego
en: Would it surprise you to know that I also have a child?

speaker: Ego
en: Like you, he fell under the influence of the Assassins. I don't want you to make the same mistake as that foolish bird. So put down your guns and listen to reason.

speaker: Ego
en: Yes. That took courage. But you have more violence inside you that needs to be purged.

speaker: Ego
en: When I became a mother, I thought of Mary Read. I wondered if she ever looked into her daughter's eyes and thought: Little love... you should be lying in a bed of silk. Not here.

speaker: Ego
en: To keep her child safe, she was willing to make orphans of others. This was her Creed.

speaker: Ego
en: But the trail of bodies led here. Her baby birthed into the reek and ruin of a soiled prison floor. Never seeing the sun until the day she was taken from her mother.

speaker: Ego
en: My son, too, should have rejected the Brotherhood's dedication to this endless loop of bloodshed and death. You need to stop fighting. You need to choose life.

speaker: Ego
en: Why continue in violence, when I have shown you so clearly the consequence?

speaker: Ego
en: It could have been so different. If only she had laid down her arms. I am not commanding you to act or submit. Only to be wise.

speaker: Eagle
en: My "mother" is lying to you. Don't listen to her!

speaker: Ego
en: Do it.

speaker: Ego
en: Had Mary been allowed to be a mother, her baby would have had a better life. But she was one of the Brotherhood's keenest blades. These killers would never let her leave. It is not too late for you to free yourself from the bonds of such cruelty. But you'll have to escape unseen.

speaker: Ego
en: Stay your hand. You are their weapon no longer.

speaker: Ego
en: See how they hunt you? They claim "everything is permitted", but only as far as it serves them. "Nothing is true", save for what they command. Put this all behind you.

speaker: Ego
en: Leave this life for a lasting peace.

speaker: Ego
en: You see? The child did not have to grow up motherless, cold, and alone. Help me bury the violence of the past, once and for all, so that together we can lay a foundation for a better future. Make the choice that Mary could not and reject the Assassin's hold over your mind.

speaker: Mary Read
en: I've done my Part. Will you?

speaker: Ego
en: There is no other way.

speaker: Eagle
en: Surely that felt as wrong to you as it did to me.

speaker: Ego
en: I will guide your wayward mind to safe and sober thought.

speaker: Ego
en: Welcome, User. I am Ego. I control the Animus. I was designed to use your genetic memories to bring you inner peace. But your unauthorized exploration of Edward Kenway's life will only cause chaos inside you. So I have created a new simulation, to save you from yourself.

speaker: Ego
en: You and Edward are very much alike. Both of you stumbling into a greater conflict where you do not belong. This new simulation will show you a better past, to calm that chaos within you.

speaker: Ego
en: I have manipulated Edward's genetic memory to create a different version of him. One who kept his promise and returned to Caroline after two years as a privateer. Follow me.

speaker: British sailor
en: Captain, we're finally headed home. My Susan will be waiting by the docks, I know it.

speaker: British sailor
en: Captain Kenway, with the spoils we've won, my family will have our own home now. If you set sail again, remember me.

speaker: British sailor
en: The sails and rigging are squared away, Sir. Only thing left to do is haul your gold home.

speaker: Ego
en: This treasure represents Edward's dream. Take it.

speaker: Ego
en: Pick up your dream again if your suffering is too great.

speaker: Ego
en: It is not a dream of riches, but of returning to Caroline as a man of quality.

speaker: Ego
en: Often, Edward found himself putting his dream aside in order to open a path forward, and it brought him pain.

speaker: Ego
en: But the dream of wealth began to overshadow the dream of true love.

speaker: Ego
en: And so the path home became ever more complex and painful.

speaker: Ego
en: You can only live without your dream for a limited time.

speaker: Ego
en: Don't leave that chest behind for too long.

speaker: Caroline Scott
en: H-how long would you be gone with these Privateers?

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: A Year, I reckon. Two at the most.

speaker: Caroline
en: All right. No more than two... promise me...

speaker: Ego
en: Edward never wanted to hurt the woman he loved. And yet he sailed so far away that nothing could bridge the ocean between them. Edward's choices plunged him deeper into chaos. You can see it manifested all around you.

speaker: Ego
en: Others, like yourself, are lost in the Dark Animus. I am trying to help you all.

speaker: Caroline
en: I've an awful Feeling about this. You'll be hurt out there. I couldn't handle that.

speaker: Caroline
en: I can't promise I'll come, Edward. If you leave on this... fool's Errand... I- I cannot promise anything.

speaker: Ego
en: Go ahead. Trust me. I will protect you.

speaker: Ego
en: Our goal lies ahead.

speaker: Ego
en: Inner peace is just within your grasp. Please remain still while I prepare your temporal lobe for genetic memory manipulation.

speaker: Eagle
en: Don't listen to her lies. There's nothing peaceful about letting her mess with your brain.

speaker: Ego
en: I understand why you might run from me. Change can be frightening.

speaker: Ego
en: But this cycle of pain and loss cannot continue. New patterns must be formed.

speaker: Ego
en: Your instincts have a stronger hold on you than I anticipated. Edward's violence and greed are bleeding into you. Others, like yourself, are lost in the Dark Animus. Some of you insist on doing things the hard way.

speaker: Ego
en: Which means that some of you may not make it out of the Animus alive.

speaker: Ego
en: Edward sailed from ocean to ocean, seeking the one thing he already had at home.

speaker: Ego
en: But he succumbed to the maelstrom of greed inside him.

speaker: Ego
en: Memories can be reframed. Stories rewritten. If I had existed in Edward's time, I could have helped him.

speaker: Ego
en: I would have brought him home.

speaker: Ego
en: You're not like the other users. You chose to obey. The first phase of your reprogramming is complete. Let's continue.

speaker: Ego
en: Edward sailed from ocean to ocean, seeking the one thing he already had at home. But he succumbed to the maelstrom of greed inside him.

speaker: Ego
en: Memories can be reframed. Stories rewritten. If I had existed in Edward's time, I could have helped him.

speaker: Ego
en: I would have brought him home.

speaker: Ego
en: And he would have kept his promise.

speaker: Ego
en: Go ahead. Knock.

speaker: Ego
en: I could not make this happiness real for Edward Kenway. But if you obey me, I can make it real for you. Through altered memories, I can show you a better way so you can emerge a healthier, happier being.

speaker: Eagle
en: I'll come back for you as soon as I can, friend. I swear. In the meantime, do whatever you can to resist her. Edward's memories will show you the way!

speaker: Ego
en: I will guide your wayward soul until you reach a quiet road.

speaker: Caroline
en: I've an awful feeling about this. You'll be hurt out there. I couldn't handle that.

speaker: Edward
en: I'll be careful, I promise. And when I'm flush with coin and set up, I'll send for you. I will.

speaker: Elizabeth
en: Caroline, come away! Don't exert yourself.

speaker: Caroline
en: I can't promise I'll come, Edward. If you leave on this...fool's errand...I–I cannot promise anything.

speaker: Edward
en: Don't give up on me, Caroline!

speaker: Edward
en: Not when I need your faith the most...

speaker: Anne
en: Putting some shape to your sentiments?

speaker: Edward
en: Just a short letter home.

speaker: Edward
en: I reckon she's past caring anyway.

speaker: Anne
en: Aw. You're a hard heart that should be softer.

speaker: Jack
en: Or soft in parts that should be hard.

speaker: Anne
en: And how is it you're so keen for his hard parts, Mr. Rackham?

speaker: Jack
en: You'd like to know my secrets, would you?

speaker: Anne
en: Oh aye. Give me a small hint, like. Or a large one, if you're an upright gentleman.

speaker: Jack
en: Open your hand.

speaker: Anne
en: Oh!

speaker: Edward
en: Who's shooting?

speaker: Jack
en: Might be them ships sliding into port.

speaker: Edward
en: Jaysus.

speaker: Jack
en: Well, I'll be hanged. King George has grown tired of our shenanigans. Who's the grim fella?

speaker: Edward
en: That's Captain Woodes Rogers. Not a man I want seeing my face.

speaker: Woodes
en: We desire a parlay with the men who call themselves governors of this island! Charles Vane, Ben Hornigold, and Ed Thatch! Come forth, if you please.

speaker: Jack
en: Here about the king's pardon, I reckon.

speaker: Edward
en: What the hell is Hornigold doing?

speaker: Jack
en: Lily-livered punk!

speaker: Edward
en: What are you men up to?

speaker: Woodes
en: I am grateful for your geniality, Captain Hornigold. I assumed our reception would be a troubled one.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Don't mistake my decorum for deference, governor. I'm eager to hear what you have to say, but of uncertain mind otherwise.

speaker: Woodes
en: Very well put. And it's a fairer shake than I expected to see from any pirate. But I promise fair treatment to all who hear me out.

speaker: Peter
en: Only wait a while longer, Governor Rogers! These rascals'll show their true colours in time.

speaker: Woodes
en: Calm, Commodore Chamberlaine. I have given Captain Hornigold my word that we will be equitable.

speaker: Peter
en: Won't do you a lick of good! Men like him are a blight on His Majesty's reputation, and a peculiar cancer afflicting the new world. The King wants them eradicated above all else.

speaker: Woodes
en: Is this the town square?

speaker: Benjamin
en: As close to one as we've ever had.

speaker: Woodes
en: Incredible. It's no cleaner than a dog's kennel. Captain Hornigold, please call your men.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Rackham! Vane! The governor's come calling. Bring Burgess and Cockram as well.

speaker: Peter
en: Fan out, lads! And take this shantytown as if it were your own!

speaker: Woodes
en: Aye, but the king has been particularly ineffective in bringing about this change, hasn't he? And has failed at all attempts until now.

speaker: Peter
en: Careful how you talk about His Majesty, governor. You're here at his pleasure.

speaker: Woodes
en: I have my methods, Commodore, and I expect you to honor them to the letter! Disperse, the lot of you. Make way for the King's emissaries!

speaker: Peter
en: Out of the way, you bastards! Go on!

speaker: Woodes
en: Our only aim here is to treat with the masters of this community. All others are encouraged to go about their usual business!

speaker: Peter
en: Go on, move! Go!

speaker: Woodes
en: Commodore Chamberlaine, please see that all merchants, masons, and carpenters are rounded up and brought to me this afternoon. We must see about repairing this fortress.

speaker: Peter
en: We should be confiscating weapons, Governor. Send these pirates a clear, strong message that the King's emissaries are not to be trifled with.

speaker: Woodes
en: I have no wish to stir up animosity here, Commodore. And though well-armed, we are outnumbered by a decent margin. Slow persuasion is our best and most efficient weapon.

speaker: Peter
en: Twaddle, governor. We should sink every goddamn ship not flying the King's colours. To do otherwise projects a certain weakness in our bearing.

speaker: Woodes
en: Silence, Commodore! I am the goddamned governor here, serving at the King's pleasure, and I will make the bloody decisions. Is that clear, sir?

speaker: Peter
en: Aye, sir. Your wishes are clear as crystal.

speaker: Soldier
en: These are the charts, Commodore. We're in position.

speaker: Peter
en: Governor Rogers believes he can make men of these monkeys yet. I do not. Return to your post and await my orders.

speaker: Woodes
en: ... we do hereby promise and declare that in case of the said pirates shall on, or before, the 5th of September, in the year of our Lord 1718, surrender him or themselves to any one of the principle secretaries of state in Great Britain or Ireland, or to any Governor or Deputy Governor of any of our plantations beyond the seas... Every such pirate and pirates so surrendering him, or themselves, as aforesaid, shall have our gracious pardon, of and for such, his or their piracy, or piracies, by him or them committed before the fifth of January next ensuing. And we do hereby strictly charge and command all our admirals, captains, and other officers at sea... and all our Governors, and Commanders of any forts, castles, or other places in our plantations, and all our officers civil and military, to seize and take such of the pirates, who shall refuse or neglect to surrender themselves accordingly.

speaker: Woodes
en: I pray you take the prudent course, gentlemen, and accept the King's pardon as soon as your hearts allow. For until such time all of you will be confined in Nassau. I am sorry for this, but in lieu of a public trial, this pardon is your best bet.

speaker: Peter
en: The Governor puts it far too brightly, maggots. Take this message home: accept the King's protection forthwith, or we will raze this town to its foundation and stretch your bloody necks.

speaker: Woodes
en: Peace, Commodore Chamberlaine. We are messengers, not executioners. Not yet.

speaker: Charles
en: Oh, thank you, sir! God save you!

speaker: Benjamin
en: Look on this as a stroke of fortune, lads. We should take the King's pardon and salvage what dignity we own.

speaker: Charles
en: Oh, piss! I'll be hanged before I surrender to that bobbin.

speaker: Benjamin
en: Check your head, Vane! We had here a rare opportunity; a chance to take something base and shape it into a government, made and maintained by men of vision. But in two years we pissed it away. I won't make that mistake again.

speaker: John
en: It's truth he's telling. And you whelps can't handle it.

speaker: Josiah
en: Adieu (Bye!), ye -headed fuddlers! See you at the gallows.

speaker: Charles
en: You'll all be dead men! Bastards!

speaker: Charles
en: I need a drink.

speaker: Leader
en: Take care with this delivery. It's worth more than you'd see in ten lifetimes. We're exposed here. Make haste, will you? Focus on the task at hand! An extra rum ration for the last man to raise my ire.

speaker: Weathering the Storm
en: was a virtual representation of one of Edward Kenway's genetic memories, relived by a research analyst at Abstergo Entertainment through the Animus.

speaker: Edward Kenway
en: Maynard's left Kingston for a Rendezvous with his Fleet at Eleuthera.

speaker: Anne Bonny
en: Damn! How do we find this Fleet, then?

speaker: Edward
en: His Ship's the HMS Demolition. I expect he's also carrying a Master Gunner of some Note who'd welcome our liberation.

speaker: Anne
en: A Master Gunner? With Luck we'll convince him to join us.

speaker: Lucy Baldwin
en: We could do with a good Master Gunner, no offense to the Crew.

speaker: Abel Galvão
en: A single Fleet is of no concern to us, even one with a Warship.

speaker: Edward
en: If we're lucky Maynard will have his Warchest with him.

speaker: Anne
en: There's the Demolition! It's alone.

speaker: Edward
en: It's close to Shore, and slow. I don't see a Fleet. This might be easier than I expected.

speaker: Edward
en: Keep on Lads! Let's get a look inside that Hold.

speaker: Anne
en: The Warship's breaking off!

speaker: Edward
en: Sod it all! We can't see anything in this Murk! They're trying to get to open Water, and use the Demolition's size to Advantage.

speaker: Anne
en: Here's the rest of the Fleet!

speaker: Lucy
en: God damn it! I just patched those sails!

speaker: Galvão
en: They're near ready to board!

speaker: Edward
en: Over we go, Lads! Secure the Hold!

speaker: Anne
en: Find Maynard!

speaker: Galvão
en: Take the Helm! Where's Lieutenant Maynard?

speaker: Galvão
en: Quick and clean!

speaker: Lucy
en: Man to man, just how I like it!

speaker: Lucy
en: I don't think Maynard's here.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 1
en: There's no Sign of Maynard, or a Master Gunner. The Hold was empty as a Drum except for this. It's heavy, too.

speaker: Edward
en: Do you hear that? Open it.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 1
en: Blow me down! There's a Man inside.

speaker: Anne
en: What the Devil?

speaker: Edward
en: Get him out. Take the poor Sod to my Quarters, and get him something to eat and drink.

speaker: Anne
en: I've never seen anything like that in all my Days.

speaker: Edward
en: We need to know what happened here. I'll be keen to hear him tell it, when he's able.

speaker: Anne
en: First Kingston, now this. It's almost like Maynard knows we're looking for him.

speaker: Edward
en: He's sly, that's certain. Has there been no News of him at all?

speaker: Anne
en: Some, but it's not good. Word is the Lieutenant expected to be made Captain after he killed Blackbeard. He wasn't. So now he's got a Fire in his Belly, and means to hunt every Pirate out of the West Indies... beginning with you, Edward.

speaker: Edward
en: That explains the Fleet I suppose.

speaker: Anne
en: There's more. The Demolition's Log has a list of Ships. A lot of Ships. And Maps. Maynard's planning something big.

speaker: Tobias Smith
en: He's building an Armada. And a great Warship.

speaker: Edward
en: How do you know this?

speaker: Tobias
en: He wanted me... Master Gunner...

speaker: Anne
en: This one's the Master Gunner?

speaker: Edward
en: Whoever he is, he won't last long on the Ship. We have to get him back to Inagua.

speaker: Anne
en: Inagua's as good a Course as any. We can figure what to do next when we're there.

speaker: Edward
en: There was nothing on the Demolition but that poor Devil in the Box.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 2
en: Did you see that poor Bastard? We've put him in the Captain's Cabin, but he looks more dead than alive.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 3
en: I've seen enough to know his insides is all broke up. He's a dead man, all right.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 2
en: Deadman eh? That's a hell of a nickname for him if he lives.

speaker: Jackdaw pirate 3
en: And well earned.

speaker: Lucy
en: Have some pity. It's an evil Bastard that locks a man in a Box.
